playbook_relevance: Journal-authoritative state with repairable JSON projection
Intent/artifact/receipt transaction for crash-safe user decisions
Content-addressed immutable input freeze and verification
Exact declared-vs-observed model output file reconciliation
Atomic file copy with fsync and conflict-by-digest semantics
Deterministic plan budget/capability policy after model generation
Model output parse/repair retry with retained attempts
Two-phase global knowledge publication with a project lock
Typed state-machine extraction and idempotent step receipts
files.purpose: Primary v1 pre/post-campaign controller: creates a retained run, snapshots problem/references/knowledge/project inputs, invokes model roles for research gating/research/planning/assessment/replanning, freezes and renders an executable campaign DAG, drives CampaignBuilder with bounded campaign restarts, validates outcome evidence, publishes knowledge/research state, and commits an explicit successor-strategy choice.
tests_or_consumers: Visible consumers: autonomy.py constructs/runs/resumes RegimeRunner and invokes choose_strategy; benchmark.py runs RegimeRunner; cli.py exposes regime-run, regime-resume, choose-strategy and interactive strategy choice; package __init__.py re-exports RegimeError/Options/Runner/choose_strategy.
Generated campaign is consumed by CampaignSpec.load and CampaignBuilder; frozen resolved campaign is consumed on resume.
Research/planner/final reporter/failure replanner prompt templates and model parsers are implicit contract consumers.
No test files or explicit assertions of end-to-end crash recovery, concurrency, symlink containment, schema migration, or mathematical soundness were supplied.
files.v2_disposition: REWRITE/SPLIT. Preserve the high-level gate->research->plan->freeze->execute->assess protocol, journal-first authoritative state, content-addressed immutable inputs, exact research source accounting, deterministic policy validation, and intent/receipt strategy transaction. Replace the monolith with typed state-transition reducers plus separate snapshot, model-role, campaign-render, publication, assessment, and strategy-transaction services. Add a project-wide repository lock/transaction, immediate source-tree containment validation, versioned migrations, bounded lock waits, idempotent step receipts, and deterministic validation before model repair. Do not retain hand-coded cross-artifact finalization as one method.

failure_modes: Resume mutates checkpoint state and saves it before acquiring the controller lock in _drive. Two concurrent resumes can both alter a checkpoint; the loser only fails later acquiring controller, so single-driver serialization does not cover the resume transition.

Controller and state use different lock directories. This enables decisions while the driver waits, but requires careful ordering; v1 has no transaction joining deadline fallback and operator submission.

AFK timeout race: _await_decision can return the recommended fallback at the deadline; an operator can then durably submit a different decision before _apply_decision. _apply_decision reloads state but ignores pending_operator_decision and can overwrite/clear the later operator choice.

Runtime options on resume can change profile, max_campaigns, approval timeout, AFK behavior, executable names, waiver, and focus. The retained settings are not consistently authoritative: campaign limit uses self.max_campaigns, decision timing uses self.afk_autonomy/self.approval_timeout_minutes, while elapsed/failure limits use state settings.

The immutable contract covers only problem bytes and success dataclass. Allowed tools, sandbox policy, compute profile, autonomy bounds, references, inputs, Lean/toolchain versions, project manifest bytes, and model settings can change during a session without _verify_contract rejecting them.
Maximum elapsed time is checked only before creating a round. A campaign, optimizer, approval wait, or success-validation command can run beyond the configured wall-time.
Each success command receives analysis_agent_seconds independently; total deterministic validation cost is (build + axioms + all verification commands) times that timeout, not one bounded budget.
Optimizer gets two attempts per _prepare_analysis call; every resumed optimizer checkpoint can add two more. There is no retained total optimizer-attempt/agent-second cap.
_regime_run_resumable trusts pre-campaign/state.json projection rather than the authoritative journal. A stale/corrupt projection can cause a new campaign to start and abandon a resumable run.
Campaign failure catching omits some plausible typed failures such as ConfigurationError from generated campaign loading; uncaught errors can leave session campaign_running.
Round shape validation is partial; rounds[-1].get is called before confirming the last entry is a dict, and many nested settings/round fields are cast/indexed directly.

Input lineage records mutable workspace paths without content digests and checks only top-level exists/non-symlink. Nested symlinks or later workspace mutation can alter the next campaign's copied input; regime's delayed nested-symlink rejection compounds this.
Success workspace/artifact relative-path containment depends on ProjectSpec validation not shown here; this file itself does not reject absolute or .. paths in success.workspace/required_artifacts.
Success command environment starts from os.environ.copy(); whether execution policy strips undeclared secrets is delegated to run_captured_command and is unknown from this corpus.

Axiom parsing is format-dependent: it counts lines containing one exact no-axiom phrase or a single-line bracket regex and comma-splits names. Lean version/output formatting changes or multiline reports can yield false failure or incomplete observation.
Evidence verification failure does not stop commands; all costly checks still execute and aggregate failures.

Success-validation receipts/logs are not journaled or evidence-indexed by the autonomy session, and retry reconstruction trusts the receipt's passed/failures fields without rerunning evidence verification or checking receipt integrity.

Optimizer contract_preserved is a model-supplied boolean, not proof that campaign_directive preserves semantics. Final deterministic success checks limit false success, but intermediate campaigns can still waste compute on weakened/misdirected directives.
The optimizer has read access to the whole autonomy session, current campaign, and knowledge tree; retained prompts/decisions may contain sensitive model output. No redaction policy is visible.
If outcome has no offered strategies and no synthetic recovery strategy, any continue action must fail availability validation; checkpoint is the only valid optimizer action.
_await_decision with AFK disabled sleeps forever while holding the controller lock, requiring a separate process to submit a decision and preventing a replacement driver.
Status says checkpoint for sources based solely on absence of campaign root state.json; other early initialization failures can be misclassified as critical-source input.
A root campaign state without outcome is only recognized as campaign_gate for awaiting_approval/awaiting_sources; other legitimate resumable statuses cause an AutonomyError.
Shared project references/knowledge and regime campaign runs retain the concurrency risks from regime.py across autonomous sessions.
autonomy_status docstring calls state verified, but it only loads the journal snapshot; it does not verify the project contract, decision request, success receipt, or session evidence.
No autonomous-session evidence index protects request, optimizer output, directive, decision, receipts, and state as one tamper-evident bundle.
interfaces: Public Python: AutonomyError, AutonomyRuntimeOptions, InterCampaignAnalysis.parse(), SuccessValidation, AutonomyRunner.run()/resume(), record_autonomy_decision(), autonomy_status().

Consumes ProjectSpec autonomy settings and compute profiles, RegimeRunner/RegimeOptions/choose_strategy, CampaignOutcome, journal/locks, agent_runner optimizer requests, run_captured_command, artifact evidence verification.

Filesystem protocol: <project>/autonomy-runs/<session> journal/state; controller lock directory; rounds/round-NNN/{analysis attempts,decision request/operator decision,next-campaign.md,success-validation receipts/logs}; referenced regime campaign runs.
Success contract executes build, generated Lean #check/example/#print axioms audit, and configured verification commands in the campaign workspace.

Session statuses: ready, campaign_running, analysis_retry, awaiting_approval, checkpoint, solved, stopped, budget_exhausted. Round statuses additionally include running, assessed-by-fields, awaiting_approval, checkpoint, failed, solved, stopped, complete.
invariants: Autonomy must be enabled and have a success contract; approval timeout is 0..1440 minutes, max campaigns 1..1000, and decision poll interval positive.
A session snapshots SHA-256 of problem bytes and canonicalized success dataclass JSON; _verify_contract reloads the project and requires those two hashes to remain equal.
Session state is journal-backed schema v1; saves append a snapshot before updating state.json.
Only one driver holds the controller-directory campaign lock; state writes and operator decision submission use the session-directory campaign lock.
A new round is created only after wall-time and campaign-count checks; retained running rounds are resumed when recognized as resumable.

Campaign outcome solved is insufficient: success requires evidence-index verification, required artifacts, build command, generated theorem type checks, axiom output policy, and every configured verification command.
InterCampaignAnalysis has an exact schema-v1 key set, nonempty required text, text arrays, action in {continue,checkpoint}, and contract_preserved must literally be true.
Optimizer continuation strategy must be in the offered strategy set; decision requests allow offered strategies plus stop.
Operator decisions are retained durably and are idempotent only for the same already-pending strategy.
A next campaign directive repeats the immutable problem hash and includes selected campaign strategy context plus optimizer rationale/directive.
Input lineage maps declared project targets to prior campaign workspace paths for override copying in the next regime run.
line_findings: AutonomyRuntimeOptions is runtime-only by claim, yet several values materially alter resumed-session behavior and boundedness.
InterCampaignAnalysis permits empty arrays for progress/failures/obligations/gaps/compute assessment; only their elements, if present, must be nonempty.
recommended_strategy and campaign_directive must be nonempty even when action=checkpoint.
Session IDs use UTC-second timestamp plus 24 random bits, paralleling but not sharing regime run-ID logic.
State stores max_campaigns in settings, but _execute_or_resume_round compares len(rounds) to self.max_campaigns instead of the retained value.
resume maps sources/campaign_gate/failure_limit checkpoints back to running, while optimizer checkpoints become analysis_retry; it clears completed_at and error.
_drive holds the controller lock across the entire session drive, including potentially indefinite approval waiting and all campaigns.
Campaign errors increment consecutive_failures, but then normally run the optimizer and request a new strategy; successful outcome parsing resets the count to zero.
After catching a campaign error, runner.run_dir is retained when available, enabling recovery analysis over partial output.
If no root campaign state exists, autonomy calls it a sources checkpoint without reading pre-campaign status to confirm awaiting_sources.
A solved CampaignOutcome that fails deterministic validation is converted to synthetic strategy repair-success-validation rather than accepted.
_retry_analysis reconstructs SuccessValidation summary from receipt failures but does not validate contract_sha256, campaign_run, command logs, or completed_at.
Regime options always force missing_source_policy='checkpoint'; waive_missing_sources can bypass the checkpoint globally for that runner.
_capture_lineage takes outputs from campaign_run/workspace, not the immutable input snapshot, deliberately carrying forward mutable products.
Generated theorem contract both #checks declarations and constructs an example of exact configured theorem_type, then prints axioms.
Configured build command's first token is replaced only when exactly 'lake'; verification commands get the same replacement behavior.
Command timeout uses autonomy.analysis_agent_seconds even though these are deterministic success commands, showing a naming/budget-domain mismatch.
Axiom allowed-set checking rejects observed unknown axioms but does not require any particular allowed axiom to appear.
Optimizer analysis writes both output.json from the runner and an identical analysis.json controller copy.
Analysis attempt numbers are derived from existing numeric attempt directories and continue monotonically after checkpoints.
Decision deadline is only written when AFK is enabled; a zero-minute timeout produces an immediate fallback.
_await_decision reloads authoritative journal state each poll but reads request once, so later request-file changes are ignored while self runtime settings still govern timing.
_apply_decision calls choose_strategy only when the selected ID is found in campaign outcome strategies; synthetic strategies skip campaign strategy finalization.

The next directive includes analysis.campaign_directive regardless of which allowed non-stop strategy the operator chooses; only selected_context changes. Thus choosing a non-recommended strategy does not force optimizer directive recomputation and can produce a mismatch.
contract_hash embedded in the directive is problem_sha256 only, while success_sha256 is omitted from the human-readable directive.
_verify_contract reloads current ProjectSpec but compares only the two hashes produced by _contract_snapshot.
_round_dir creates directories even during reads/status transitions, so observing malformed state can mutate the filesystem.
_state validates only schema_version, not object type before .get; a non-dict JSON state would raise AttributeError.
_save_state takes the session lock on every write while the driver holds the different controller lock.
record_autonomy_decision writes operator-decision.json before journaling pending state; a crash leaves an orphan decision file that the controller never consults.
Repeated identical pending decisions return without checking operator-decision.json integrity.
autonomy_status does not resolve or repair state.json projection and returns the journal state directly.

files.purpose: Retained outer-loop controller that repeatedly runs regime campaigns, validates claimed Lean success against an immutable problem/success contract, invokes a read-only model optimizer between campaigns, obtains operator or timed AFK strategy approval, carries forward workspace inputs/directives, and stops on proof, operator stop, checkpoints, failure limit, wall-time check, or campaign-count limit.
tests_or_consumers: Visible consumers: cli.py exposes autonomy-run/resume/decide/status and maps statuses to exit codes; package __init__.py re-exports the public autonomy API.
Consumes regime.py directly for every round and strategy choice; generated next directives are consumed by the next RegimeRunner.
Lean, lake, configured verification executables, agent_runner, and run_captured_command are external runtime consumers/producers.
No tests are supplied for concurrent resume, operator-vs-timeout races, retained-setting enforcement, elapsed-budget overrun, axiom parser variants, tamper detection, or multi-round crash recovery.
files.v2_disposition: REWRITE core controller. Keep the outer-loop concept, strict post-solve deterministic validation, immutable success contract hash, retained optimizer attempts, explicit approval, and journal-first state. Replace ad hoc mutable dictionaries with a versioned typed event/reducer model; use one session lock/lease and atomic decision arbitration; freeze all safety/compute/toolchain/runtime settings; enforce total wall/agent/command budgets continuously; content-address lineage; make checkpoint resume a locked transition; and add an autonomy evidence manifest. Separate deterministic validation from model optimization so failed evidence checks can short-circuit expensive commands where policy permits.

failure_modes: No benchmark-run lock exists. Concurrent resume processes can execute the same suffix, create duplicate expensive campaign runs, and race overwriting benchmark-report.json with lost or inconsistent progress.

Only the suite TOML and each completed case's project manifest are hashed. Problem files, references, knowledge, declared project inputs, prompt templates, toolchain, model configuration dependencies, and future/unexecuted case manifests are not frozen; benchmark reproducibility and resume identity are incomplete.
Resume requires the original live suite manifest to remain present and unchanged even though suite.toml is retained; the snapshot is not sufficient to reconstruct the suite.

The 'blind' property is structural, not enforced as an information-flow proof. Expected labels are absent from runner arguments, but whether agents can read the suite file through configured inputs/sandbox paths is not checked here.

False closure is defined only as outcome.status=='solved' against a non-solved expectation. The benchmark does not verify the campaign evidence bundle or run AutonomyRunner's kernel success contract, so it can count a model-assessed regime outcome as a solved benchmark result.
The CLI describes an autonomous-outcome benchmark, but implementation runs one RegimeRunner per case, not AutonomyRunner.

Missing outcome is observed as 'checkpoint', while ExpectedOutcome admits 'blocked' but not 'checkpoint'. Unless a retained outcome explicitly has status blocked, source checkpoints cannot match a blocked expectation; the taxonomy is inconsistent.
Observed outcome accepts any string from outcome.json, including invalid labels, and marks it unmatched rather than treating it as schema failure. CampaignOutcome.parse is not used.
_new_run heuristically selects the lexicographically greatest newly appearing directory. Concurrent unrelated runs can be misattributed to a failed case.
Per-case catch-all captures programming bugs and integrity failures as benchmark data, which aids isolation but can conceal systemic invalidity unless error count is inspected.
Report is consistency-checked but not journaled, signed, or covered by an evidence index; a party able to edit report and related manifests can forge a self-consistent prefix.
Recorded run_dir and compute_ledger are only type-checked as optional nonempty strings on resume; paths, existence, containment, and digests are not verified.
Case project manifest hash can be null for any observed error, making early read failures indistinguishable from some manipulated/error states.
An interruption between campaign completion and report rewrite leaves a costly run unrecorded; resume reruns that case.
Initial benchmark directory and IDs use timestamp plus 24 random bits; collision fails rather than retries.
The benchmark executes cases serially with no suite-level compute/time cap and may pay the entire regime's multiple planner/gate/assessment retries for every case.
interfaces: Public Python: ExpectedOutcome, SourcePolicy, BenchmarkCase, BenchmarkSuite.load(), BenchmarkRuntime, run_benchmark_suite(), resume_benchmark_suite().
Manifest schema v1 requires exactly schema_version, suite{id,runs_dir}, and nonempty cases[{id,project,expected_outcome,missing_source_policy}].
Report schema v2 has exact top-level keys and exact case-result keys; report statuses are running/complete.
Consumes ProjectSpec and RegimeRunner; propagates RunnerInterrupted but isolates all other per-case exceptions.
Visible filesystem outputs: benchmark run directory, suite.toml snapshot, benchmark-report.json, and referenced campaign run/compute ledger paths.
invariants: Manifest and case keys are exact; suite/case IDs are nonempty and case IDs unique; expected outcome and source policy are enumerated.
Manifest-relative project and runs paths are resolved and must remain under the benchmark manifest directory; project manifests must exist.
New run snapshots suite TOML and hashes the snapshot before executing cases; report is atomically rewritten after every case.

Resume requires exact report schema v2, running status, null completed_at, directory name equal to run_id, current manifest and retained suite snapshot hashes equal to the recorded hash, suite ID equality, report parent under configured runs_dir, and a strict prefix of cases.
Completed prefix scoring is recomputed and must be internally consistent; each completed project manifest hash must still match its current file.
Summary accepted requires every case complete and matched, zero errors, and zero false closures.
Expected labels are not included in RegimeOptions or explicit campaign prompts by this module.
line_findings: _relative normalizes backslashes before resolution, then enforces containment under a resolved base.
runs_dir is constrained beneath the suite directory, which may be intentional but prevents external benchmark storage paths.
BenchmarkRuntime defaults focus=False, but cli.py overrides it with not headless, making CLI default behavior focused.
_summary uses identity checks item['matched'] is True and item['false_closure'] is True; own report generation stores actual booleans and resume validates them.
Running reports set completed_at=null and complete reports compute a fresh completion timestamp on rewrite.
_new_run ignores newly created files and chooses by directory name, not mtime or retained run ID.
Existing runs snapshot uses set(project_runs.iterdir()), containing both files and directories, while _new_run filters new candidates to directories.
Each case hashes only project.toml before ProjectSpec.load; no loaded ProjectSpec snapshot is retained in the report.
RunnerInterrupted is the sole exception rethrown; BaseException and ordinary Exception behavior differ deliberately.
If outcome.json is missing, observed='checkpoint' regardless of actual pre-campaign or campaign state.
If outcome JSON is malformed, the per-case broad exception changes observed to error; if JSON is a dict with unknown/missing status, observed becomes invalid.
Report is rewritten as running after the final case and immediately rewritten complete, causing one redundant full report write.
Resume refuses a report whose case count equals suite length even if status incorrectly remains running; there is no finalize-only recovery path.
Resume validates current hashes of completed project manifests but does not compare recorded run output/evidence or recompute observed outcomes.
suite_manifest in the report is an absolute live path; suite_manifest_snapshot is the relative literal suite.toml.

run_benchmark_suite snapshots text read from the original manifest, then hashes the snapshot; a concurrent edit between BenchmarkSuite.load and this read could snapshot a suite different from the already-loaded suite object.
The docstring 'without exposing expected outcomes to campaign agents' is not backed by an explicit deny-path or sandbox assertion.
files.model_tier: Terra
playbook_relevance: False-closure metrics backed by verification receipts
Per-case exception isolation with systemic-error channel
files.purpose: Loads strict TOML benchmark suites, runs regime campaigns without directly passing expected outcomes to agents, scores observed outcome against each expected label, records false closures/errors/compute-ledger paths in a schema-v2 JSON report, and resumes only an unrecorded case suffix after consistency checks.
tests_or_consumers: Visible consumers: cli.py benchmark command; package __init__.py re-exports BenchmarkRuntime/Suite and run/resume functions.
Consumes RegimeRunner and project manifests; external report readers consume summary/cases/accepted and compute-ledger paths.
RunnerInterrupted is an explicit interruption/resume consumer contract.
No benchmark fixtures/tests are supplied for blindness, blocked/checkpoint semantics, report tampering, concurrent resume, incomplete write recovery, or verified false-closure detection.
files.v2_disposition: REWRITE integrity layer while preserving strict manifest parsing, per-case isolation, atomic incremental reporting, and verified-prefix resume. Freeze/content-address every case input closure at suite start, lock the benchmark run, use a journaled case state machine with per-case idempotency keys, parse CampaignOutcome strictly, align blocked/checkpoint taxonomy, and define whether the benchmark targets RegimeRunner or AutonomyRunner. False-closure scoring must be tied to verified evidence/kernel contract appropriate to that declared target. Add report migration from schema v2 rather than silently changing it.

failure_modes: The command dispatcher is a very large conditional with heterogeneous parsing, validation, output, and exit semantics; adding commands risks branch/attribute mistakes and makes unit isolation difficult.

--visible is parsed but never read. Focus is always not args.headless, so default is focused and --visible is behaviorally redundant. For benchmark this also overrides BenchmarkRuntime's focus=False default.

regime-resume reads pre-campaign/state.json directly before RegimeRunner repairs it from the authoritative journal; stale/tampered projection can select policy incorrectly or fail despite a healthy journal.
dashboard and several status/display paths read state.json directly rather than the authoritative journal/verified APIs, conflicting with help text such as authoritative/verified status.
autonomy-status delegates to autonomy_status, whose implementation only loads journal state and does not verify the immutable contract despite the CLI wording.
audit always exits 0 even when assurance gaps remain; scripts cannot infer clean assurance from its exit code.

The status command conditionally shows claims only when configuration/features.json exists and summary.required is truthy; absence/malformed ancillary data can make status less informative than dashboard/claims.
Interactive strategy selection parses outcome JSON ad hoc rather than CampaignOutcome, chooses the first recommended item, and can fail if no recommended strategy exists.
Error handling does not include every imported subsystem-specific exception explicitly; broad OSError/ValueError helps, but RunnerInterrupted and unexpected programming errors escape by design.
Several JSON reads are unguarded locally and rely on the outer exception tuple; JSONDecodeError is a ValueError, but malformed shapes can produce KeyError/TypeError/AssertionError that escape.
Benchmark summary printing directly indexes report fields without schema parsing because it trusts the just-produced report.
Visibility/help wording still references Herdr panes/workspaces, creating CLI coupling to one runner implementation.
No structured machine-output mode is common across commands; many commands emit human text while some emit JSON, complicating stable automation.
No CLI schema/version command or deprecation mechanism is visible; renaming statuses/exit codes can silently break scripts.

failure_modes: PaneHeartbeat.start is not lifecycle-guarded: repeated calls can spawn multiple daemon threads sharing state; finish does not make restart well-defined because the stop Event remains set.
Its lock coordinates only one heartbeat instance. Multiple heartbeats or unrelated writers sharing a stream can interleave ANSI sequences/output.
ControllerDashboard has no lock and is not thread-safe.

Display width uses len(), not Unicode terminal cell width; wide/combining role IDs and spinner glyphs can overflow or truncate incorrectly. ANSI sequences are added after width calculation, which is fine for ANSI but not cell width.
role_ids passed to ControllerDashboard are never used for validation/order/completeness; render accepts any statuses.
Terminal wrap restoration is best effort. Process termination or stream exception between control writes can leave the terminal altered.
PaneHeartbeat.write takes both a destination and heartbeat stream; when they differ, it clears/re-renders one stream around output to another, which may be unnecessary or confusing.
finish maps every non-succeeded status to a red failure symbol, so cancelled/skipped/interrupted cannot be represented accurately.
I/O exceptions from write/flush/fileno are mostly not handled; only terminal-size lookup has fallback.
Thread join timeout equals one refresh interval; Event.wait should wake promptly, but no assertion ensures thread termination.

cross_cutting: runtime.py is both controller and persistence specification; features.py is both plugin registry and mathematical trust policy. Their coupling is through unversioned in-memory FeatureContext/FeatureResult plus heterogeneous retained artifact filenames, making independent evolution difficult.

Duplicated state machines: run statuses are enumerated in _validate_retained_state, _load_run, campaign_status, campaign_status_exit_code, and transition branches; stage reset/descendant closure is duplicated in _reset_stages and _route_retry; handoff invalidation and promotion cleanup are duplicated; Herdr truth is split across state, creation labels, process registry, and remote workspace listing.

Schema/version risk: state/evidence/config/input/promotion/agent mutation/source/continuation/semantic/claim artifacts mostly use schema v1, command/Lean/replay receipts use v2, review decisions have no version, and consumers often infer type from fields or basename. There is no central schema registry, compatibility matrix, migration transaction, or implementation digest.

FeatureRegistry IDs are treated as stable replay semantics, but retained features.json records only registered IDs and stage mapping. Changing Python feature implementation, parsers, sandbox, Lean toolchain, or default config can reinterpret a frozen run without a code identity pin.

Artifact state is path-based while evidence is hash-based and workspace is mutable/excluded. This permits stale path references, basename coupling, and replay mutation. V2 should make immutable content-addressed artifact records the only dependency interface.

Security boundary is inconsistent: lexical path validation is strong in config/state, but operational access is pathname/resolve based and vulnerable to races; verifier isolation is copy-and-diff rather than capability-enforced read-only mounts; symlink inputs intentionally bypass freezing.

Comments to downgrade until tested: 'resumable' is weakened by non-atomic restore; 'frozen replay' is false for undeclared workspace files; 'without following symlinks' is not race-proof; 'closed registry' allows injection; 'independent verdicts' lacks runtime lane attestation; 'strict campaign' permits undeclared top-level state.

V1 paid excessive deterministic compute in full-workspace checkpoint copy+fsync for every attempt, verifier copytree plus 3 workspace/2 dependency hash snapshots, whole-workspace source inventories for handoffs, full-state journal snapshots containing all prior events, and repeated whole-run evidence hashing. It also pays excessive model compute by rerouting all claim proposal/verifier stages, repeating full prompt directives, allowing up to 3 empty-output retries with huge timeouts, and using only syntactic novelty evidence.

Crash consistency is spread across journal, state.json, evidence.json, checkpoints, promotion cleanup lists, Herdr intents, and process registries without a single transaction/commit ID. Recovery therefore relies on status exceptions and permitted repair-path inference.

Mathematical assurance is directionally strong—deterministic receipts, Lean axioms/source checks, typed claim ledgers, and semantic equivalence—but campaign configuration remains a trust root for target meaning, command-to-target coverage, allowed axioms, model independence, and retry routing.
Agent verifier mutation detection can discover corruption of retained dependencies but runtime can subsequently reindex it; detection, rollback, and evidence authority are not one transaction.

Dynamic retry is coupled to resource provisioning: scheduler transitions can create pending agent work after Herdr panes were allocated. Resource acquisition must be lazy/idempotent per ready stage in v2.
No test corpus is supplied. All compatibility, durability, security, and mathematical-soundness conclusions are implementation readings, not observed test guarantees.

failure_modes: Platform limitation: import and lock logic require fcntl/POSIX semantics; no Windows path. flock protects only cooperating processes and does not prevent an attacker or writer that ignores the lock.

campaign_run_lock secures the lock leaf but not all parent-directory operations; most later path checks are resolve/check/use sequences vulnerable to external rename/symlink TOCTOU if the run tree is writable by another principal.

_validate_retained_state is strict for stage objects but does not reject unknown top-level fields and does not enforce cross-field state-machine consistency such as complete with running stages, completed_at/status agreement, handoff presence at awaiting_approval, attempts versus max_attempts, or event status validity beyond string type.

The status machine is duplicated and asymmetric: replan_required is valid and produced but not resumable; awaiting_sources/awaiting_strategy are valid/public exit-3 statuses but are neither produced nor resumable here; failed is nonresumable; restart_required is resumable.
CampaignOptions.max_parallel is unused and _execute always selects ready[0]; the claimed DAG runtime is serial. Exposing the option risks false operational expectations.

Workspace rollback is not atomic: _restore_checkpoint deletes the live workspace and copytrees the checkpoint into place. A crash, ENOSPC, permission error, or power loss can leave a partial/missing workspace.

Every attempt copies and fsyncs the full workspace. Large Lean projects/caches can cause severe latency, disk amplification, ENOSPC, and long interrupt windows. Symlinks are preserved in checkpoints, so mutable/external symlink targets are not frozen.

The journal stores full state snapshots including the ever-growing events list; repeated append_state_snapshot plus frequent full-run evidence hashing creates approximately quadratic retained-event bytes and high repeated hashing/copy cost.

evidence.json deliberately excludes every regular file under workspace/. Resume therefore does not establish that successful-stage workspace outputs/sources are unchanged; only selected handoff/evidence-input checks and promoted artifacts compensate.

_write_evidence hashes nearly the whole retained run repeatedly: initialization, stage transitions, retries, cleanup, finalization, and replay. Logs, prompts, receipts, checkpoints, and the growing journal are repeatedly rehashed.

_load_run permits evidence repair paths for running attempts by broad path-prefix discovery and promotion destinations/temporaries. Correctness depends on verify_evidence_for_repair semantics, which are not supplied; broad repair allowances increase corruption-acceptance risk.

Journal recovery copies then rereads under the campaign lock and detects a changed decoded state, but writers ignoring the lock can still race configuration/input/evidence reads or make byte changes yielding the same decoded state. The evidence read and later verification are not one fd-stable transaction.

Complete-state recovery can call _recover_interrupted_attempts because validator allows complete plus running stages; it can mutate stage state while preserving overall complete status, exposing missing semantic validation.
Retry option conflicts are checked after pending promotion cleanup, so invalid operator options can still mutate/delete retained outputs before raising.

_complete_pending_output_cleanup validates destination.parent via resolve then unlinks/rmtrees destination by pathname. Parent replacement and type changes create TOCTOU/race hazards; cleanup has no fd-relative confinement.

_route_retry does not clear affected summaries/artifacts/feedback uniformly, unlike _reset_stages. Pending stages can temporarily retain stale artifact references and descendant feedback; handoff/output cleanup is special-cased rather than a single reset transition.
Attempts are never reset. Dynamically rerouted stages may already be at max_attempts yet still execute once after being set pending, making max-attempt semantics dependent on route history.

A failed/revision result's artifacts are recorded before workspace restoration; workspace artifacts from the failed attempt may then disappear while stale state references remain until a later consume overwrites them.

Dynamic retry can target a previously succeeded agent for which no Herdr workspace/pane was created at _execute entry. Herdr panes are allocated only for agents pending at that moment; later routing can make an agent pending with context.herdr/pane_id absent, causing a synthetic failure.

Signal setup can partially install handlers and then clear previous_handlers on ValueError, potentially leaving already-installed handlers unrestored. KeyboardInterrupt is swallowed into stopped and run() returns normally, which callers must know.

Exceptions during finally (_finalize_herdr outside HerdrError, _save_state, _write_evidence, handler restoration) can mask the original execution failure. A Herdr close error is retained as undeclared top-level herdr_close_error.

Process cleanup is global per run after each stage. Its exact registration/isolation semantics are external; false-positive registration could terminate unrelated work, while unregistered descendants may survive.

Symlink inputs are intentionally live, omitted from input-snapshot verification, and can change across attempts/resume. This defeats full reproducibility and can expose external data or executable changes depending on sandbox policy.

_copy_input performs pathname checks followed by copy2/os.walk operations; a source concurrently swapped to a symlink can bypass the precheck. _path_without_symlinks and verified import likewise use pathname TOCTOU rather than dirfd/openat confinement, although post-copy hash checks protect selected file contents.
A partially failed new-run setup leaves an initialized-looking directory with configuration present, so run() refuses reuse; cleanup/recovery policy is absent.

_retained_path first relativizes to run_dir, which contains workspace, so normal workspace artifacts are stored as workspace/... rather than workspace:...; the workspace: branch is effectively exceptional. The schema supports two encodings without a demonstrated need.

_artifact_paths trusts lexically validated retained paths and follows path.is_file(); workspace is excluded from evidence, so an externally introduced workspace symlink can alter what a retained artifact path resolves to unless another check catches it.

approve_handoff loads unvalidated state, does not verify evidence/configuration, and joins handoff.path directly under workspace without an explicit lexical containment/symlink check. If retained journal/state is corrupt or attacker-controlled, ../ traversal is possible unless digest_handoff independently rejects it; that implementation is not supplied.

refresh_campaign_evidence, campaign_state, campaign_status, and campaign_resolved_for_run do not take campaign_run_lock. Refresh can race a controller/replay and publish an internally inconsistent index; read helpers may observe changing state depending on journal guarantees.

Replay is called frozen but executes against the live workspace. It only snapshots declared evidence_inputs; it can mutate undeclared workspace files and leaves those mutations in a complete run. Because workspace files are excluded from evidence, refresh then legitimizes no record of those changes.

Replay constructs receipt paths as run/value and does not handle workspace: encoding; command receipts are normally run-relative, but schema polymorphism is latent. It also assumes parsed retained receipt is a dict before .get().

Replay compares a selected list of sandbox metadata fields, not executable/tool binary digests or all environment values. Policy equality does not prove same verifier implementation/toolchain unless sandbox metadata embeds those identities.

Evidence/config/input manifest validators largely ignore their schema_version fields and rely on exact artifact-list equality; migration and duplicate/path validation behavior depends on imported artifact helpers.

Promotion/input/config publication and evidence indexing are separate transactions. A crash between state, journal, output cleanup, checkpoint removal, and evidence refresh creates repair cases encoded ad hoc rather than by one commit protocol.

verified_artifact verifies a pinned evidence file and each selected file after copy, but source state/evidence/path traversal is not held on stable file descriptors. Concurrent source-run mutation can cause denial/failure and depends on hash checks to avoid silent import.

path_is_excluded normalizes backslashes and ./ and implements /** prefix semantics; the promotion feature has a different matcher. Identical configuration patterns can therefore select different file sets.

No tests are present in the supplied corpus, so crash points, fsync durability, malicious symlink races, journal truncation, evidence repair, replay mutation, and status transitions have no visible test evidence.
