No CLI caller is supplied, although the exit-code mapper and public helpers strongly imply one.
invariants: Exactly one cooperative controller per resolved run directory is intended: .campaign.lock is opened O_NOFOLLOW/O_CLOEXEC, required to be regular, and held with nonblocking exclusive flock for run/resume/approval/replay.

Retained state must have schema_version exactly 1, matching campaign_id, exact stage-ID set, safe lexical artifact paths, valid enum-like statuses, nonnegative attempts/revisions/interruptions, unique artifacts/cleanup IDs, and a handoff matching frozen campaign producer/path/schema/digest/approval timestamp.
A stage marked running must have attempts>0; every execution attempt checkpoints the entire workspace before marking the stage running and saving state.
Only pending stages whose dependencies succeeded are runnable; failed/skipped dependencies force descendants to skipped. Build stages are additionally gated by a succeeded and approved handoff.
Required-stage success is the mathematical campaign completion criterion; failed required stages produce incomplete, while failure_policy may produce replan_required or restart_required.
Retries reset selected/upstream-routed stages plus transitive descendants; handoff state is invalidated when its producer is affected; promoted outputs are scheduled for durable cleanup before rerun.
A retained handoff is approved only for an exact SHA-256 digest; later digest change is rejected before build scheduling.

Configuration and copied input snapshots are digested and checked before resume. Provenance imports pin source run ID, campaign ID, complete status, evidence-file digest, indexed path hashes/sizes, and reject observed symlink ancestry.
Feature artifacts must resolve under run_dir/workspace; handoff paths must remain under workspace and be regular non-symlink files at campaign handoff time.

Replay requires a complete evidence-verified campaign, a retained replayable command stage, unchanged declared evidence inputs, and equality of selected sandbox/security metadata before and after execution.

Durability intent is explicit: atomic JSON writes, append-only snapshots, directory/file fsync for checkpoints, temporary staging plus replace for checkpoint publication, and evidence refresh after controller-owned replay receipts.

Security is filesystem-integrity based, not authenticity based: hashes detect mutation relative to retained indexes/pins but there is no signature, MAC, remote attestation, or hostile-owner protection visible.
line_findings: Module docstring claim 'Resumable stage-DAG runtime': dependency scheduling and recovery exist, but scheduling is serial and workspace certification is incomplete.
_REPLAY_SECURITY_FIELDS: useful explicit compatibility allowlist, but omission becomes policy; executable identity and full environment equivalence are not visibly bound.
campaign_run_lock: O_NOFOLLOW plus regular-file check is strong leaf defense; nonblocking lock makes contention explicit rather than waiting.
_validate_retained_artifact: accepts both ordinary relative and workspace: paths but normal writer rarely emits workspace: because workspace is under run_dir.
_validate_retained_state: exact stage-ID equality safely rejects campaign drift; top-level extras remain accepted, enabling herdr_close_error but weakening 'strict' schema semantics.
_validate_retained_state events loop: event status is any string and chronological timestamps are not parsed; event log is structurally, not semantically, validated.
CampaignOptions.max_parallel: declared and retained nowhere, never read after construction.
CampaignBuilder.__init__: validates all feature configs eagerly, a good fail-fast property; registry code/version identity is not retained, only IDs/mapping.
run(): creates a caller-specified directory before checking configuration; a concurrent external initializer is only partly controlled by later lock.
_select_new_run: timestamp plus 24-bit random token and mkdir(exist_ok=False) provides collision detection, not guaranteed collision avoidance.
_prepare_new_run: seven directories are created non-transactionally; initial state controller_pid is observability, not lease ownership.
_load_run first journal pass: copying to a temporary run avoids repairing the authoritative journal before evidence verification, a sound recovery idea.
_load_run second journal pass: confirms decoded-state equality but not immutable bytes; recovered_tail is reassigned from the authoritative load.
_verify_resume_evidence: status mismatch exception for running+pending_output_cleanup is an implicit transaction state encoded outside the formal status machine.

_recoverable_attempt_evidence_paths: attempt file matching uses startswith(attempt_name), so attempt-01-extra also qualifies; checkpoint unindexed files and promotion temporaries are permitted repair material.
_reset_stages versus _route_retry: duplicated descendant-closure/reset state machines have materially different field clearing behavior.
_schedule_promotion_output_cleanup: state/evidence are persisted before deletion and again after deletion, intentionally crash-resumable but expensive.
_execute: ready[0] proves max_parallel is dead and topological order determines all execution.
_execute finally unregister condition: close_herdr=False intentionally keeps campaign registration when workspace ID remains; lifecycle depends on external registry persistence semantics.
_ready_stages: mutates skipped stages while merely querying readiness, mixing scheduler query and transition side effects.
_checkpoint_workspace: os.replace publishes the copied workspace tree, but existing checkpoint removal and source copy are not fd-confined.
_restore_checkpoint: destructive delete-then-copy is the main corruption window and should not survive v2.
_cleanup_orphan_checkpoints: deletes every recovery child without validating ownership/name; safe only because recovery/ is trusted and controller-exclusive.
_recover_interrupted_attempts: reconciles saved IDs, process registry, creation labels, and Herdr listing—four sources of resource truth indicate a duplicated distributed state machine.
_recover_interrupted_attempts: without a journal, missing checkpoints are tolerated and a running stage is reset against whatever live workspace remains, so legacy recovery is nondeterministic.
_run_stage: catches selected operational exceptions into FeatureResult but lets programming errors fail the whole run, a useful distinction if made explicit in v2.
_consume: cleanup failure overrides an otherwise successful mathematical result, correctly treating leaked execution as campaign failure.
_consume revision path: global campaign revisions and per-stage attempts are separate budgets whose combined semantics are not formalized.
_route_retry: unknown targets call _fail_required even when requesting_stage may not be required; naming and policy are coupled.
_finish_from_stages: optional stage failures do not block complete, by design; completion does not require all stages terminal beyond scheduler exhaustion.
_approval_needed: digest is recomputed whenever build is pending; approved handoff mutation raises rather than invalidating approval, correctly fail-closed.
_create_herdr_workspace: saving creation_label before create and retaining it until workspace ID save is a sound crash-reconciliation pattern.
_finalize_herdr: stores herdr_close_error outside the validated declared state schema.
_retain_configuration: retains resolved config and source instructions, but feature implementation version/package digest is absent, so replay semantics can drift under the same feature ID.
_create_inputs symlink branch: records source path only and does not digest target content, explicitly trading reproducibility for liveness.
_retained_path: run-relative branch shadows workspace-relative branch for ordinary layouts.
_save_state: journal append precedes state.json projection, correctly makes journal authoritative; full snapshots and duplicate JSON writes are costly.
_fsync_tree: ignores symlinks and disappearing files; it fsyncs every regular file and deepest directories first, favoring durability over scale.
_approve_handoff_locked: status gate is present, but full retained-state/evidence/path validation is absent.
verify_campaign_bundle: returns artifact count only; it does not expose verified root/digest or schema, limiting machine attestation value.
replay_verifier_command: verifies evidence before replay but then intentionally modifies the certified run by adding receipts and potentially modifying workspace.
campaign_state/campaign_status: repeat schema/status logic rather than calling the campaign-aware validator; campaign identity and stage structure are unchecked.
campaign_status_exit_code: all noncomplete/nonawaiting statuses collapse to 1, losing replan/restart/stopped distinctions at process boundary.
_write_campaign_evidence: excludes .campaign.lock correctly and workspace files wholesale; generated_at guarantees evidence-file digest changes on every refresh.
_verify_configuration_manifest: does not explicitly require schema_version=1 and trusts artifact serialization/order contract from digest_tree.
_copy_input: rejects source symlinks in the non-racing case and applies exclusions before symlink rejection, so excluded symlinks are ignored rather than rejected.
_copy_verified_file: post-copy SHA-256 and size verification is a strong defense against source mutation during import.
path_is_excluded: custom /** behavior differs from plain fnmatch and from features._matches.
_verify_input_manifest: silently skips unknown/symlink strategies rather than rejecting them; symlink records therefore receive no resume integrity check.
files.model_tier: deterministic — all orchestration, validation, hashing, scheduling, recovery, approval digest binding, and replay policy must remain non-LLM; human is required only for manual handoff approval and exceptional corruption adjudication.
playbook_relevance: Transactional run-store playbook: immutable event records plus materialized state, commit IDs, checksummed/versioned schemas, atomic projection rebuild, and crash-point testing.
Filesystem confinement playbook: openat2/dirfd operations, O_NOFOLLOW at every component, same-filesystem staging, atomic directory swap, ownership/mode checks, and explicit hardlink/mount policy.

DAG retry playbook: one formal transition table for pending/running/succeeded/failed/skipped and run statuses, dependency closure, attempt budgets, handoff invalidation, artifact tombstones, and deterministic idempotence.
Content-addressed workspace playbook: snapshot only changed files/trees, Merkle roots, immutable stage outputs, overlay/reflink checkpoints, and no full copy/fsync per attempt.

Evidence commit playbook: append artifact hashes incrementally at publication, bind state/event/output roots in one commit, distinguish mutable workspace from certified artifacts, and sign/export attestations when trust crosses principals.
External-resource intent playbook: durable create/close intents, idempotency keys, reconciliation, lease ownership, and tests for every crash window.
Verifier replay playbook: disposable read-only snapshot, pinned executable/toolchain digest, minimal environment, declared inputs/outputs, mutation rejection, and retained receipt attestation.
Provenance import playbook: signed/pinned source bundle, fd-stable traversal, per-file post-copy verification, destination staging, and atomic publication.
Cost-control playbook: avoid repeated full-run hashing and full-state snapshots; benchmark O(changed bytes + new events), not O(total run bytes) per transition.
files.purpose: Owns the v1 campaign controller lifecycle: create/retain a run, serialize stage-DAG execution, checkpoint/restore the mutable workspace, persist journal/state/evidence, route retries/revisions, manage Herdr resources, approve typed research-to-build handoffs, import provenance-pinned artifacts, verify bundles, and replay retained command verifiers. The module is also the de facto filesystem schema and recovery protocol for a run.
tests_or_consumers: Visible production consumers: CampaignBuilder itself consumes every helper; FeatureRegistry and all feature IDs feed _run_stage; claim/semantic/command receipts and handoffs are consumed through artifact paths; prior campaign runs are consumed by verified_artifact.
Public status/exit/replay/approval helpers are likely CLI-facing, but no CLI source or named call sites are supplied; treat actual external compatibility as unknown.
No test modules, fixtures, assertions, or explicit test names are supplied. Comments/docstrings are implementation claims, not test evidence.

Required v2 consumers to add: deterministic state-transition tests; property tests for retained-state and path schemas; kill-at-every-write crash recovery tests; concurrent writer/TOCTOU adversarial tests; symlink/hardlink/mount escape tests; evidence-repair tests; large-workspace cost benchmarks; replay non-mutation tests; Herdr crash-window and dynamic-reroute tests; cross-version migration fixtures.
files.v2_disposition: REWRITE/DECOMPOSE. Preserve the public concepts and proven security checks, but replace this monolithic controller with separately versioned RunStore, StateMachine, Scheduler, WorkspaceTransaction, EvidenceIndex, ResourceManager, HandoffApproval, ProvenanceImporter, and ReplayService. Provide a v1 read-only/migration adapter; do not carry forward ad hoc full-state journaling or live-workspace replay semantics.

failure_modes: Path safety uses resolve/check/use and therefore remains TOCTOU-sensitive under concurrent filesystem mutation. It does not visibly address hardlinks, bind mounts, mount replacement, special files, or hostile shared ownership.

_workspace_path resolves the leaf. Callers that later test path.is_symlink() cannot detect that the configured leaf was a symlink; notably PromotionFeature accepts a symlink to an in-workspace file/tree despite claiming linked sources fail.

snapshot_workspace_inputs checks symlink ancestry before resolution and then traverses by pathname; a concurrent swap can bypass checks. Overlapping declared inputs are silently deduplicated by artifact path, which may or may not match schema intent.

Verifier isolation copies the whole workspace for every attempt and computes up to three full workspace source snapshots plus two retained-dependency snapshots. This is excessive I/O/hash compute for large Lean workspaces.

Verifier source snapshots intentionally exclude agents/, configured agent handoffs, common caches, and every path with symlink ancestry. Mutations there are invisible to mutation enforcement; whether all exclusions are safe depends on later consumers.

If a verifier mutates retained dependency evidence, the feature detects it but does not restore it. Runtime checkpoints restore workspace only; the subsequent evidence refresh can index the corrupted retained dependency as current, turning detection into failure without repair.

Verifier canonical workspace mutation is only rolled back because runtime restores the stage checkpoint after failed FeatureResult. Direct use of the feature outside CampaignBuilder would leave mutation behind.

Verifier copytree preserves symlinks in the isolated workspace. Live symlink targets are not isolated and may expose/change external state subject to sandbox enforcement, whose implementation is not supplied.

Agent tools are only nonempty strings at general validation; no global tool allowlist is enforced here. Claim/semantic verifier handoffs receive a narrow read/grep/glob/write list, but other verifier/review configurations can differ.

Agent workspace_executables defaults true, a risky default for mutable/untrusted workspaces. The actual runner sandbox, tool permissions, secret filtering, and receipt atomicity are external and unknown.

Agent request JSON retains absolute workspace/run/prompt/log paths, model/thinking choices, tools, and execution policy. Whether any policy fields or paths reveal sensitive deployment information is not assessed.

The host environment is inherited for CommandFeature, and agent runner behavior is external. Declared secret names are prohibited only from inline command config; secret injection, redaction, sandbox metadata, stdout/stderr leakage, and replay treatment are unknown.

_wait_for_receipt polls a mutable JSON file and accepts any dict whose status is not running. It does not validate receipt schema/identity/attempt, and a partially or maliciously written status can end waiting early. Timeout formula can reach roughly four days at maximum settings.
Agent report/output/handoff reads occur after receipt observation without an explicit publication transaction or fsync. Safety depends on agent_runner writing receipt last and atomically, not shown.
Novelty validation is syntactic and self-reported: it does not establish a materially new mathematical method or evidence. Treating it as a substantive novelty gate would be unsound.

Continuation decision stop returns FeatureResult failed. Runtime may retry it and eventually mark a required campaign incomplete, conflating evidence-based successful termination with execution/mathematical failure.
Review decision receipt lacks schema_version while adjacent receipts are versioned. Handoff and receipt schemas span v1/v2 with no central envelope or migration mechanism.

_write_source_inventory hashes almost every regular workspace file on each handoff attempt, including prior agent material/caches not excluded there; this is another major repeated-compute hotspot and its inclusion policy differs from verifier snapshots.

Source inventory skips symlink ancestry but otherwise identifies sources only by content digest; duplicate-content files share acceptable digests, so a research-v1 citation may not prove the claimed path unless the handoff schema separately binds path.

Agent failure evidence excludes prompt/request/stdout/stderr from FeatureResult artifacts even though global run evidence indexes them; consumers using only stage artifacts see an incomplete forensic set.

CommandFeature records evidence inputs only before execution. A successful command can mutate those inputs and still produce a passing original receipt; ClaimLedger later catches changes for configured receipt stages, but ordinary command consumers do not.
Command receipts record argv/cwd but do not visibly pin executable binary/toolchain hashes. replayable=true therefore means policy/config replay, not byte-identical verifier implementation.

ScalarBound does not validate ordering of baseline and limit; impossible/reversed intervals become runtime rejection. Strict inequalities reject candidates exactly at the configured limit, which must be intentional and documented.

Lean contract can mutate the workspace project/caches during proof execution. Runtime rollback occurs only on a failed/retried stage; successful proof side effects become part of mutable workspace but are not workspace-evidence indexed.
Lean repair_target validation checks only existence, not graph direction, mode, feature compatibility, self-targeting, or attempt-budget feasibility; routing can create pathological recomputation.

Claim model diversity is inferred from configured (omp, model) pairs only. Aliases can count as diverse, actual runtime model identity is not attested, thinking/tool lane is ignored, and independence from shared prompts/data is not established.

Claim deterministic coverage is self-declared by covers_targets in frozen command config/receipt. The engine does not prove that the command semantics actually establish those mathematical targets; configuration review remains a trust root.
Claim ledger failure retries proposal plus every verifier, even when only one target/verdict is unresolved, potentially paying unnecessary high-tier agent compute.

SemanticContractFeature contains a concrete validation bug: when repair_target is non-null it is unconditionally added to unknown, so every configured repair_target is rejected even when present in campaign.by_id.
Semantic rejection can produce no detailed required_changes when Lean passed and review relation is non-equivalent but review.issues is empty; rerun feedback then lacks a repair obligation.
Semantic independence is role/configuration based. The reviewer directly depends on the Lean stage and no runtime model/provenance attestation proves independent generation.
Promotion initial destination nonexistence check is racy; Path.replace may overwrite a file that appears between check and replace. It lacks explicit file/directory fsync after publication.
Promotion of an empty directory succeeds with zero promoted artifacts. Whether that can satisfy a required output obligation is not constrained.
Promotion and input exclusion matchers have different normalization and /** semantics, creating campaign-authoring surprises and possible unintended retention.

FeatureRegistry(features=()) selects defaults because of features or defaults, so callers cannot intentionally construct an empty registry. Constructor injection also means the registry is not truly closed globally despite the docstring claim.
Retained configuration records feature IDs but not implementation/package digests or per-feature schema versions. A v2/new installation can reinterpret a resolved v1 campaign under changed code.

Many execute methods rely on runtime catching ConfigurationError/OSError/RuntimeError/ValueError. Direct consumers of the feature protocol see exceptions rather than uniformly normalized FeatureResult.

No supplied tests verify parser boundaries, mutation detection/rollback, tool restrictions, model diversity, receipt uniqueness, Lean substitution injection resistance, semantic equivalence identity, promotion races, or feature schema compatibility.
interfaces: Core Python contracts: FeatureResult, FeatureContext, CampaignFeature Protocol, FeatureRegistry.feature_ids/feature()/validate(), snapshot_workspace_inputs().
Stable feature IDs selected by campaign data: agent, command, lean_contract, claim_ledger, semantic_contract, artifact_promote.

Config schemas: AgentConfig, CommandConfig, LeanContractConfig/LeanSubstitutionConfig/ScalarBound, ClaimLedgerConfig, SemanticContractConfig, PromotionConfig; validation rejects unknown keys through _table.

Agent execution interface: retained request JSON for campaign_builder.agent_runner, Herdr.run_in_pane, prompt/output/stdout/stderr/receipt paths, tools/model/thinking/max_time/retry options, execution policy, sandbox read paths, and optional typed handoff.

Typed handoff interfaces consumed from handoff/claims/semantic modules: research and review contracts, claim-proposals-v1, claim-verdicts-v1, semantic-review-v1, plus ReviewDecision and ContinuationDecision textual parsers.

Command interface: argv tuple executed without a shell through run_captured_command; receipt schema_version=2 includes inputs, output hashes/truncation, sandbox metadata, target coverage, replayability, and exit/error data.

Lean interface: run_proof_gate over a workspace project and frozen input-snapshot contract, typed substitutions, allowed axioms, Lake executable, timeout, optional scalar bound and repair route; proof-gate receipt is expected to be schema_version=2 by semantic consumers.
Claim/semantic interfaces: external build_claim_ledger(), ClaimProposalBundle/ClaimVerdictBundle/SemanticReview parsers; direct dependency artifacts are located by retained basename/schema.
Promotion interface: copies one workspace file/tree to a run-relative destination and emits receipt schema_version=1.

Visible consumer: runtime.CampaignBuilder validates configs and invokes execute(context), then consumes status/artifacts/retry_targets/required_changes. replay_verifier_command reconstructs CommandConfig. No tests are supplied.
invariants: All feature tables are intended to be closed schemas: required keys must exist and unknown keys are rejected; strings are nonempty, integers bounded, booleans exact, and relative paths reject absolute/empty/dot/dot-dot components.
Workspace path helpers resolve and require containment under the resolved workspace. Evidence input snapshots reject symlink ancestry/tree symlinks and require regular files when paths are declared.
Agent handoff and schema must be configured together; handoff agents require read+write; review and handoff are mutually exclusive; continuation gates cannot also be review/handoff stages.

Verifier-typed agents run in a copied isolated workspace. Protected source snapshots before/after, canonical workspace snapshots, and retained dependency snapshots are compared; a detected mutation fails the feature.
Agent success requires a successful runner receipt and report file. Typed handoff success additionally requires a regular non-symlink handoff passing digest/schema/source-digest validation.

Novelty gate requires byte difference plus an exact Retry novelty section with three minimally long fields; continuation gate requires a typed JSON decision; review requires a typed accept/revise decision.

Commands are shell-free, sandboxed through campaign execution policy, optionally replayable, and bind configured evidence inputs into a schema-v2 receipt. Target coverage requires evidence_inputs and declared target IDs.
Command inline environment cannot contain names declared as secret_environment, but host environment is inherited at execution.

Lean substitutions are name/kind validated; metadata references require configured JSON metadata fields containing strings; proof success is delegated to run_proof_gate and optional scalar bounds are strict interior bounds.

Claim ledger stage must be required and directly depend on proposal, every verifier, deterministic receipt stages, and optional adjudicator. Proposal/verdict handoff schemas, verifier category/tools, receipt replayability, target declarations, and optional configured model diversity are validated.

Claim target closure requires passing deterministic receipts for covered targets when receipt stages are configured, unchanged receipt evidence inputs, loaded proposal/verdict bundles, and build_claim_ledger reporting all required targets verified.

Semantic contract stage must be required, directly depend on Lean and reviewer stages, require reviewer dependence on Lean, exact declaration/informal-statement identity, exactly one matching Lean axiom report, Lean pass, equivalent review relation, and no review issues.

Promotion destination must remain under run_dir, must not preexist at initial check, and promotion tree traversal rejects encountered symlinks. Outputs and receipts are returned as retained artifacts.
Feature registry rejects duplicate IDs and raises ConfigurationError for unknown feature IDs; campaign validation is eager and deterministic.

Mathematical trust is layered: agent prose alone is not certification; deterministic command receipts, Lean proof gates, typed claim verdict aggregation, and semantic equivalence review are separate gates. The soundness of imported parsers/gates is outside this file.
line_findings: Module docstring claim 'Typed reusable execution features': config dataclasses are typed, but retained JSON envelopes and artifact references are heterogeneous and version coupling remains implicit.
FeatureResult.succeeded: only literal succeeded is success; continuation stop and revision_requested are non-success, forcing runtime-specific interpretation.
_table: strict unknown-key rejection is a strong forward-compatibility brake; v2 needs explicit extension/version policy rather than silently loosening it.
_relative: normalizes backslashes before PurePosixPath validation, yielding platform-independent retained path syntax.
_workspace_handoff_path: validates resolved parent but intentionally does not resolve leaf, allowing safe removal/replacement of a leaf symlink; this differs importantly from _workspace_path.
snapshot_workspace_inputs docstring claim 'without following symlinks': implementation checks symlinks by pathname but is not race-free and digest_file behavior is external.
_verifier_source_snapshot: handoff exclusion is derived only from agent feature configs; non-agent generated files can remain protected or unprotected unexpectedly.
_retained_dependency_snapshot: configuration and input-snapshot are hashed for every verifier, duplicating global evidence work.
_remove_prior_handoff: permits deleting regular file or symlink only and rejects directories/special files, a good fail-closed leaf rule.
AgentFeature.validate: verifier_type is permitted only for review or selected handoff schemas, tying verification role to output shape rather than an explicit capability contract.
AgentFeature.validate: handoff requires read/write but does not reject additional dangerous tools except later for claim/semantic verifier schemas.
AgentFeature._execute_verifier: canonical prior handoff is deleted before source snapshot; runtime checkpoint is the only rollback mechanism if execution fails.
AgentFeature._execute_verifier: isolated personal results are copied to canonical workspace before mutation verdict, but agents/ is excluded from canonical snapshots by design.
AgentFeature._execute_agent request: max wait multiplies max_time+70 by empty_output_retries+1, making retries a potentially enormous wall-clock budget.
AgentFeature._execute_agent: personal failure.json is in workspace and will be rolled back on retry, while run-dir failure evidence persists.
Novelty path: _validate_retry_novelty hashes current report by filename rather than passed text; correctness depends on output text and file being identical/stable.
Continuation prompt says 'Return exactly one JSON object'; parse_text enforces imported semantics, but stop is mapped to failed rather than a distinct terminal outcome.
Review receipt: unlike most JSON outputs, attempt-NN-decision.json has no schema_version.
_write_source_inventory: source digests include dependency reports but not all dependency artifacts; handoff evidence scope is report-centric.
_has_symlink_ancestor: assumes path is beneath root; callers satisfy this, but the helper itself has no termination guard for an unrelated path.

_render_agent_prompt: rereads campaign/stage instruction files at execution. Runtime retains copies but config paths are rewritten only in resolved campaigns; for a fresh campaign, external instruction mutation after validation could alter prompts unless configuration retention/config objects freeze paths as expected.
_render_agent_prompt: absolute retained paths and full campaign directive are repeated for every attempt, increasing token cost; shared immutable prompt prefixes should be cached/referenced.
_wait_for_receipt: any terminal status string returns immediately; no allowed-status set or role/attempt correlation.
CommandFeature.validate: cwd '.' is represented as empty string, creating a canonicalization special case visible in retained config.
CommandFeature.validate: covers_targets validates declared IDs but not target kind or what verifier class is suitable.
CommandFeature.execute: on evidence-input validation failure receipt schema remains v2 but omits sandbox/output fields, so consumers must support shape variants.
CommandFeature.execute: evidence_inputs_after is absent from original receipts but present in replay receipts, creating asymmetric mutation guarantees.
ScalarBound.accepts: minimize is limit<candidate<baseline and maximize baseline<candidate<limit; endpoint exclusion is hard-coded.
LeanContractFeature.validate: legacy string substitutions default to token, preserving compatibility at the cost of weaker explicit typing.
LeanContractFeature.execute: contract is deliberately loaded from frozen input-snapshot while project is mutable workspace, a sound separation if contract path semantics are documented.
ClaimLedgerFeature docstring claim 'independent stage verdicts': direct stage separation is enforced; actual model/process independence is not.
ClaimLedgerFeature.validate: receipt stage must depend directly on proposals, and each verifier must depend directly on all receipts, creating dense DAG coupling.
ClaimLedgerFeature.validate: model diversity compares config omp/model objects, not normalized provider/model IDs or receipts.
ClaimLedgerFeature.execute: exactly one JSON artifact per receipt stage is required; adding another diagnostic JSON to CommandFeature artifacts would break this consumer.
ClaimLedgerFeature.execute: when receipt_stages is empty, deterministic coverage requirement is disabled even for required targets.
_claim_stage_handoff: category must equal literal verification and tool set must be a subset of read/grep/glob/write, a useful reusable verifier profile.
_dependency_handoff: identifies handoff by basename among dependency artifacts; two configured paths sharing a basename are ambiguous at consumption time.
SemanticContractFeature.validate: repair_target bug is the expression unknown.add(repair_target) rather than adding only if repair_target not in by_id.
SemanticContractFeature.execute: exact informal_statement string equality freezes wording, not merely semantics; this is intentionally stricter than reviewer relation.
_matching_lean_axiom_report: requires exactly one matching declaration report and validates axioms as strings, preventing ambiguous declaration identity.
_lean_dependency_receipt: identifies proof receipts by schema_version=2 plus axiom_reports, not an explicit receipt_type discriminator.
PromotionFeature.execute: source returned by _workspace_path is already resolved, so source.is_symlink() cannot enforce the stated linked-source rejection.
PromotionFeature.execute: tempfile is in destination parent, so replace is same-filesystem; no-replace and fsync semantics are still missing.
_copy_promoted_tree: exclusion is evaluated before symlink rejection, allowing excluded symlink entries to be silently skipped.
FeatureRegistry.__init__: features or defaults makes an empty tuple impossible and custom injected registries possible, contradicting a literal reading of 'Closed'.
FeatureRegistry.validate: dict comprehension preserves eager all-stage validation but loses richer per-feature schema/version metadata.
files.model_tier: deterministic for validation, command/Lean execution, claim aggregation, semantic receipt checking, promotion, and model routing; Luna for routine extraction/reporting, Terra for mathematical proposal/verification and semantic review, Sol only for exceptional hard research/adjudication, human for campaign contracts and approval—not for state transitions.
playbook_relevance: Versioned feature-envelope playbook: feature_id, config_schema, result_schema, implementation digest, deterministic validator, migration adapter, and capability declaration.
Model-lane playbook: task risk/complexity routing, immutable model/provider identity receipt, independence constraints, budget caps, and escalation Luna→Terra→Sol→human.

Verifier-isolation playbook: immutable read-only source snapshot, writable scratch/output mounts, no canonical workspace paths, declared output schema, and discard-on-exit instead of copy-and-diff as primary security.
Typed-handoff playbook: canonical JSON, schema URI/version, source path+digest citations, producer identity, frozen campaign target binding, and deterministic validation before publication.

Deterministic receipt playbook: command binary/toolchain digest, argv/cwd/environment policy, before-and-after input roots, declared outputs, sandbox attestation, replay recipe, and one schema envelope.

Lean certification playbook: template/substitution injection safety, exact declaration identity, axiom allowlist, source issue checks, toolchain pin, semantic correspondence gate, and minimal retained proof receipt.

Claim adjudication playbook: proposal IDs/content hashes, verifier-type coverage matrix, runtime lane identity, explicit conflict resolution, target-to-receipt semantics, and selective retry of unresolved obligations.
Artifact publication playbook: stage into same filesystem, fsync content/tree, no-replace atomic publish, immutable destination, Merkle manifest, and idempotent cleanup tombstone.

Retry-economics playbook: route only implicated proposal/verifier/repair stages, retain valid independent verdicts, cap high-tier calls, and require machine-checkable new evidence rather than self-declared novelty.
files.purpose: Defines the closed-by-ID v1 feature layer and typed config validation for agent work, sandboxed commands, Lean proof contracts, claim ledgers, semantic equivalence contracts, and artifact promotion. It also renders agent prompts, validates typed handoffs/reviews/continuation decisions, snapshots evidence inputs, isolates verifier agents, and normalizes all outcomes into FeatureResult for the runtime.
tests_or_consumers: Visible consumers: runtime.CampaignBuilder calls FeatureRegistry.validate and CampaignFeature.execute; runtime replay validates/replays command stages; ClaimLedgerFeature and SemanticContractFeature consume artifacts produced by AgentFeature, CommandFeature, and LeanContractFeature.

External imported consumers/producers visible only by API: campaign_builder.agent_runner must consume request JSON and publish runner receipts/output; Herdr provides pane execution; claims/handoff/semantic/lean/command modules define substantive parsers and gates.
No test files or named tests are supplied. There is no visible evidence that comments such as 'independent', 'frozen', 'without following symlinks', or 'closed' have adversarial tests.

Required v2 consumers/tests: config-schema golden files; property/fuzz tests for every parser/path; feature contract tests with malformed receipts; immutable artifact publication tests; verifier escape/mutation tests; Lean injection/axiom/declaration identity tests; claim disagreement/model-identity tests; semantic repair_target regression; promotion crash/race tests; cost benchmarks on large workspaces.
files.v2_disposition: REWRITE/DECOMPOSE while KEEPING the feature concepts. Give each feature an independently versioned config/result/receipt contract and pure validator; separate deterministic executor adapters from model-task definitions; replace mutable Path artifact lists with content-addressed immutable artifact references. Replace full-state journal snapshots with immutable transition events carrying sequence/commit IDs and checksums; derive state deterministically and atomically publish a projection. Formalize every allowed run/stage transition and cross-field invariant once.
Ship a v1 read-only validator/importer and explicit one-way migration. Never let v2 code silently reinterpret v1 feature IDs/config defaults or mutate a v1 bundle before migration.

Use immutable content-addressed stage outputs and workspace snapshots. Implement checkpoints via reflink/overlay/Merkle-delta where available, publish by atomic root-pointer swap, and never delete the only live workspace before a restore is durable.

Bind state root, event head, artifact Merkle root, configuration root, input root, and resource-intent head in one evidence commit. Incrementally hash new immutable files; stop rescanning the entire run after every transition.

Make workspace trust explicit: forbid live symlink inputs for certified runs or mark campaigns nonreproducible/nonreplayable; use fd-relative no-follow traversal and ownership/mode checks for all trusted filesystem operations.
Implement lazy per-stage agent resource provisioning so any dynamically routed pending agent receives a workspace/pane; make create/close idempotent with durable idempotency keys and leases.

Either implement max_parallel with deterministic concurrency semantics, isolated workspace branches, merge/conflict policy, and resource caps, or remove the option. Do not expose inert concurrency controls.

Unify retry/reset logic: compute affected closure once, clear/tombstone summaries/artifacts/feedback consistently, enforce attempt/revision budgets before scheduling, invalidate handoffs/promotions generically, and route only unresolved obligations.
Represent continuation stop as a first-class successful terminal/policy outcome rather than failed; define its effect on required stages and public exit codes.

Run verifier agents and replay commands in disposable immutable/read-only snapshots with writable scratch/output-only mounts. Compare before/after roots as defense in depth, then discard the environment; never mutate a complete certified workspace.

Pin verifier executable, package, model/provider lane where relevant, Lean/Lake/toolchain, sandbox backend/policy, and normalized environment contract. Replay must verify these identities, not only selected metadata fields.

Command receipts must include before and after declared-input roots, declared output hashes, executable/toolchain identity, receipt_type, and sandbox attestation. A mutating verifier must fail before a passing receipt is published.
Fix SemanticContractFeature repair_target validation; validate graph direction/feature compatibility for every repair target and add a regression fixture.
Replace config-tuple model diversity with runtime-attested normalized lane identities and declared independence policy. Preserve valid verdicts and selectively rerun only implicated claims/verifiers.

Make claim target coverage machine-auditable: target kind determines acceptable deterministic/Lean/semantic evidence classes; a command's self-declared covers_targets alone cannot establish semantics.
Centralize path/exclusion semantics and use the same normalized matcher for input copy, verifier snapshots, source inventory, evidence inputs, and promotion.
Use atomic no-replace publication plus fsync for promotions and immutable artifacts; encode cleanup as artifact tombstones rather than pathname deletion lists.

Approval must validate the full migrated state/evidence/config contract under lock, confine the handoff path fd-relatively, bind approver identity/policy as appropriate, and sign or MAC exported approvals if trust crosses filesystem owners.
Public state/status/evidence readers need snapshot-consistent locking or commit-head reads. Evidence refresh must be locked and should be impossible while a transaction is open.

Establish model budget policy: deterministic first; Luna for routine extraction; Terra for proof search/verification/semantic review; Sol only after measurable Terra failure or exceptional hardness; human for frozen contracts/approvals/corruption. Record cost, tokens, latency, and escalation reason.

Add exhaustive tests: transition model/property tests, parser fuzzing, crash injection at every durable operation, process/Herdr crash windows, symlink/hardlink/mount races, concurrent readers/writers, replay mutation, evidence repair, migration golden bundles, mathematical receipt forgery, and large-workspace performance thresholds.

cross_cutting: Authoritative-state coupling is unresolved: journal.py declares events.jsonl authoritative, while inspection.py consumes state.json; artifacts/evidence may bless either projection without checking equivalence. V2 needs exactly one authority plus a versioned generated projection and digest linkage.

There are duplicated persistence/path primitives: _fsync_directory exists in artifacts.py and journal.py; JSON-object/text parsing is independently reimplemented in claims.py, semantic.py, inspection.py, and metrics.py; relative-path safety is independently partial in artifacts.py and inspection.py while metrics.py has none. Consolidate to avoid policy drift.

Duplicated state/closure machines exist at several layers: claim verdict→rejected/blocked/verified, target→ledger verified/incomplete, stage→succeeded/failed/skipped, obligation→verified/rejected/blocked, campaign→complete/other, and assurance profiles. Their prerequisites are not represented in one typed dependency graph, allowing failed claim stages to produce passed closure and unrelated Lean/semantic stages to produce formalization assurance.

Schema/version risk is high and fragmented: evidence v1, journal v1, proposal v1, verdict v1, semantic v1, state/features v1, claim-inspection report v1, claim ledger output v2 with shallow v1/v2 reader support, assurance report v2, compute ledger v1, and resolved schema unchecked. Exact-key readers fail on additions, no migration registry exists, and serializers are inconsistent (SemanticReview.to_dict omits schema_version).

Integrity is repeatedly conflated with authenticity/assurance. SHA-256 manifests, journal links, and claim IDs detect some accidental mutation but are all forgeable by a writer with run access; evidence.json itself has no trusted anchor. Reports should name self-consistency, provenance, authenticity, deterministic verification, semantic review, and mathematical acceptance separately.

TOCTOU/pathname risk spans the corpus. Verification, journal access, inspection, request receipt reads, output stat, and subsequent use are not under one stable snapshot; final-component symlink checks do not secure intermediate components; metrics permits arbitrary external paths.

V1 paid excessive compute primarily in journal append (full-file read/decode/hash plus repeated full-state snapshots, yielding quadratic growth), claim ledger evidence replication across every claim, repeated topological/property dictionary construction, repeated state/features reads in assurance, full-tree hashing on each verification, and silent reprocessing of all request/receipt files for each compute-ledger write. These are mostly deterministic I/O costs and should not consume agent-model budget.

Mathematical trust is compositional only in claims.py's DAG status propagation. Semantic review, Lean stage summaries, claims, receipts, and obligations are not bound by common declaration/target/source/toolchain digests, so passed components need not concern the same theorem.

Comments/docstrings exceed implementation in several places: 'immutable ledger' returns mutable containers; 'independently scheduled/cold verifier' and semantic 'independent comparison' are not proven; compute 'reproducible' includes generated_at and mutable external reads; compute 'without trusting model self-reporting' trusts unvalidated receipt values; journal 'authoritative' is bypassed by inspection; evidence 'atomic' is not a concurrent transaction.

Error handling is inconsistent: artifacts/journal generally fail closed, claims/semantic wrap configuration errors, inspection partially validates, and metrics silently drops corruption. V2 support records need typed error classes and explicit counts for missing, malformed, rejected, and unverifiable inputs.

No supplied module enforces campaign-wide run locking, ownership/permissions, resource quotas, schema migrations, signatures, or retention/compaction. No supplied tests establish crash safety, race safety, cross-platform behavior, or mathematical soundness.

Model expenditure should be isolated from deterministic work: hashing, parsing, DAG closure, Lean execution, accounting, and report derivation require no language model; Sol/human effort belongs only to theorem invention, informal proof review, and semantic equivalence, with independent provenance and deterministic gates.

failure_modes: atomic_write_text has last-writer-wins semantics and no lock/CAS; concurrent controller writes can silently replace one another.

Atomicity/durability depend on local filesystem semantics for os.replace/fsync; network filesystems, unsupported directory fsync, permissions, full disk, and platform-specific O_DIRECTORY behavior can fail.
mkstemp replacement normally changes an existing destination's mode/ownership semantics to those of the new temporary file (typically mode 0600), which may be an unintended interface change.

Evidence verification is TOCTOU-prone: is_file/is_symlink, hashing, tree enumeration, and later consumers do not share a lock or stable file descriptors. A file or intermediate symlink can be swapped during/after verification.

Final-component symlinks are rejected by verification, but digest_file opens by pathname without O_NOFOLLOW; an attacker racing the prior checks can redirect the read. Intermediate symlink components are not explicitly rejected and may escape run_dir.
digest_tree follows item.is_file() behavior and does not reject symlink files, unlike evidence verification; its artifact set can therefore include bytes reached through a symlink.

evidence.json is self-asserted and excluded from its own manifest. Anyone able to rewrite the run can rewrite both artifacts and hashes; there is no signature, trusted root digest, append-only anchor, or campaign-state identity binding.
Strict exact-key/schema checks make additive schema evolution fail closed but provide no migration path.
permitted_paths exemptions can be absent, stale, altered, or indexed with arbitrary metadata and still remain unverified; the return tuple deliberately omits them.

PurePosixPath normalizes repeated separators and '.' components before parts inspection, so the apparent checks for empty/'.' components do not reject every noncanonical spelling. Noncanonical indexed strings then usually fail set equality, but repair-path aliases can be accepted unexpectedly.
digest_file raises uncaught OSError/ValueError for unreadable files or a path outside relative_to; digest_tree can race file deletion/change.
No file-count, manifest-size, individual-size, or total-byte bound exists, enabling I/O/CPU denial of service.
utc_now has only second resolution, so it is not a uniqueness or ordering primitive.
interfaces: Artifact(path, sha256, size) frozen/slotted DTO; Artifact.to_dict().
utc_now() -> RFC3339-like UTC string at whole-second precision.

digest_file(path, relative_to=...) -> Artifact; digest_tree(root, exclude=...) -> tuple[Artifact,...].
verify_evidence_index(run_dir) -> verified non-permitted artifacts.
verify_evidence_for_repair(run_dir, permitted_paths=...) -> verified artifacts while exempting named controller-owned paths.

invariants: atomic_write_text writes UTF-8 with LF translation, flushes and fsyncs the temporary file, performs same-directory os.replace, then fsyncs the parent directory.
JSON output is deterministic for a given JSON-compatible value: ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, sorted keys, trailing newline.
Artifact digests are SHA-256 over bytes read in 1 MiB chunks; size is observed byte count; paths are POSIX-relative to relative_to.

Evidence verification requires exact top-level/artifact key sets, schema_version exactly equal to 1, nonempty string campaign_id/status/generated_at, unique indexed paths, regular non-symlink final artifacts, exact digest/size/path equality, and equality between indexed and expected retained file sets.
Expected evidence excludes evidence.json, .campaign.lock, and every file whose first relative component is exactly workspace.
Repair exemptions are explicit relative POSIX-style names and are removed from both digest verification and set-completeness comparison.
line_findings: Artifact.to_dict emits only path/sha256/size; no algorithm/version/media type is carried per artifact.
utc_now uses timespec='seconds' and replaces '+00:00' with 'Z'.
atomic_write_text creates the parent before mkstemp and always unlinks the temporary in finally; after successful replace that unlink is harmless because the old temporary pathname no longer exists.
os.replace is atomic only because mkstemp is placed in path.parent; this implementation detail is essential to the module claim.
_fsync_directory opens a directory read-only with O_DIRECTORY when available; portability is not handled here.
digest_tree's exclude is exact-string-only and does not automatically exclude evidence.json, lock files, or workspace.
verify_evidence_for_repair checks `not pure.parts`, while artifact-index path validation does not; an empty indexed path still fails later because run_dir is not a file.
The repair validator's `part in ('', '.', '..')` over PurePosixPath.parts overstates rejection of '' and '.' because PurePosixPath canonicalizes them.
Artifact metadata sha256 and size are not independently type/range/format checked; ordinary malformed values are rejected only by observed.to_dict() inequality.
Permitted receipts are skipped before filesystem checks, digest computation, and append to verified; permission is an integrity hole by design, not merely permission to rewrite after verification.
Expected-set logic excludes workspace only when `workspace` is the first component (`parts[:1]`), not whenever that name appears deeper.
The docstring says 'every regular file named' but implementation additionally enforces completeness of all retained non-workspace files.

failure_modes: fcntl makes the implementation POSIX-specific and locks are advisory; noncooperating writers can corrupt or replace the journal.
os.open follows symlinks and is path-based; there is no O_NOFOLLOW, directory containment check, ownership check, or regular-file check.
The unkeyed hash chain detects accidental edits relative to the retained bytes' parsed values but provides no authenticity: an actor with write access can regenerate the whole chain.

Every append reads, parses, canonicalizes/hashes, and retains every prior full snapshot. With growing state and N events this creates unbounded storage and approximately quadratic cumulative I/O/CPU; this is a major place v1 paid excessive deterministic compute.
A complete final JSON record lacking LF is discarded as 'truncated'; repair is based on delimiter presence, not whether the record is complete and valid.
load_state_snapshot is destructive recovery, not read-only inspection. It requires write permission and can silently truncate a tail while returning repaired_truncated_tail=True.

`created = not path.exists()` is a pre-open TOCTOU observation. It is not a reliable proof that this process created the directory entry, so conditional parent-directory fsync semantics are race-sensitive.
Schema and integer checks use equality rather than strict types: JSON true compares equal to integer 1, so schema_version=true and sequence=true can pass for record 1.
json.loads/json.dumps use Python's default acceptance/emission of NaN and Infinity; arbitrary nested state can therefore be non-interoperable JSON while still hash-valid.
Timestamp and reason are only checked as nonempty strings; whitespace-only reasons and arbitrary timestamp formats pass.
No maximum journal size, record size, nesting depth, state schema, or replay count exists; malformed/huge retained input can exhaust memory/CPU because _read_all loads the entire file.

A crash after creating the file but before a durable parent fsync, unusual filesystem fsync semantics, ENOSPC, or a short/erroring append can affect recovery. A partial append is repairable only when it leaves no trailing LF.
The lock protects the inode opened by cooperating processes, not pathname replacement by another actor; a replacement can split readers/writers across inodes.
Earlier snapshots are integrity-checked but no semantic transition/state-machine validity is checked, so a validly rehashed arbitrary state jump is accepted.
interfaces: JournalError(ValueError).
JournalState(state, sequence, repaired_truncated_tail) frozen/slotted DTO.
append_state_snapshot(run_dir, state, reason=...) -> next sequence.
load_state_snapshot(run_dir) -> JournalState; despite its name it takes an exclusive lock, opens read-write, and can truncate/fsync the file.
journal_path(run_dir) -> events.jsonl path.
On-disk events.jsonl records use exact schema_version,sequence,at,previous_sha256,kind,reason,state,sha256 keys; schema version 1 and kind state_snapshot.
invariants: Writers use fcntl.LOCK_EX over the entire read/verify/repair/append/fsync critical section.

Each complete record is valid JSON with an exact key set; line index equals sequence; previous_sha256 equals the prior observed digest; kind is state_snapshot; at/reason are nonempty strings; state is an object; sha256 equals SHA-256 of canonical JSON excluding sha256.
Appended records are compact canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys and a trailing LF.
A final byte fragment without LF is considered repairable and removed; any malformed complete newline-terminated record, sequence break, chain break, schema mismatch, or digest mismatch is fatal.
Each append stores a full state projection rather than a delta; load returns only the latest projection after verifying every prior record.
File descriptors are closed in finally; writes loop until all bytes are written; appended content is fsynced.
line_findings: append_state_snapshot calculates `created` before mkdir/open; mode 0o600 applies only when O_CREAT creates the file and does not repair permissions on an existing journal.
Both append and load request LOCK_EX; no nonmutating shared-lock load exists.
_decode sets valid_size to the byte after the last LF; if no LF exists, valid_size becomes 0.
The repair_truncated_tail parameter exists, but both public call sites always pass True; strict no-repair decoding is not externally exposed.
`value['sequence'] != index` and schema equality accept booleans due to Python equality semantics.
The chain digest is over parsed/canonicalized semantic content, not exact line bytes; alternate whitespace, key order, escapes, or CRLF can verify if the stored digest matches canonical content.
previous_sha256 receives no direct type/hex-length validation; chain equality indirectly constrains records after the first, while first must compare equal to None.
The latest state dict is returned directly from newly parsed JSON; JournalState is frozen but its nested dict is mutable.
If a truncated tail is removed during append, the truncation is not separately fsynced before appending, but the final fsync covers the resulting file state.
Parent directory fsync occurs only on the `created` branch; an already-retained file append does not require directory-entry durability but replacement attacks remain out of scope.
_read_all joins all 1 MiB chunks, doubling peak-memory pressure around parsing/canonicalization for large journals.
The module duplicates _fsync_directory rather than reusing artifacts.py, creating drift risk.

failure_modes: The ledger is described as immutable but is returned as ordinary mutable dict/list structures.

Verifier independence and mathematical correctness are only docstring claims; the module accepts handoff files and does not establish process/model separation, provenance, signatures, Lean checking, or semantic validity.

`_evidence_reference` uses `{'stage': stage, **reference}`; a supplied reference containing its own stage key overrides the map key, allowing provenance mislabeling. Runtime evidence/receipt structures are otherwise largely unvalidated.

Generic evidence is attached to every claim without coverage semantics. Receipt evidence is attached to every untargeted claim unconditionally and to targeted claims if an untyped covers_targets list contains the target.

When verifiers disagree and no adjudicator is supplied, any rejection governs but `verifier_disagreements` remains empty because disagreement records are appended only when an adjudication object exists. The audit trail underreports unresolved disagreements.
An adjudicator bundle is ignored for unanimous verifier votes, even if it contradicts them; this policy is implicit rather than schema-declared.

Content IDs are campaign-scoped rather than globally content-addressed. Alias is excluded, and duplicate structurally identical claims can receive the same claim_id; no claim-ID uniqueness check exists.
Digest canonicalization sorts predecessor IDs while the emitted predecessors list preserves declared dependency order, creating two order conventions for the same relation.
Claim IDs do not bind verdicts, verifier identities, evidence references, or ledger policy/version. Re-evaluation can retain claim IDs while changing acceptance.
required_targets and campaign_id are only type-annotated, not runtime-validated. Bad unhashable/nonstring values can produce TypeError or surprising mappings rather than ConfigurationError.
declared_targets is optional and partial; missing declarations are silently skipped and extra declarations are ignored. Thus 'frozen targets' are enforced only when callers provide matching entries.
Claims may target identifiers outside required_targets; rejection of such claims does not prevent closed=True unless they are dependencies of required claims.
Limitations/issues arrays allow duplicates and empty arrays; proof is mandatory even for source/computation/counterexample kinds, with no kind-specific schema.
No resource bounds exist for claim count, text/proof size, evidence replication, or graph size. Every claim repeats all generic evidence, potentially causing quadratic-sized ledgers.
Topological resolution repeatedly scans all unresolved nodes by layers; acceptable for small sets but avoidable O(V²)-like work on long chains.
Strict v1 handoffs and v2 ledger output create a multi-schema coupling that needs coordinated migration; inspection accepts ledger v1/v2 only superficially.

Claim IDs hash campaign_id, kind, statement, scope, proof, sorted predecessor content IDs, target, and ordered limitations; aliases and verifier/evidence results are excluded.

Status is rejected when governing verdict logic rejects; otherwise blocked if any dependency is not verified; otherwise verified. Required-target closure ignores nonrequired claims except through dependency propagation.
With verifier disagreement, an available adjudicator controls; without applicable adjudication, any reject vote rejects. Ledger status is verified iff every required target is verified.
line_findings: _object allows optional keys in its generic helper, but all current proposal/verdict root uses are exact-key.
_text strips leading/trailing whitespace; hashes and emitted statements therefore use stripped text, while interior whitespace remains identity-relevant.
_texts does not enforce uniqueness or nonempty cardinality.
ClaimProposalBundle.by_alias and ClaimVerdictBundle.by_claim allocate fresh dictionaries on every property access; build_claim_ledger repeats some allocations.
Target uniqueness excludes None as intended; several untargeted claims are allowed.
_topological_order resolves all currently ready aliases in lexicographic batches, making output deterministic independent of proposal input order where dependencies permit.
`predecessors: sorted(predecessor_ids)` in the digest makes dependency declaration order nonsemantic for identity.
Frozen declaration comparison covers only kind, statement, and scope; proof, limitations, and target alias are intentionally/unintentionally outside it.
`adjudication = ... if len(votes) > 1 else None` means an adjudicator never reviews unanimity.
A rejected claim stays rejected even if a dependency is rejected; blocked is assigned only after the claim itself passes governing verdicts.
Evidence references for `target is None` accept every receipt regardless of covers_targets.
closed is computed only from the required_targets projection, and ledger.status is derived solely from that boolean.
Produced ledger schema is 2 although both consumed handoff schemas are 1.

cross_cutting: Highest coupling: agent_runner and command independently implement the same launch/register/pump/poll/workspace-limit/timeout/terminate/unregister/secret-cleanup algorithm. They already import private helpers across the boundary yet diverge on deadline grace, signal handling, hashes, streaming, wait behavior, and error normalization.

Duplicated process identity logic: /proc stat parsing and _process_start_time exist in process_registry.py and processes.py; group liveness scans also recur. A single parsed /proc snapshot/identity service is needed.

Duplicated/overlapping registries: controller/Herdr records live at runtime root, child records at runtime/processes, units at runtime/units. Both registry families call themselves schema_version=1 but have incompatible envelopes, validation, corruption behavior, and lifecycles.

Duplicated state machines: runner receipt running/succeeded/failed/timed_out; per-invocation retry status; controller registration alive/dead; Herdr creation_label/workspace_id nullable two-phase state; unit registered/active/terminated/unregistered; process registered/group-alive/unregistered; campaign running/awaiting_approval/stopped; evidence status. Transitions are not represented by one transactional ledger and can disagree after crashes.

Schema/version risk: exact-key readers in runner request and both registries reject additive evolution. Registry scanners then silently ignore unsupported/corrupt records, turning version skew into lost cleanup. Receipt schema has v1 but no visible reader/migration; request has no version at all.

Trust coupling: registry records retain executable paths and run directories later used to execute systemctl/Herdr and mutate state/evidence. Security therefore depends on runtime directory ownership/modes and atomic writer behavior absent from this corpus.

Path coupling: workspace/run_dir/output/log/receipt/handoff semantics are spread among caller request construction, runner validation, sandbox containment, registries, shutdown, journal, and evidence. Only selected paths receive containment checks.

Cleanup ordering differs by path: units may be killed before process signaling; secret cleanup can override execution status; receipt can commit before heartbeat finish; global shutdown can terminate units before closing Herdr; campaign state may remain running on journal error.

Process safety is Linux-specific and mixes three mechanisms: start_new_session/killpg, systemd cgroups, and pidfd-per-member signaling. The fallback fails in the important leader-dead/descendants-alive case despite durable pgrp/session data.

Race/corruption theme: atomic replacement protects individual JSON writes but no registry-wide lock/generation protects read-modify-write, enumerate-then-act, verify-then-unlink, or stop-vs-register races. Invalid files are generally ignored or repeatedly reported, not quarantined.

Redaction semantics are inconsistent: agent_runner redacts streaming output before capture; command redacts only returned bounded text and changes digest meaning when secrets exist; workspace cleanup destructively scans after execution. No shared evidence/redaction contract exists.
Artifact freshness is not bound to attempts. Runner output/handoff may predate the receipt; retries share workspace; global evidence is regenerated separately from the state journal.

Excessive v1 compute: full workspace-size traversal every 250 ms in both supervisors; executable and recursive dependency-manifest hashing on every sandbox preparation and every retry; full secret scan after every invocation/retry; process-registry pruning with repeated full /proc group scans; pidfd group operations with repeated /proc scans; evidence exclusion traversal plus digest_tree; repeated Herdr list/new-client/close calls per registration.
Bounded-output implementation uses character counts, while filesystem/resource limits are bytes. Stream SHA semantics vary with redaction and truncation, weakening machine-verifiable provenance.

Comments/docstrings requiring qualification: 'durable' lacks directory fsync and runtime records are boot-scoped; 'complete process-group cleanup' is not guaranteed when threads outlive return or leader pidfd is gone; 'verify inactive' treats all nonzero is-active statuses as inactive; 'remove exact ownership records only after their full group is gone' is violated when leader PID reuse causes early unregister without checking old group.

No supplied file enforces or checks Lean compilation, theorem statements, proof soundness, or mathematical equivalence. Execution controls can support provenance, but mathematical campaign correctness is an external unknown.

failure_modes: Strict exact-key request parsing has no request schema_version and rejects additive v2 fields; malformed/unknown fields fail before a receipt is written.

run_dir, prompt, output, logs, and receipt need not be inside a trusted root. A trusted request producer is therefore assumed; otherwise arbitrary reads/writes and registry ownership claims are possible.

An existing output is not removed when the final invocation is blank or fails. The terminal receipt always names output, so stale output can survive and be mistaken for current output. Handoff availability similarly has no freshness/attempt binding.
The effective runner deadline and sandbox RuntimeMaxSec are max_time+60, but OMP is told max_time and timeout reporting says max_time; timeout semantics are inconsistent by up to 60 seconds.

A daemon pump thread is joined for only 10 seconds. If a descendant retains a pipe or interrupt/error bypasses normal joins, the thread can continue mutating capture lists and writing heartbeat output after _invoke returns.

RunnerInterrupted is re-raised after receipt finalization but is not caught by main, so the process normally emits a traceback/exits as an uncaught exception rather than preserving 128+signal_number as the CLI exit code.
heartbeat.finish is not in a finally block. Exceptions after heartbeat.start, including unexpected _invoke failures or artifact-write failures, can leave heartbeat lifecycle and receipt at running.

Atomic replacement fsyncs file contents but not the parent directory; crash durability of the rename is not guaranteed. Destination permissions become those of mkstemp (normally 0600), which may differ from replaced files.
Capture limits count Unicode code points, not encoded bytes, so persisted UTF-8 logs can exceed the claimed 1 MiB bound.
Retries reuse the same mutated workspace and same prompt with no rollback/idempotency token; side effects accumulate and can change later answers.
Combined logs concatenate retries without separators, while output contains only final invocation stdout; per-invocation receipt entries contain no output hashes or offsets, impairing attribution.
tools values may contain commas; joining with commas can alter OMP tool-list semantics even though shell injection is avoided.
Workspace-size breach and secret cleanup can overwrite an earlier exit code with 125/126. Cleanup errors are folded into strings, not represented as typed causes.
OSError/SandboxError after Popen sends signals but does not reliably wait or join pumps before returning; process-registry unregistration failure is ignored.
If execution is absent, the inherited environment is passed wholesale and secret discovery/redaction is disabled.
interfaces: CLI: dossier-agent-runner --request PATH; main returns 0 success, 1 completed non-success, 2 request/OS/type/value error; RunnerInterrupted currently escapes main.

Input JSON is an exact-key object. Required: role_id, attempt, omp, workspace, run_dir, prompt, output, stdout_log, stderr_log, receipt, tools, model, thinking, max_time. Optional: execution, handoff, empty_output_retries, sandbox_read_paths, workspace_executables.

Output receipt schema_version=1 with running and terminal forms; terminal fields include status, timestamps/duration, exit_code, output/log paths, handoff_available, truncation flags, error, and per-invocation sandbox metadata.
Filesystem outputs: receipt, stdout_log, stderr_log, and output when the final invocation has nonblank stdout; writes use temporary file + fsync(file) + os.replace.

Subprocess contract: OMP receives --mode=text --print --no-session --auto-approve --max-time, --cwd, tool/model/thinking options, and @PROMPT.
invariants: role_id and omp are nonempty strings; attempt>=1; max_time>=30; empty_output_retries in [0,3]; tools are nonempty strings; model/thinking are null or nonempty strings.
All path strings are expanded and resolved; only handoff is required to lie inside workspace. Handoff availability additionally requires a regular non-symlink file.
Child is started with stdin closed, UTF-8 replacement decoding, separate stdout/stderr pipes, and start_new_session=True; registration verifies new-session identity.
Captured stdout and stderr are each intended to be bounded at _MAX_CAPTURE=1,048,576 Python characters, while pane output is streamed without that bound.
Secrets selected by ExecutionSpec.secret_environment are redacted across stream chunk boundaries before pane output, retained output, logs, output artifact, and returned errors.

A sandbox unit is registered before Popen and a child process is registered immediately after Popen; cleanup attempts unit termination/unregistration, process unregistration, signal-handler restoration, and secret-bearing-file removal.
Success requires exit_code==0 and nonblank stdout. Exit 124 or stderr containing 'deadline exceeded' maps to timed_out; blank exit-0 may be retried.
No Lean proof or mathematical validity invariant is enforced here; this layer only preserves execution/provenance artifacts on which later mathematical review may depend.
line_findings: Module claim 'durable output and receipt capture' is only partially implemented: file data is fsynced, but containing directories are not fsynced and receipt can remain running after unexpected exceptions.
_request compares exact key sets but does not validate schema_version; this is a brittle implicit schema.
_path.resolve follows existing symlinks, but only handoff receives containment validation; the other resolved paths remain unrestricted capabilities.
_StreamingRedactor orders secrets as supplied; secret_values supplies longest first, which matters for overlapping values but is not guaranteed by the class interface itself.
_pump closes source streams and sends all redacted text to heartbeat.write; only in-memory capture is bounded, not terminal output.
_retain_and_write prefixes every streamed chunk, but callers pass an empty prefix for both streams, so merged pane presentation has no stdout/stderr attribution.
_invoke initializes sandbox metadata as backend='preparation-failed' whenever execution exists, even when execution.sandbox is false; prepare_sandbox later replaces it in normal paths.
Signal handlers are installed only on the main thread and raise a Python exception directly from the handler.

Sandbox units are durably registered before the systemd-run wrapper is launched, closing one crash window; process registration necessarily occurs after Popen, leaving a smaller unregistered-child crash window.
On normal non-unit child exit, TERM then KILL are sent to the entire group before wait to remove descendants. Unit-backed cleanup is deferred to terminate_sandbox in finally.
Workspace usage is rescanned recursively every 250 ms and once after exit; _observed is discarded, so expensive measurements do not become evidence.
The local deadline is max_time+60 and prepare_sandbox receives the same extension, while status text later claims max_time.
Interrupt handling records interrupted_signal in sandbox metadata and receipt, then execute raises after heartbeat.finish; main does not translate it.
remove_secret_bearing_files runs in finally on every invocation, including each blank-output retry, and can destructively alter the shared workspace before the next retry.
_bounded_capture applies another aggregate cap over already per-invocation-capped captures; earlier retries can consume the entire final log budget and hide the last attempt.
deadline_exceeded trusts a free-text stderr substring even with a non-timeout exit, coupling status to OMP wording.
blank_success requires the exact error string built immediately above; this is a duplicated, string-coupled state predicate.
The running receipt is updated only between blank retries, not during a long invocation; liveness is externalized solely through PaneHeartbeat.
output is written only when final_stdout is nonblank and is never unlinked otherwise.
handoff_available rejects symlinks but does not prove the handoff was created by this attempt or remained unchanged after the check.
The final receipt is committed before heartbeat.finish; a heartbeat failure can leave a terminal receipt even though execute raises.
main catches OSError/TypeError/ValueError only; SandboxError is a RuntimeError and unexpected cleanup failures can escape with traceback.

failure_modes: This duplicates agent_runner's supervisor with materially different semantics: timeout grace, error codes, signal handling, streaming, hashes, cleanup placement, and retry behavior can drift.
If Popen succeeds but an OSError/SandboxError occurs later, signals are sent but process.wait and pump-thread joins are not guaranteed before return.
The normal pump joins time out after 10 seconds; daemon threads can survive and mutate capture/digest state concurrently with result construction.
Capture limits are characters rather than bytes.

Digest semantics change when secrets exist: without secrets, hashes cover the full stream; with secrets, hashes are recomputed over only the redacted bounded capture. Thus the same fields alternately mean full-stream digest and truncated-output digest.
Post-capture redaction cannot preserve a full-stream redacted digest and stores the original full digest only transiently; truncation plus secret policy makes evidence incomparable.
OSError/SandboxError can return exit_code=None rather than a normalized typed launch failure, forcing callers to interpret both error and exit_code.
Secret-bearing cleanup is inside the main try path; paths that fail before reaching it do not run the scan, and cleanup itself can raise uncaught filesystem errors.
On unit-backed timeout terminate_sandbox performs immediate SIGKILL/stop, while non-unit timeout attempts graceful TERM; policy differs by backend.
Workspace scans every 250 ms are O(tree size) and can dominate short or filesystem-heavy commands.
Private Linux waitid flags and /proc-dependent registration make the API nonportable despite no platform guard.
Process and unit unregister return values are mostly ignored; surviving ownership records are silently retained and caller receives no structured indication.
The function does not validate timeout>0 before computing the deadline; sandbox preparation rejects nonpositive runtime, but unsandboxed execution can time out immediately with surprising behavior.
Secret redaction uses exact replacement; short/common configured values can corrupt outputs and trigger destructive cleanup elsewhere.
interfaces: Public Python API run_captured_command(argv, cwd, env, timeout, execution=None, workspace=None, allow_workspace_executables=False, run_dir=None, read_paths=()) -> CapturedCommand.
