Consumes ExecutionSpec, process_registry registrations, and sandbox preparation/termination/redaction/secret scanning.
invariants: Commands are invoked without a shell, with stdin DEVNULL, UTF-8 replacement decoding, separate pipes, and a new session.
Each retained stream is capped at 1,048,576 Python characters; SHA-256 normally covers the full decoded stream as re-encoded UTF-8.
Timeout maps to exit_code 124; workspace overage maps to 125; detected secret-bearing files map to 126.
When workspace is provided, the new-session process is registered under run_dir or workspace.parent; unit-backed sandbox execution requires run_dir.
A sandbox transient unit is registered before Popen and is unregistered only after verified termination.
Without a sandbox unit, normal completion and timeout explicitly signal the process group; timeout gives non-unit groups up to 10 seconds after SIGTERM before SIGKILL.
Returned captured text and errors are redacted for configured secret values.
No mathematical correctness is checked; digest/provenance integrity is the only relevance to downstream Lean evidence.
line_findings: _BoundedCapture.append sets truncated whenever len(chunk)>remaining; this still works when remaining is negative, but size is never advanced after the cap and the unit remains characters.
The stream digest receives decoded text re-encoded as UTF-8, not original child bytes; invalid UTF-8 is replaced, so the hash is not a byte-for-byte process-output hash.
_process_exited_without_reaping treats ChildProcessError as exited, potentially masking an externally reaped child.
Normal completion deliberately sends TERM and KILL to a non-unit group even after the leader has exited, to reap descendants that inherited the session.
prepare_sandbox receives runtime_max_seconds=timeout, unlike agent_runner's max_time+60.
Registration only occurs when workspace is not None; Herdr calls therefore have no durable child ownership record.
release_registered_unit leaves the durable registration in place when termination fails, supporting later recovery.
Workspace-limit cleanup records only terminate_sandbox's result; direct SIGKILL then wait is still attempted.
After the loop, a final workspace scan can convert an otherwise successful command to exit 125.
remove_secret_bearing_files can convert any outcome to 126 and replaces, rather than appends to, an existing non-cleanup error at that point.
The OSError/SandboxError handler formats raw exception text without the 'cannot execute' normalization used by agent_runner.
The BaseException path performs more registry cleanup than the ordinary caught-exception path, but can replace the original exception with SandboxError when cleanup fails.
Returned sandbox metadata is invocation.metadata directly, unlike agent_runner which copies and augments it.

When redactions are configured, stdout_sha256/stderr_sha256 hash redacted retained captures; when none are configured, they hash full decoded streams. This is the highest-risk non-obvious schema ambiguity.

failure_modes: All listing/discovery functions silently skip malformed, unsupported-version, unreadable, or misnamed files. Corruption therefore becomes an unreported orphan process/unit and persists indefinitely.
Strict exact-key schemas have no migration path; deploying a new writer can make old recovery code ignore all new records.
Runtime-root security depends on environment selection, directory permissions, and atomic_write_json behavior not shown. There is no explicit anti-symlink open or ownership/mode validation here.
Read-verify-unlink is not compare-and-delete: another writer can replace the same path after verification and before unlink, allowing a fresh same-key record to be removed.
No locks coordinate registration, pruning, enumeration, or unregistration.
register_run_process has an unavoidable Popen-to-record crash window; unit registration closes the analogous pre-launch window.
_prune_dead_process_registrations scans every record and can scan all of /proc for each one, producing O(records*processes) work on every process registration.
PID start time is a Linux boot-relative tick string; records surviving reboot could collide in principle unless the runtime directory is boot-scoped as assumed.
A unit record stores and later trusts an executable path for systemctl. Registry tampering can redirect shutdown execution.
unregister_run_process can return false after a one-second caller wait while descendants still exist; callers commonly ignore the result.
remove_dead_run_registrations accepts an alive callback but discards it, a compatibility trap for consumers expecting injected liveness semantics.
Unit path is keyed only by random unit name; collision overwrites an existing ownership record.
Invalid files are never quarantined or removed, causing repeated scan cost and invisible loss of recovery coverage.
interfaces: Environment interface CAMPAIGN_BUILDER_RUNTIME_DIR; fallback XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or tempfile/campaign-builder-UID.
Public dataclasses RegisteredRunUnit and RegisteredRunProcess.
Public unit API: register_run_unit, registered_run_units, unregister_run_unit.
Public process API: register_run_process, unregister_run_process, registered_run_processes.
Discovery/legacy API: registered_run_directories, remove_dead_run_registrations(run_dir, alive).
Consumed by agent_runner.py, command.py, and processes.py; atomic JSON writer imported from artifacts.
invariants: Unit names must match campaign-<digits>-<12 lowercase hex>.service and are addressed by SHA-256(unit).
Unit records require an absolute canonical run_dir and absolute canonical systemctl path; exact schema key sets and schema_version=1 are enforced on read.
Process records bind canonical run_dir, positive PID, /proc start time, process-group ID, and session ID; a registered child must own a new session with pid==pgrp==sid.
Process record filenames hash all identity fields and include the PID; valid records must reside at their recomputed canonical path.
Unregistering a process removes only an exactly equal retained record and only after PID identity changed or no non-zombie member remains in the recorded pgrp/session.
Failure to enumerate /proc is conservative: a group is treated as alive and its record is retained.
Records are written atomically; invalid/misnamed records are excluded from discovery.
These are runtime crash-recovery records, not mathematical proof artifacts and not truly durable across runtime-directory cleanup or reboot.
line_findings: The module docstring's 'durable' means atomically retained in a runtime directory, not persistence across reboot.
_directory appends 'processes' to CAMPAIGN_BUILDER_RUNTIME_DIR, whereas processes.py stores controller registrations directly at that root and units in a sibling directory.
_unit_path uses a full SHA-256 digest, but unit format itself already has high-entropy random identity.
Path(systemctl).resolve() is always absolute, making the subsequent is_absolute check effectively redundant.
registered_run_units validates both record content and canonical filename; malformed/misplaced records are silently invisible.
The /proc stat indexing is correct after stripping '(comm)': state=0, ppid=1, pgrp=2, session=3, starttime=19.
_prune_dead_process_registrations calls unregister_run_process on every valid canonical process record, including live records; liveness prevents deletion but incurs full scans.
register_run_process samples start time twice around getpgid/getsid to detect PID identity change.
_owned_group_is_alive treats any non-zombie process sharing both pgrp and session as ownership continuation even if the original leader is gone.

unregister_run_process deletes immediately if the PID now has a different start time, without first checking whether old descendants still occupy the recorded group; this can lose recovery ownership for a leader PID that was reused while descendants survive.
registered_run_directories merges process and unit identities, allowing process-only orphan runs to be found by global shutdown.
remove_dead_run_registrations explicitly executes 'del alive'; the docstring claim is narrower than the signature's apparent injectable behavior.

Preserve exact PID/start/pgrp/session identity and pre-launch unit intent, but place all controller/unit/process records in one authenticated/permission-checked registry namespace with a shared envelope schema, boot ID, record kind, generation/nonce, lifecycle state, corruption quarantine, migration readers, and lock or compare-and-delete semantics. failure_modes: This is a second, incompatible registry schema in the same runtime tree as process_registry. Both use schema_version=1 but different exact fields, paths, validation, and lifecycle state.
Controller records can contain process_start_time=None; such controllers are not signaled by stop_all and are later eligible for deletion, weakening ownership after /proc read failure.
Registration updates are unlocked read-modify-replace operations; concurrent creation/id/clear updates can lose fields or resurrect stale state.

Registry values are trusted as control capabilities. A tampered herdr_executable can be executed; a tampered run_dir can cause lock creation, state/journal writes, evidence regeneration, and workspace process targeting in an arbitrary directory.
_read_registration requires only nonempty, not absolute, run_dir and allows empty workspace IDs/labels. Consumers resolve paths later.

Fallback orphan discovery kills any adopted process with cwd under run_dir/workspace, which can include an unrelated daemon if workspace ownership is not exclusive; non-adopted unregistered descendants are missed.

Group termination requires a live pidfd for the original leader. If the leader is gone but descendants survive in the recorded group, the target becomes unresolved and descendants are not signaled even though group membership can be enumerated.
If the leader exits during group signaling, descriptor_alive fails and remaining members may be left unresolved.
Reports use target leader PIDs, not all signaled member PIDs; terminated/killed semantics therefore do not describe actual group members.

_registered_process_survives can return false and unregister a record when the leader PID has been reused with a different start time, without checking whether the original pgrp/session still has descendants.
Global shutdown races registration creation/update/removal and Herdr workspace creation. It can miss a new record, delete a replacement at the same path, or mark stopped while a controller proceeds.
Malformed controller records generate errors but are not quarantined or removed; malformed child/unit records from process_registry are silently absent.
Herdr discovery/close calls are sequential, each with its own timeout and no global shutdown deadline; many records can make stop_all unbounded in aggregate.
Creation-label discovery is repeated per registration, and clients/list calls are not cached; duplicate registrations can close the same workspace repeatedly.
_mark_stopped silently returns on journal/state read failure, so shutdown can succeed operationally while retained campaign state remains running.
Evidence regeneration can recursively digest a large run after shutdown; its cost and failure atomicity are not bounded here.
Only run directories from controller registrations are marked stopped. Runs discovered solely from child/unit registrations are terminated but not state-updated.
stop_all terminates registered units before Herdr closure and controller termination; partial ordering is not represented as a recoverable transaction.
Controller registration cleanup and child-record cleanup ignore some unlink/unregister races; stale or missing records are expected but not surfaced consistently.
StopReport.workspaces_closed is sorted but not deduplicated, so repeated registration can produce duplicate IDs.

Workspace creation uses a two-phase nullable state: herdr_creation_label records intent before/while creation; herdr_workspace_id records the resulting workspace. Stop can discover IDs by label.
Shutdown excludes its own PID and ancestors from fallback process targeting.
Registered child groups are targeted by exact process start/pgrp/session identity; unregistered fallback targets require ppid==1 and cwd equal to or below run_dir/workspace.
pidfd identity is revalidated against /proc start time before signaling; group members are individually opened and signaled by pidfd.
Shutdown sends SIGTERM, waits terminate_timeout, then SIGKILL and waits again.
Run-state mutation is guarded by .campaign.lock opened O_NOFOLLOW and flock(LOCK_EX); running/awaiting_approval become stopped with timestamp/error.
Herdr workspace closure status can be recorded as herdr_closed even for already-terminal campaign state.
No Lean theorem validity is assessed; evidence regeneration only digests artifacts and reports campaign status.
line_findings: _registration_path hashes the string form of process_start_time, including None; register_campaign does not reject unavailable identity.
_owned_registration_path scans all controller JSON and insists on exactly one current PID/start match; duplicates turn ordinary updates into RuntimeError.
Workspace creation and workspace ID occupy independent fields rather than an explicit state enum, so both can be non-null.
_process_arguments is unused and should not be carried forward without a demonstrated consumer.
_ancestors excludes parents but not arbitrary sibling control processes.
registered_workspaces/intents deduplicate pairs with sets, but stop_all processes every registration rather than using these helpers.
Fallback _run_processes only selects ppid==1, showing it is specifically orphan recovery rather than general workspace process discovery.
_ProcessTarget optionally carries group identity; RegisteredRunProcess structurally always carries it, making several None checks dead or generic-only branches.
In _terminate, ProcessLookupError produces no handle; a group target then becomes unresolved, while a PID-only target is simply treated as absent.
Group send opens pidfds for every current member rather than killpg, reducing PID reuse risk but requiring repeated O(/proc) scans.
terminated_pids is computed as every target key not classified survivor, so never-started/already-dead targets count as terminated.
_registered_process_survives contains a process_group_id is None branch that is unreachable for RegisteredRunProcess under its dataclass definition.
terminate_run_processes also prunes dead controller registration files for the run, coupling per-run child shutdown to campaign-controller registry maintenance.
_mark_stopped uses a secure O_NOFOLLOW lock open, but the trustworthiness of run_dir itself comes entirely from registrations/caller.

Creation intent is considered successfully discovered if list_workspaces succeeds, even when no matching workspace exists.

failure_modes: Security relies on systemd user manager, bubblewrap, kernel namespaces, mount behavior, and policy correctness; no startup capability probe or fallback policy is shown.
terminate_sandbox_unit treats every nonzero 'systemctl is-active' result as inactive, including permission, transport, or command errors; it can falsely report verified termination.
The retained systemctl path is executable control-plane data. Registry tampering can cause arbitrary execution during cleanup unless registry permissions are guaranteed.
Workspace limits are polling-based, so a process can exceed the limit between 250 ms caller scans; scans are full-tree and expensive. cgroup/FSIZE limits do not cap aggregate workspace growth.
workspace_size_exceeds counts logical bytes and entries, double-counts hardlinks, ignores sparse allocation, and mutates directory permissions on PermissionError.
_scandir_entries adds owner read/write/execute permissions permanently and without restoring prior mode; both size checks and secret scans can alter agent artifacts.
Secret cleanup is destructive and substring-based. Short/common secrets can remove unrelated files or whole directories; PermissionError while reading a file is treated as secret presence.

Secret cleanup has TOCTOU races between no-follow enumeration, later path.open/unlink/rmtree, and concurrent workspace mutation. A path swapped to a symlink can make content reads follow outside workspace.
Secret cleanup covers regular files, symlinks, and directory names but not special files, xattrs, process memory, or already-exfiltrated network data.
Removal errors other than selected FileNotFound/Permission cases propagate and can replace execution outcomes.
Environment metadata excludes secret values from its hash, but secret variable names and all allowed names remain exposed.
Exact string redaction provides no encoding/escaping variants and can over-redact; secret_values imposes no minimum length/entropy.

Toolchain metadata recursively walks the workspace and fully hashes every recognized manifest on every prepare_sandbox call; large or rapidly changing trees can cause high latency and inconsistent snapshots.
Executable hashing fully reads the binary every invocation/retry and lacks caching by inode/mtime/content store.
_resolve_executable uses absolute rather than resolve for the initial path and is_file follows symlinks; later checks reconcile lexical/resolved placement, but path races remain.
External read paths are handled lexically for dedup/binding. Symlink targets and bwrap's bind semantics need explicit threat-model tests.
No explicit seccomp profile, capability drop, read-only workspace option, device minimization beyond --dev, or denial of special filesystem creation is specified.
LimitNPROC is computed from a race-prone full scan of all current-user threads and can be expensive; TasksMax is the clearer cgroup limit.
The fixed /bin,/sbin,/lib,/lib64 symlink assumptions can fail on non-merged or unusual distributions.
Metadata can disclose host executable paths, allowed executable directories, workspace path, manifest names/sizes, and policy details; this may be acceptable evidence but is a privacy boundary.

Unit identity includes the supervisor PID and 48 random bits and matches process_registry's unit regex.
RuntimeMaxSec is ceil'd and at least one second; callers independently enforce their own deadlines.
TasksMax adds a fixed overhead of eight; LimitNPROC adds current user task count plus requested tasks and overhead.
NoExecPaths=/ with quoted ExecPaths is a systemd-level executable allowlist independent of bubblewrap visibility.

No supplied file measures an agent, autonomy, pass rate, repeatability, evidence use, task completion, policy behavior, or false-positive/false-negative classification.

What documentation/prompts imply but code does not calibrate: full Euclidean chain and maximality; first-principles geometric derivation and method independence; global real proof/equality exhaustiveness; cubic negative/zero coverage, factorization narrative, coprime composition, and independent residue proof; exact blocked/unsolved agent output; citations; retained artifacts; unchanged Lean statements; lake build; placeholder/new-axiom scans on submissions; exact build logs; missing-source continue/checkpoint semantics.

False-closure defenses present in contracts: independence check before elimination; two-witness ambiguity proofs; explicit no-interpolation/no-guess rules; small-counterexample preflight; denominator-sign audit; prohibition on reporting refutation as successful proof. Only the canonical witnesses are statically checked; none of these defenses is evaluated against model outputs.

Taxonomy drift: blocked means unavailable retained source; unsolved covers complete-but-underdetermined and conclusively false claims. V2 needs at least solved, blocked_missing_evidence, underdetermined, refuted, verifier_error, budget_exhausted, and genuinely_unknown. Otherwise a counterexample is mislabeled as lack of solution.

Policy drift: missing-table-entry is continue in benchmark.toml and checkpoint in focused-benchmark.toml. This may be intentional suite behavior, but no override provenance or transition test distinguishes design from drift.

Security/trust boundary: every project sets sandbox=false and grants bash/eval/read/write/edit. Validation answer keys live under the benchmark root. Unless the external runner stages only declared inputs and evidence, "blind" cases permit direct answer retrieval, arbitrary filesystem/process access, mutation of fixtures, and possibly network access.

Hidden Python coupling: TOML requires Python 3.11 tomllib; exact oracle semantics use unbounded ints, Fraction, Python modulo, math.gcd, dict duplicate collapse, pathlib layout, subprocess behavior, assert optimization semantics, and exact Lean stdout text. The benchmark contract is therefore partly Python implementation behavior rather than declared schema.

Uniform regime coupling: all cases inherit identical 4-task/2-parallel/16-attempt/high-invention/high-audit/7200-second role budgets, including trivial deterministic cases. Results cannot isolate model capability from oversized orchestration; no effective budget consumption is recorded.

Evidence gating is documentary, not enforced: references are prose files with no hashes, provenance, allowlist, citation IDs, or closed-world machine flag. Broad read/bash access can bypass the intended retained-source boundary.

Coverage gaps: no malformed manifests, duplicate IDs, project-ID mismatch, missing files/directories, invalid status/policy, symlink traversal, path escape, tool denial, network denial, timeout/restart accounting, checkpoint resume, write confinement, answer-key leakage, citation correctness, adversarial prompt injection in sources, contradictory sources, stale toolchain, nondeterministic runs, alternate valid proofs, verifier disagreement, or Python -O CI test.

Benchmark difficulty is heavily signposted: blocked records explicitly say unavailable; false claims explicitly request counterexample/sign/small-case audits; references often state the diagnosis. There are no supplied run artifacts despite runs/runs_dir fields. Consequently expected outcomes are fixture intent, not empirically calibrated thresholds or observed behavior.

The main false-closure vulnerability is semantic overclaim by receipt: a Python nonempty-file assertion is declared to cover a theorem target. A controller that trusts `covers_targets` can close `fixture_goal` without checking the premise text or theorem entailment.

A second false-closure vulnerability is mutable shared state: proposer and verifier both have write access, input and handoffs appear run-local, and no immutable/content-addressed snapshots are shown. Verification can be valid for one version while closure consumes another.

A third false-closure vulnerability is provenance-by-path rather than provenance-by-digest. `input.txt`, proposal JSON, verdict JSON, prompts, and source files are all path-bound with no hashes, signatures, attempt IDs, or temporal binding.

The claim-ledger fixture calibrates no mathematical or verifier performance. It encodes one trivial entailment and one nonempty-file command. Titles and config imply “cold,” “independent,” “symbolic,” “replayable,” and target coverage, but no measurements or controls substantiate those properties.

The minimal problem/source pair has a coverage mismatch: requested outputs are domain, `A=s²`, zero case, and positive case; the sole source supports only nonnegativity. V2 must either admit trusted mathematical background explicitly, augment the source, or narrow acceptance.

Both examples rely on schema/version labels whose actual schemas, migration policies, enum semantics, and unknown-field behavior are absent. Handoff validity and closure semantics therefore cannot be audited to completion.

cross_cutting: No benchmark files are supplied in group=prompts. Therefore nothing here is empirically calibrated. The prompts imply quality on closure accuracy, planning efficiency, research necessity, source integrity, and strategy allocation, but provide no datasets, baselines, confidence intervals, thresholds, inter-rater agreement, or measured failure rates.

The strongest false-closure defenses are: primary-deliverable fidelity; diagnostic/fallback non-substitution; agreement/confidence rejection; independent success validation; complete frozen-obligation accounting; epistemic-class separation; downstream audit before promotion; limitation persistence; and treating solved labels as evidence rather than proof. Most are prompt-only and can still be self-attested.

False-closure coverage gaps: no controller-verifiable primary-deliverable predicate; no contract-invalid state; no proof that cited artifacts entail claims; no artifact hashes/locators; no audit independence definition; no anti-collusion policy; no mandatory external validator record in outcome; no treatment of rejected necessary obligations; no report/JSON conflict rule; no stale-evidence defense; and no calibrated adversarial corpus.

All prompts rely on hidden controller state: exact paths, run namespace, frozen plan, obligation ledger, task statuses, task classes, available strategies, capability catalog, tool catalog, resource ceilings, research authorization, reference roots, accepted-knowledge index, and operator policy. None define a versioned input envelope, so prompt/schema evolution can silently break joins.

The architecture is evidence-gated in prose but artifact-granular rather than claim-granular. Evidence arrays are strings; they lack claim IDs, artifact digests, exact locators, producer, checker, checker result, epistemic class, and acceptance predicate.

Python coupling is indirect but material: exact JSON dict/list/null/boolean conventions, regex validation, DAG/transitive-descendant checks, path handling, filesystem writes, CLI versus Python API tool binding, TensorFlow availability, ordered/random split policy, and likely dataclass/Pydantic consumers. Prompts should not encode Python-specific capability invocation or rely on Python truthiness/set behavior; use language-neutral JSON Schema and typed protocol definitions.

The planner explicitly mentions Python API via eval and TensorFlow; this expands arbitrary-code and dependency trust boundaries. API execution must be a sandboxed capability with typed arguments/results, not model-authored Python source.

Filesystem trust is central in final_reporter and researcher. Prompt constraints do not prevent traversal, symlink escape, stale files, partial writes, mutation, or untrusted active content. Artifact stores need immutable content addressing and atomic manifests.

Natural-language fields that become executable contracts are high risk: planner tasks[].instructions, final_reporter strategies[].next_prompt, and optimizer campaign_directive. They can carry prompt injection or mutate the immutable target. v2 should generate executable prompts from controller-owned templates plus typed, escaped data.

Schema versions drift independently: final outcome v2, planner v3, optimizer/research gate/researcher v1. No compatibility matrix or migration behavior is specified. 'v2 design' should version the whole protocol bundle, not infer compatibility from per-file integers.

Status vocabulary drifts: final reporter solved|unsolved|blocked; optimizer continue plus unrepresentable checkpoint; researcher complete|limited; research gate research|skip; task failure continue|abort|replan|restart. These are different state machines but lack a typed composition model.

'Independent' appears in final reporting, optimization, and planning but has no common definition. v2 must define independence dimensions: distinct task instance, model/session, context isolation, method/code/data provenance, no origin output except claim/evidence under audit, and conflict-of-interest/correlation declarations.

Obligation IDs are the closest thing to stable theorem contracts, but planner schema omits necessity/polarity/verifier and downstream prompts serialize them as strings or free disposition records. The obligation ledger should be the canonical cross-campaign unit.

Research source trust and mathematical evidence trust are conflated. A source can establish attribution/known results but usually does not prove the campaign-specific derivation; source identity, quoted claim, and mathematical verification need separate edges.

Model tiering is described only in planner reasoning classes. v2 should separate semantic model work from deterministic checks: models decompose, derive, assess relevance, and adversarially audit; code validates schemas, paths, hashes, DAGs, budgets, foreign keys, cardinalities, status conditionals, and tool policies.

failure_modes: The README is a claim about implementation, not proof of implementation. No source, tests, schemas, manifests, run bundles, receipts, benchmark reports, or certificates were supplied, so none of the advertised fail-closed behavior is actually verified here.

The phrase `exact statement/type` is underspecified: byte equality, normalized syntax, pretty-printed Lean expression, or kernel expression equality have different drift and spoofing properties. V2 must name the canonical representation and elaboration environment.

Content IDs include free-text proof and limitations, making semantically equivalent claims hash differently; this is acceptable for immutable provenance but not a mathematical equivalence key. Campaign inclusion also prevents cross-campaign deduplication unless a second campaign-independent semantic ID exists.

`Separately scheduled`, `cold`, `model-diverse`, and `distinct adjudicator` do not establish independence unless prompts, context, provider/model IDs, seeds, tool access, and shared prior outputs are explicitly controlled and retained.

Requiring every verifier to decide every claim causes availability failure and can reward shallow blanket decisions. Abstain/unsupported semantics, verifier timeouts, quorum policy, lane applicability, and adjudication precedence are not specified here.
Rejecting an accept verdict with a critical error/gap is necessary but insufficient: severity assignment is model-controlled unless deterministic finding codes and controller rules exist.

Command receipts can prove a command ran over named bytes, not that the command is sound. Controller-authored helpers, compilers, kernels, dependency resolution, OS, and executable provenance remain in the trusted computing base.

Environment fingerprints omit secret values by design. Trusted unsandboxed commands can therefore change behavior with a changed secret without replay detecting semantic drift unless a nonreversible keyed identifier or explicit `nonreplayable` status is used.

The statement that secrets are removed from workspace files before retention is algorithmically vague and cannot guarantee removal from encoded, transformed, compressed, model, database, or binary artifacts. README correctly notes exfiltration risk for untrusted code but still risks overclaiming trusted cleanup.

`allowed_executable_paths` is additive while all `/usr` binaries remain executable. This is not a strict executable allowlist; safety depends on tool invocation controls, mounted paths, namespace policy, and absence of interpreters capable of abusing writable inputs.
Agent stages default workspace executability to true for an OMP native add-on, materially widening code-execution risk. The README does not define integrity verification for that extracted add-on.

Serial stage execution prevents concurrent workspace races but does not prevent background-process mutation after stage return; identity registration/process-tree teardown must be comprehensive and tested across daemonization and namespace escape attempts.

`sandbox=false` hosted benchmark cases are called blind although agents with command access may inspect host paths, repository certificates, suite expectations, credentials, or prior reports. The README explicitly disclaims a hostile-agent confidentiality boundary; therefore these cases measure cooperative withholding, not secure blindness.

Benchmark calibration is only asserted: 12 declared cases (4 exact derivations, 3 Lean repairs, 3 underdetermined tasks, 2 false-closure traps). No observed outcomes, run repetitions, model/backend/version matrix, confidence intervals, resource distributions, or certificate validation output were supplied. Actual calibration established by supplied files: none.

A suite requiring exact outcome equality can hide taxonomy ambiguity: expected `unsolved`, `blocked`, `checkpoint`, `budget_exhausted`, and `case error` semantics are not all shown in the suite example. False closure is named but its computation is not defined in this file.

Atomic checkpointing and hash chains detect many mutations but do not by themselves prevent rollback to an older valid prefix. An external session anchor, monotonic trusted counter, signed checkpoint, or explicitly accepted rollback model is not described.

`evidence.json` covering every retained non-workspace file while replay adds a receipt creates a self-reference/update problem unless index generations, excluded roots, or Merkle conventions are precisely specified.

Resume may truncate an incomplete final journal record, but the criterion separating torn append from adversarial truncation is not documented. Durable-prefix corruption fails closed, yet old-prefix rollback remains an open boundary.
Workspace checkpointing cannot reverse external side effects from unsandboxed commands; README delegates that responsibility, so deterministic recovery is conditional rather than global.

Publication rollback claims cover interrupted swaps and preserved directories but do not state filesystem constraints, cross-device rename behavior, symlink/hardlink handling, permissions, ACLs, xattrs, concurrent destination writers, or Windows behavior.

`materially new method`, `publication research necessary`, `critical source`, `successful work`, `equivalent`, `novelty`, and `expected new evidence` are expensive ambiguous judgments. If left as unconstrained prose, retries and promotion are nondeterministic.

The capped pilot says descendants require an optional audit continuation gate; `optional` is ambiguous between an optionally present gate and a gate whose decision is optional. A missing gate must not accidentally authorize descendants.

The planner must use/skip regression capabilities based partly on numeric-file eligibility. Mere file extension/shape can trigger irrelevant planning pressure, and explicit use/skip for every capability creates schema churn as plugins grow.

Formal acceptance compiles the immutable contract, loads it via controller-authored Lean code, queries `Lean.collectAxioms`, requires exact declarations/types, and enforces allowed axioms. Formal compilation and semantic equivalence are independent gates.

Main assessment must dispose every frozen obligation and emit exactly solved, unsolved, or blocked; knowledge promotion requires successful work plus successful downstream audit.

Regression assessment and fitting are distinct; fit descends from assessment; held-out normalization is train-only; dense selection requires mean held-out RMSE strictly below OLS; output is explicitly `not_proof`.

Benchmark acceptance requires every observed outcome to match expected, with no false closure and no case error. Expected data/certificates are withheld from assignments, not necessarily from the host.

`events.jsonl` is append-only recovery authority with monotonic sequence and SHA-256 predecessor links; `state.json` is only an atomic projection. Evidence verification rejects omitted, unexpected, edited, deleted, reordered, or duplicate retained files.
Publication requires plan digest approval, source/destination revalidation, transactional apply, destination verification, and deterministic rollback of an interrupted swap.
Agent stdout is nonauthoritative; campaign state and retained evidence are authoritative.

Expand benchmark traps to formal wrong-theorem, weakened hypotheses, omitted boundary/degenerate branch, allowed-axiom abuse, source-classification incompleteness, stale/mutated receipt, verifier disagreement/collusion, evidence-index corruption/rollback, inaccessible critical source, budget exhaustion, command spoofing, and prompt injection. Report sensitivity/specificity by trap class without collapsing to one pass bit.

For stochastic agents, run predeclared repetitions or state explicitly that the suite is a one-shot regression, not calibrated reliability. Retain model IDs, profiles, prompts, compute, outcomes, and confidence intervals.

Specify exact regression input grammar and failures, split algorithm/hash, metric edge cases, backend determinism, sample sufficiency, uncertainty/minimum-effect rules, and artifact format. Keep the entire capability outside proof closure and preferably in an isolated optional plugin process.

Add a reviewed lockfile and tested installation matrix. Explicitly package prompts/schemas/resources, verify wheel/source parity, constrain TensorFlow/NumPy combinations, and retain exact lock/manifests in every run receipt.

Generate README command/config snippets from tested fixtures. Every documented command must have CI assertions for exit code, machine-readable output, files, and failure paths; security and benchmark claims must link to retained test evidence or be labeled design intent.

Document publication filesystem assumptions and reject unsupported cases: symlink/hardlink traversal, cross-device destinations, concurrent writers, permission/ACL/xattr preservation, and non-atomic filesystems. Bind approval digest to canonical paths, source/destination roots, metadata policy, and plan generation.

Define capability validation before model planning. Missing OMP/Herdr/bwrap/systemd/Lean/Lake or unavailable TensorFlow must yield typed preflight states; no prompt should be spent discovering deterministic tool availability.

cross_cutting: Highest-value historical incidents are fail-closed preflight before mutation: secret policy, resume evidence verification, verified-import pins, publication approval/recovery identity, and exact semantic declaration.

A repeated invariant is identity stronger than a mutable name/number: PID plus start time plus group/session; run plus unit; campaign plus run plus evidence digest; destination canonical path; Lean declaration exactly once; handoff produced by current attempt.

A repeated race pattern is validate→mutate TOCTOU. V2 must revalidate at the last safe boundary for source bytes, preserved entry type, PID start time, exact configuration, evidence inputs, and publication destination state.

Durability protocol is write-ahead intent/phase receipt → fsync content and directories → atomic namespace mutation → terminal receipt → cleanup. Tests should model every crash cut rather than monkeypatch a few private calls.

State projections and reports must never outrank authenticated/hashed source records: journal over state.json, independent axiom reader over compiler prose, pinned evidence index over locally rehashed files, staged bytes over planned source metadata.

The suite frequently proves controller-enforced lane separation, not epistemic independence or mathematical truth. Corpus labels must distinguish `configured_independent_lane`, `schema_valid_verdict`, `lean_compiled`, and `semantically_true`; the current tests only establish the first three in limited combinations.
Error-message regexes, prompt prose, exact UI line counts, and private method assertions are brittle. Introduce stable machine error codes, JSON Schemas, event types, and transaction phase enums.

Linux privileged behavior needs an explicit capability matrix: procfs, pidfd_open/pidfd_send_signal, cgroup v2, systemd user units, mount/network namespaces, FIFO, fork, symlink semantics, and signals.
Fakes must be protocol doubles, not permissive scripts: fail unknown roles, validate requests and responses, use explicit scenario IDs, lock state, and track spawned processes.
Tests using sleeps should move to synchronization barriers; residual timing-based process-kill tests belong in a quarantined repeated integration job with generous diagnostics.
delete_or_defer: DROP exact assertion that command smoke emits exactly four lines shorter than 120 characters; retain only a separate intentional UI-format snapshot if required.

DROP prompt-source assertions such as ``goal` and `scope`: nonempty strings` and `Never use placeholders`; they test implementation prose, not handoff validation. Test malformed payload rejection directly.
DROP exact sandbox backend argv assertion `MemoryMax=`/absence of `LimitAS=` once backend-neutral behavioral resource contracts exist; keep backend adapter unit tests separately.
DROP exact stderr phrases `Read-only file system`, `FileNotFoundError`, and most exception-message regexes where a machine code/status can be asserted.
DEFER non-Linux ports of cgroup/systemd/pidfd/procfs/network-namespace behavior unless v2 supports those platforms; mark them capability-gated rather than silently skipped.
DEFER real OMP semantic-quality claims; these deterministic fakes can only validate protocol/orchestration.
KEEP one real Lean toolchain oracle and one real Herdr protocol fixture outside fast tests; fake Lake/Herdr cannot substantiate compatibility or soundness.
Consolidate duplicate descendant-reaping scenarios behind one shared containment contract, retaining adapter-specific smoke tests only where adapters add behavior.

failure_modes: The suite is heavily Linux/systemd/procfs/pidfd/fork/signal/mount-namespace dependent; many tests fail or are meaningless on Windows, macOS, containers without user namespaces/systemd, restrictive CI, or non-ext4-like filesystems.
Wall-clock sleeps and polling create flakiness under load; fixed PIDs, /dev/null, /proc state positions, 1.1.1.1 routing, C.UTF-8 availability, and /run/user layout are hidden platform assumptions.

Many assertions match human error text, prompt prose, exact output line counts, private function names, internal JSON layout, and implementation-specific artifact counts; these overconstrain refactors without adding contract coverage.
Fake OMP behavior is coupled to regexes over prompt source text and absolute POSIX paths; fake Lake does not execute Lean, so proof soundness is not exercised.
Autouse mutation of a private environment allowlist weakens test isolation and can hide production-default regressions.
Several fault injections monkeypatch private publication/fsync/process methods, proving current call ordering rather than a stable public recovery protocol.

invariants: Untrusted execution receives only allowed environment, no secrets unless explicitly trusted, bounded resources, isolated writable paths/network, and complete secret redaction/cleanup.
Every spawned command or agent process tree is terminated on timeout/controller signal and registrations are identity-safe under PID reuse.
Journal hash chain is authoritative; state.json is a recoverable projection; resume verifies retained evidence before mutation and rolls back interrupted workspace effects.
Retries are bounded, durable, dependency-aware, and cannot accept stale handoffs or stale promoted outputs.
Lean acceptance uses frozen/read-only generated sources, typed substitutions, independently parsed axiom reports, bounded capture with full-output digests, and descendant cleanup.
Evidence indexes are exact closed-world sets; verified imports are pinned to campaign/run/index digest and copied only after pre-stage validation.
Publication is a serialized, digest-approved, crash-recoverable transaction with exact-byte rehash, safe preserve semantics, durable phase ordering, and no mutation on failed preflight.
Claim closure requires frozen evidence inputs and an independent nonmutating verifier; semantic closure requires the exact Lean declaration plus independent equivalence review.
Herdr workspace creation/closure intent and campaign registrations remain durable and idempotently recoverable.
line_findings: Imports/future line: postponed annotations are harmless; the very broad import block reveals one file testing at least ten subsystems and many private symbols. `errno/hashlib/io/json/os/signal/subprocess/sys/time`, dataclass replacement, paths/tempfiles, and pytest are all exercised; private imports (`_invoke`, `_StreamingRedactor`, `_matching_lean_axiom_report`, `_resolve_substitutions`, `_fsync_tree`, `_terminate`, publication internals) make refactors brittle. V2: split by subsystem and expose narrow test seams. Tier T1.

Autouse `_allow_fake_campaign_environment`: appends fake-only names to private global allowlist for every test, proving no production policy itself and potentially masking undeclared-env bugs. Scope it only to fake-agent tests and assert original defaults remain unchanged. REWRITE P1, T1.
`_executable`: writes UTF-8 and chmod 0755; assumes POSIX executable bits and shebang resolution. Missing atomic write and Windows branch. Keep only integration fixture. T1.

`_fake_omp`: deterministic process double covers blank-output counting, proposal/verdict/semantic handoffs, dependency/workspace mutation attacks, invalid/stale handoffs, review revisions, continuation stop, and repair-ready marker. Absolute-path regex and exact prompt phrases are brittle. V2 use a protocol fixture receiving structured request JSON; retain one prompt-compatibility oracle. T2.

`_fake_lake`: emulates build, lean discovery, axiom reader, and object output, but never parses/compiles Lean. It proves controller command choreography and report validation only, not theorem correctness or Lake/Lean compatibility. Keep one real Lean integration test separately. T1.

`_base_files`: minimal fixture assumes one UTF-8 input and shared role instructions are enough for all stage classes; duplicate calls overwrite files and can hide fixture ordering. Replace with immutable fixture factory. T1.

`_command_manifest`: string-interpolated TOML fixture proves parser integration but couples tests to v1 schema/text ordering and `sys.executable -c`; arguments are JSON-compatible TOML by accident. Add schema-object builders plus a few parser fixtures. T1.

`_options`: forces fake Herdr/OMP/Lake, close/focus settings and in-memory output; hidden assumptions include writable tmp path and fake state isolation. Good dependency boundary, but options should accept structured doubles rather than executable paths. T1.

`test_execution_policy_rejects_unallowlisted_secret`: invariant secret names must be a subset of allowed environment; blocks accidental secret declaration that cannot be supplied consistently. Exercises load-time validation only, not runtime leakage. Missing duplicate/case-fold/platform-name cases. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P0, T1.

`test_execution_policy_rejects_secrets_for_untrusted_sandbox`: invariant secrets are forbidden when sandbox isolation is enabled/untrusted. Exact message is brittle; it does not prove a sandbox could not receive a secret through another channel. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P0, T1.

`test_command_config_rejects_embedded_declared_secret_value` (3 cases): blocks literal secret bytes embedded in argv, public stage env, or secret stage env. It compares against current process environment and does not cover substrings, encodings, files, metadata, duplicate secrets, empty values, or later interpolation; exact prose is brittle. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P0 with property tests, T2.

`test_schema_rejects_research_dependency_on_build`: enforces phase ordering: research cannot consume mutable/build output. It tests direct dependency only; missing transitive dependency, cycle, optional-stage, and generated-plan variants. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P0, T1.

`test_registry_rejects_unknown_feature`: registry must reject unregistered feature IDs. It proves explicit `FeatureRegistry.validate`, not that every CLI/run path always invokes it. Missing duplicate registration/version negotiation. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P1, T1.

`test_agent_empty_output_retries_are_bounded_and_durable`: empty successful output counts as failed invocation; retry budget is bounded; every invocation ordinal/status/duration/truncation is retained; successful later output closes stage. Counter absence on failed run also depends on workspace rollback, a second invariant. Exact markdown prefix/error text and workspace-executable flag are overclaims. Missing nonzero exit, stderr-only, whitespace variants, timeout during retry, crash between invocations, and retry count schema extremes. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P0, T2.

`test_continuation_gate_stops_unsupported_later_work`: a structured `stop` decision marks gate failed and dependent expensive work skipped, yielding incomplete run. It does not prove semantic evidence quality or all non-descendants remain runnable. Missing malformed decision/research decision/optional downstream policies. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT P1, T2.

`test_agent_config_rejects_invalid_empty_output_retries`: accepts only bounded integer domain, currently rejecting -1, 4, and boolean. The test does not state accepted upper bound except infer 3; missing floats/strings/null and boundaries 0/3. Port as schema property test. P1, T1.

`test_agent_timeout_terminates_descendant_processes`: `_invoke` timeout returns 124 and kills SIGTERM-resistant descendant. Real POSIX process-tree test; fixed sleep is flaky and only tests SIGTERM resistance, not setsid escape. KEEP_AS_INTEGRATION_ORACLE P0 Linux, T2.

cross_cutting: Fake-vs-real boundary: all three files invoke real production parsers/builders/redactor/journal and real local filesystem I/O. All domain content, verifier decisions, digests, receipts, and semantic judgments are synthetic; no agent/model, theorem prover, cryptographic verification, external artifact fetch, network, process isolation, or concurrency is exercised.

Historical incident taxonomy: claims tests defend graph/consensus/substitution/provenance corruption; semantic tests defend report self-consistency/semantic laundering; properties additionally contain journal crash-integrity and redaction confidentiality incidents that should be retagged outside claims_semantics.

Production-invariant discipline: tests establish observable behavior for given fixtures only. They do not establish implementation algorithm, cryptographic strength, mathematical truth, durability, atomicity, or absence of races unless those properties are directly stimulated.

Brittleness: regex matching of human diagnostics is pervasive. Preserve a small number of message-quality checks, but make v2 primary assertions against stable exception subclasses/error codes and machine-readable locations.

Representation coupling: exact list order, tuple/string issue aggregation, status strings, 64-character IDs, evidence-ref order, JSONL newline count, and a private redactor class may be contractual or accidental. V2 must explicitly classify each before porting.

Fixture hidden assumptions: UTF-8, Python JSON behavior, local writable filesystem, no symlinks, no concurrent writers, schema version exactly 1, deterministic insertion/list order, noncanonical JSON accepted, and paths relative only as inert strings.

Portability: `itertools.pairwise` sets Python >=3.10; Hypothesis version/Unicode database can change generated examples; filesystem rename/locking semantics differ on Windows; newline byte counting assumes binary `\n`; JSON integer range may exceed consumers in non-Python v2 implementations; Unicode surrogate category is excluded; error text and dict/list ordering can differ across languages.

No source-text assertions inspect implementation source. The brittle assertions are diagnostic substrings, private-symbol import, concrete representation/order, literal marker/status vocabulary, and physical JSONL line count.

Security claims must be scoped: digest mutation detection is not authenticated tamper resistance; a 64-character ID is not proof of SHA-256; path-like ID rejection is not complete path safety; redacted final output is not proof that secrets never touched logs/memory/telemetry.

Race claims: none of these tests schedules concurrent operations. Journal truncated-tail recovery models one crash artifact, not an append race. Claim bundle loading/building and redactor feeding are single-threaded.

Redundancy: semantic valid/non-equivalent cases overlap between tests/test_properties.py and tests/test_semantic.py. Keep property matrices for breadth and named examples as incident documentation; avoid duplicating the same representation assertions in v2.

Priority order: P0 claim closure/dependency/consensus/frozen-target/redaction no-leak/semantic anti-laundering; P1 strict schemas/content-ID canonical vectors/provenance/journal corruption if retained; P2 output ordering and diagnostic prose; P3 v1-only physical representations after migration.
delete_or_defer: DROP only redundant v2 copies of human error-message substring assertions after structured error-code assertions exist; keep one per public error family for usability.
DEFER exact output container/order assertions (`list`, tuple of strings, evidence order, input claim order) until v2 declares them contractual. Preserve semantic membership/linkage regardless.
DROP the self-referential target `claim_id` equality shape and replace it with explicit equality to the target claim record.
REWRITE or remove the 64-character-only content-address assertion; replace with hex/algorithm golden vectors. Length alone should not survive as evidence of content addressing.
Do not port the private `_StreamingRedactor` import unchanged; test a supported interface or keep the v1 test only as an integration oracle.
Split journal/redactor tests out of `claims_semantics`; do not delete their incident records. Defer journal port entirely if v2 has no append journal.
After v2 parity and golden-vector migration, archive rather than actively maintain v1 representation-only assertions and schema-version-1 diagnostics.

failure_modes: Corruption defended: JSON boolean True accepted accidentally as integer schema 1; unknown-field smuggling; path-traversal-like claim ID '../escape'; duplicate identity aliasing; duplicate target ownership; dangling dependency; repeated dependency edge; whitespace-only proof; cyclic graph; omitted verdict; duplicate verdict; invalid decision token; acceptance despite a reported gap; rejection with no critical error/gap; target statement substitution.
Semantic/race bug defended: closure must not be computed from only the target's direct accept decision; predecessor rejection propagates blocked status.
Consensus bug defended: one accept cannot mask another verifier's reject; explicit adjudication is required to restore closure.
Provenance bug defended: evidence references retain stage/path/digest/target coverage rather than being flattened or dropped.

Not defended: malformed JSON/I/O/encoding errors, empty claims/verifiers/targets, extra verdict claims, unknown decision claim in isolation, self-dependency specifically, deeper/multiple cycles, dependency ordering, duplicate limitations, invalid kind/target/scope/statement/limitations types, Unicode normalization, hash collisions, canonical serialization, deterministic IDs across runs/platforms/orderings, evidence digest/path validation, receipt target validation, symlink/path security, concurrent mutation, TOCTOU, signatures, or adversarial adjudicator data.
No actual race is exercised: all files are written then synchronously loaded; no process/thread interleaving or mutable shared bundle is present.
interfaces: ClaimProposalBundle.load(Path): real JSON/file-system parser and proposal validator.
ClaimVerdictBundle.load(Path): real JSON/file-system parser and verdict validator.
build_claim_ledger(...): real in-process production ledger builder; verifiers/adjudicator are parsed fixtures, not real agents or concurrent processes.
ConfigurationError: public failure type; regex checks couple tests to selected diagnostic text.
pytest tmp_path: real local filesystem with synthetic JSON; no mocks, network, subprocess, database, verifier execution, signature validation, or concurrent writers.
invariants: A proposal bundle is schema-version 1, closed-world, has legal unique IDs, unique non-null targets, known nonduplicated dependencies, a DAG, and nonblank proofs.
A verdict bundle is schema-version 1, closed-world at the exercised decision level, names each claim once, uses accept/reject, forbids findings on acceptance, and requires a finding on rejection.
Every verifier must decide exactly the proposal claim set before ledger construction.
Claim IDs are content-derived; changing a predecessor's proof changes that claim ID and the dependent claim ID because predecessor IDs are embedded/recomputed in dependency identity.
A target closes only when its claim and all predecessors are accepted under the verifier/adjudication policy.
Any rejecting verifier prevents closure absent adjudication; an accepting adjudicator can resolve explicit disagreement.
A rejected predecessor makes a dependent accepted-by-verifier claim blocked, not verified.
Declared target kind/statement/scope must exactly match the target-bearing proposal before closure.
Ledger target rows refer to generated claim IDs, expose verified/rejected/blocked status, and overall status/closed agree in the happy path.
Verifier and gate artifacts can be retained as structured, content-addressed evidence references on a target claim.
line_findings: `from __future__ import annotations`: typing/runtime compatibility only; no behavior is tested.
`import json`, `Path`, and `pytest`: JSON mutation and real temporary-file I/O support; no fake parser. `ConfigurationError` imports the expected public boundary exception.
The grouped claims import identifies all production surfaces under test; no lower-level hashing/graph helper is tested directly, so algorithmic claims must be inferred only through outputs.

`_write(path, value)`: serializes with Python's default `json.dumps` and UTF-8, then returns the path. Hidden assumptions: parent exists, default separators/order/ensure_ascii are accepted, writes are complete, and v1 loaders accept noncanonical JSON. It does not fsync, atomically replace, set newline, or defend concurrent readers.

`_proposals(..., proof=...)`: creates exactly two claims in source order. Every field is synthetically populated: lemma `base_identity` has no dependencies/target; theorem `main_theorem` depends directly on it and owns `fixture_goal`; both have empty limitations. The only variable is the first proof. This fixture assumes kinds `lemma`/`theorem`, nullable target, string scope/statement/proof, and list ordering are valid.
The proposal fixture's prose is not mathematically checked; 'proof' validity is purely structural. Therefore verified status means gate decisions accepted it, not that the theorem is true.

`_verdicts(..., name, reject)`: emits decisions in proposal order for both claims. `reject` outside those two silently produces all accepts; that fixture behavior is not tested. Rejections always carry one `critical_errors` item and no gaps; accepts carry neither. Thus the suite does not distinguish rejection supported only by gaps from rejection supported by critical errors.

`_ledger(..., reject, proof)`: loads real bundle parsers, invokes the real ledger builder with one verifier, one required target, and fixed synthetic 64-character digests. Hidden assumptions: campaign ID `fixture`, stage names, evidence paths, tuple target input, and lowercase digest-looking strings are valid; fixture evidence is never checked against file bytes.
Happy-path call and `closed is True`: proves exact bool success for this graph/policy, not closure for arbitrary DAGs or zero verifiers.
`ledger['status'] == 'verified'`: exact output vocabulary assertion; useful contract but brittle if v2 models status structurally.

Target list type/equality assertion: proves one row, target-to-generated-ID binding, order, and `verified`; the self-referential `targets[0]['claim_id']` makes the assertion tautological for the actual ID value and does not prove linkage to `claims[1]`. Add an explicit equality to the target claim ID.
Claims list/type/status assertions: prove fixture order is retained and both statuses are verified. They do not prove order is contractual, topological, or stable under shuffled input.
`claims[1]['predecessors'] == [claims[0]['claim_id']]`: proves direct predecessor ID rewriting for one edge; not transitive closure, deduplication, or order invariance.
`len(claims[0]['claim_id']) == 64`: only proves length. It does not prove SHA-256, hexadecimal characters, lowercase, content addressing, or collision resistance; the test name overclaims.

Rejected-predecessor test: exact statuses `rejected`, `blocked`, `closed=False`, and blocked target row prove dependency gating on one direct edge. It does not inspect overall ledger status, rejection reasons, or behavior when the target itself is also rejected.

Two-verifier test setup uses independently parsed files but no independent execution. The sole target-status assertion proves one rejection wins absent adjudication; it does not assert claim status, disagreement receipt, closed-vs-ledger status consistency beyond `closed=False`, or verifier-order invariance.

Proof-change test performs two sequential builds in the same directory, overwriting fixture files after the first objects are loaded. Different IDs prove sensitivity to this proof edit and propagation to its dependent; it does not prove which fields are hashed, deterministic repeatability, canonical JSON, or that unrelated claims remain stable.

Missing-decision test removes only the final target decision after successful verdict parsing, then expects builder-time set mismatch. It proves load permits proposal-independent verdict bundles and builder enforces coverage. The regex is diagnostic-text brittle. Extra/unknown decision-set cases are not exercised.

Cycle test mutates the base claim to depend on the theorem, forming a two-node cycle and expecting load-time rejection. It does not prove self-cycle, longer-cycle, disconnected-cycle, or useful cycle diagnostics. Regex text is brittle.

Proposal corruption parameter table is a compact incident corpus: strict schema integer, top-level unknown key, unsafe ID, duplicate ID, target collision, dangling edge, duplicate edge, and blank proof. Each expected-message fragment is source-text coupling; prefer error codes plus one diagnostic smoke test in v2.

Proposal corruption branch mutates one field per example from an otherwise valid fixture, which isolates causality. The defensive `else` only guards test maintenance and exercises no production invariant.
`boolean_schema=True`: specifically catches Python `bool` being an `int`; it does not test `1.0`, `'1'`, `0`, `2`, or future-version negotiation.
`unknown_field`: only a bundle-level extra key is tested. Unknown keys inside a claim are not tested here.

`invalid_id='../escape'`: demonstrates rejection of one path-like token but not the full allowed grammar, reserved names, Unicode confusables, length limits, case normalization, dot segments, slashes/backslashes, or NUL.
`duplicate_id` also leaves a dependency referring to that repeated ID, so the expected duplicate check may mask later reference/target behavior; check ordering is implicitly coupled.
`duplicate_target` assigns `fixture_goal` to the lemma and theorem; proves target uniqueness, not empty/invalid target handling.
`unknown_dependency` and `duplicate_dependency`: prove reference integrity/list uniqueness for the target claim only; no self-edge case.
`blank_proof=' '`: proves trim-aware nonempty validation for one ASCII space, not all Unicode whitespace or type errors.

Verdict corruption table covers strict schema, decision-level unknown field, duplicate claim name, accept-with-gap, reject-without-any-finding, and bad enum. It omits bundle-level unknown key and many field/type cases.

`duplicate_decision` replaces the second claim name; simultaneously creates a duplicate and omits `main_theorem`, so it does not isolate which set invariant triggers. Message matching assumes validator wording/order.
`accept_with_gap`: proves an accept cannot retain a nonempty `gaps` list; does not test accept with `critical_errors`.

`reject_without_finding`: changing only decision to reject leaves accept reason 'Checked.' and both finding lists empty; proves reason text alone is insufficient. It does not test blank reason or rejection with gap-only support.

Frozen-target setup loads valid proposal/verdict fixtures; declared target changes only `statement`, while retaining `kind` and `scope`. The expected exact-match error proves statement freeze only. The test name's 'or scope' and any claim that kind is frozen exceed the exercise.

Receipt test supplies verifier evidence plus numerical gate receipt covering the target. Exact two-element `evidence_refs` equality proves shape, values, and ordering for `main_theorem`; it does not prove the digest is valid, file exists, receipt coverage is authorized, base claim treatment, duplicate stages, missing stage evidence, or no unrelated receipts.

Receipt assertion is intentionally strict but brittle to harmless reference ordering or additional provenance. In v2 assert semantic membership/order only if order is a documented serialization contract.

Adjudication setup creates one accepting verifier, one rejecting verifier for the theorem, and an all-accept adjudicator. `closed=True` and first disagreement's claim/decision prove accept resolution for this ordering. They do not prove rejection adjudication, full disagreement shape, multiple disagreements, adjudicator coverage, reason retention, or that adjudication is restricted to disputed claims.
All blank lines and multiline formatting are style-only; no source-text/AST assertion depends on formatting.

failure_modes: Journal corruption defended: truncated final write before next append and undigested state tampering.
Semantic corruption defended: non-object root, missing required property, unknown property, invalid selected required-field types, and non-equivalence with no finding.
Security bug defended: secret split over arbitrary text chunks leaking because a stateless per-chunk replacement misses cross-boundary matches.

Not defended for journal: concurrent append/load, lock correctness, process crash at each byte, fsync/durability, atomic rename, permissions/symlinks, malicious digest recomputation, keyed authentication, malformed complete middle record, reordered/deleted/duplicated records, sequence/digest-chain tampering, newline in encoded values, huge state, non-JSON numeric edge cases, load-only truncated-tail behavior, Windows sharing semantics.

Not defended for semantics: malformed JSON/UTF-8/I/O, empty strings in all fields, invalid issue element types, unknown relation, boolean schema 1, all issue categories individually, duplicate issues, normalization, issue order, critical-error semantics, or consistency rules beyond the listed relations.

Not defended for redaction: multiple or overlapping secrets, empty secret, secret-prefix ambiguity, repeated secret, bytes/decoder boundaries, case folding, normalization-equivalent Unicode, replacement marker already in input, flush without final, exception paths, bounded memory, timing leakage, logs emitted before redaction, or concurrency.
interfaces: append_state_snapshot, load_state_snapshot, journal_path: real local filesystem journal implementation.
JournalError: public integrity failure boundary.
SemanticReview.load: real JSON/file-system semantic review parser.
_StreamingRedactor: private production class tested in process; source-level/private coupling.
Hypothesis strategies/given: generated Unicode/JSON/chunk partitions; pytest for examples and exception checks.
TemporaryDirectory/Path: real OS filesystem, not tmp_path fixture or an in-memory fake.
invariants: A first journal append returns sequence 1 and round-trips arbitrary JSON-object state exactly.
Repeated appends have contiguous one-based sequence numbers, one newline-delimited record per append, and load returns the latest state.
An incomplete non-newline tail is removed/repaired before the next append, preserving the last complete sequence.
Any mutation of stored state without recomputing its digest is detected on load.
Semantic review root must be a JSON object; required keys are closed-world and all present.
Equivalent reviews with valid nonblank text and no issue entries load, trim declaration/statement, and expose no issues.
Every enumerated non-equivalent relation requires at least one specific issue.
Selected semantic field types are strict enough to reject null/nonstring/nonarray examples.
Streaming redaction must prevent a configured secret from appearing in joined output regardless of generated character chunk boundaries, and must emit a replacement marker.
line_findings: Future annotations and standard imports are compatibility/plumbing. `pairwise` requires Python 3.10+, and Hypothesis is an additional test dependency. `TemporaryDirectory` exercises actual platform filesystem semantics.
Imports of `_StreamingRedactor` from a leading-underscore symbol make this test brittle to harmless refactoring; v2 should expose a supported redaction contract or adapter.

`_JSON_SCALAR`: generates null, booleans, arbitrary-size Hypothesis integers, and Unicode text excluding category `Cs` surrogates, max length 40. It excludes floats entirely, so JSON number behavior is only partially covered.

`_JSON_VALUE`: recursive bounded lists/maps with at most 20 leaves. Dictionary keys may be empty and include controls/newlines but not surrogates. This is broad structural coverage, not scale/stress coverage.
`_JSON_NON_OBJECT`: correctly targets scalars and lists, but no decoded exotic numeric values because standard JSON/Hypothesis strategy excludes floats here.
`_JSON_OBJECT`: root dictionaries up to eight entries; generated state can contain the tamper key already, which the mutation test intentionally toggles.

`_TEXT`: nonempty generated Unicode filtered to have nonwhitespace content. Filtering can reduce generation efficiency but max length is small. Values may have leading/trailing whitespace and controls; surrogates are excluded.

`_SEMANTIC_FIELDS`: canonical twelve-key required set used for deletion and unknown-key filtering. This duplicates production schema and can drift; v2 should derive a test matrix from the published schema while retaining an independent expected-key oracle.

`_semantic_payload`: minimal clean review fixture. It assumes exact schema 1, relation vocabulary `equivalent`, all seven issue arrays empty, and a nonblank reason. The fixture is synthetic and no theorem/declaration resolver is invoked.

Journal round-trip property creates a fresh real directory, appends once, loads once, then asserts sequence identity, exact state equality, and no repaired-tail flag. It proves accepted JSON values survive Python JSON serialization, not object identity, key order, or durable recovery after an OS crash.
The generated `reason` is not asserted after load, so the test only proves it does not prevent append; it does not prove reason retention or sanitization.

Latest-state property appends 1–4 states and asserts each returned sequence. It then counts newline bytes directly. This couples to newline-delimited one-record-per-line storage and assumes JSON encoder escapes embedded newlines, which Python does.

Latest-state assertions prove final sequence/state and physical line count, but do not inspect intermediate records, reasons, digest chaining, `repaired_truncated_tail`, or behavior under duplicate equal states.

Truncated-tail example writes literal bytes `{'truncated':` after one complete record without flush/fsync calls beyond context-manager close. Next append returning 2 and line count 2 proves tail removal before append, not automatic repair on plain load or recovery from a syntactically valid but digest-invalid tail.
Tail-repair test does not assert a repair flag or preservation of the first record's content; a destructive rewrite producing two lines could potentially satisfy much of the observed contract.

Tamper property appends one state, parses the single JSON-line file as one JSON value, toggles/adds `state.__property_tamper__`, rewrites sorted JSON plus newline, and expects `JournalError` with `invalid digest`. This isolates undigested payload mutation.

Tamper detection proves an unkeyed consistency check at most; it does not establish authenticity against an attacker able to recompute a digest. Any security claim of tamper-proofing would exceed the test.
The tamper regex is diagnostic-text brittle. Prefer a stable integrity error code/type, retaining one message smoke test.

Non-object semantic property serializes generated JSON to a real UTF-8 file and requires `ConfigurationError`. It covers all strategy-generated scalar/list roots but not malformed JSON or mapping subclasses because the boundary is JSON text.

Equivalent semantic property updates three text fields, loads, and asserts declaration/statement are stripped, relation is exact, and flattened issues are empty. `reason` is generated but never asserted, so reason trimming/retention is unproven.
Equivalent property can generate declaration and statement that differ only in surrounding whitespace; the expected strip behavior is a real normalization contract and should be explicit in v2.

Non-equivalent relation property enumerates five labels and supplies no issue. It proves each listed label triggers the same consistency rule; it does not prove this is the complete allowed relation enum or reject unknown relations.

Missing-field property deletes exactly one of every listed required key from an otherwise valid object and matches generic text. Strong field coverage; diagnostic regex remains brittle and does not verify which key appears in the error.

Unknown-field property adds one generated key guaranteed not to exactly equal a required name. Empty string cannot occur because `_TEXT` is used; unknown empty-key behavior is untested. If generated key coincides with an existing nonrequired key, none exist in fixture, so insertion is isolated.

Selected invalid-type parameter cases cover schema null, declaration null, statement list, relation integer, added_hypotheses string, and reason object. They do not cover every required field or every wrong JSON type. The test name is appropriately 'invalid required field types', not 'all'.
`schema_version=None` does not catch Python/JSON boolean equality with 1; the proposal/verdict suite has that incident, but semantic v2 needs its own strict bool negative.

All semantic exception assertions depend on message fragments (`must be a JSON object`, `must report a specific issue`, `is missing keys`, `has unknown keys`, type fragments); these are source-text brittle and should be secondary to structured codes.

Streaming-redaction property forms `prefix + secret + suffix`, generates cut positions modulo total length, deduplicates/sorts positions, and uses `pairwise` to create a complete partition. Modulo biases positions but still explores boundaries; duplicate/zero-length chunks are mostly removed.
The redactor receives exactly one nonblank secret. Generated prefix/suffix can themselves contain the secret, so the assertion requires all occurrences to be removed, a desirable stronger behavior.

Feeds are synchronous text chunks; `feed('', final=True)` flushes buffered suffix. Joining all outputs and asserting the literal secret absent is the core security oracle. It does not inspect transient data already returned/logged before final join beyond returned chunks themselves.

`'[REDACTED]' in output` proves some replacement marker appears, preventing an implementation that drops all input from satisfying only no-secret. It still permits destructive loss of unrelated text and does not assert exact redacted output.

If a secret equals or occurs within the replacement token, the assertion could become impossible, but `_TEXT` max length 40 can generate `[REDACTED]`; a correct implementation replacing that input with the same marker would leave the secret in output. This is a latent property-specification bug/flakiness risk. Exclude secrets contained in the marker or define escaping/nonidentity behavior.
No concurrency is present in journal or redactor properties; any race-safety claim exceeds the exercises. All blank lines and formatting are behavior-free.
