failure_modes: Semantic laundering defended: declaring equivalence while admitting an added hypothesis.
Unsupported conclusion defended: declaring a conditional fragment with no concrete finding.
Data-loss defended: a concrete added-hypothesis scope failure must survive parsing and appear in aggregate issues.

Not defended: every other issue category under equivalence, multiple/mixed issues and ordering, critical errors, unknown relations, malformed/missing/extra fields, field types, whitespace-only issue strings, duplicate findings, relation-specific category requirements, declaration lookup, truth of informal/formal statements, Unicode normalization, or file I/O failures. Some generic boundaries are covered in tests/test_properties.py, not here.
interfaces: SemanticReview.load(Path): real JSON file parser/validator.
ConfigurationError: public validation failure type with regex-coupled message fragments.
pytest tmp_path: real per-test local filesystem; no semantic agent, theorem prover, declaration resolver, network, or mock.
invariants: A schema-1 review claiming `equivalent` is valid when every issue category is empty and required text is nonblank.
An `equivalent` relation cannot coexist with an added-hypothesis mismatch.
A `conditional_fragment` relation must carry at least one specific issue.
A valid non-equivalent review retains relation and exposes the issue text through the normalized `issues` tuple.
line_findings: Future annotations, `json`, `Path`, and `pytest` are test plumbing. Imports target the public parser and public configuration exception.

`_review(tmp_path, **overrides)`: builds a complete clean schema-1 fixture, then blindly applies overrides. Hidden assumption: Python insertion order and JSON default encoding are irrelevant to parser semantics; parent directory exists; writes are complete UTF-8.

Every fixture field is significant: declaration/informal statement identify the compared artifacts; relation is `equivalent`; seven mismatch/error arrays are empty; reason is nonblank. The prose is never externally validated, so tests enforce self-consistency of a report, not theorem equivalence.

Blind `value.update(overrides)` permits unknown-field/type corruption in future tests but can also let a caller accidentally replace schema shape. Current tests use only `added_hypotheses` and `relation`.
Fixture always writes `semantic.json`; tmp_path isolation prevents cross-test collision. There is no concurrent access, partial write, symlink, permissions, or alternate encoding exercise.
Clean test asserts exact relation, empty tuple issues, and declaration retention. It does not assert statement, reason, schema version, every category, or trimming.
The clean test name's 'equivalence review is accepted' is accurate only for this one syntactically self-consistent payload; it does not prove actual semantic equivalence.

Added-hypothesis test puts one nonblank string into `added_hypotheses` while relation remains equivalent and expects a consistency error. It proves one category; generalized claims that equivalence rejects all mismatch categories exceed this test unless supported by the property/production schema elsewhere.
The `cannot report mismatches` regex is brittle to wording and may accidentally match the wrong validation branch; v2 should assert a stable code such as `EQUIVALENT_WITH_ISSUES`.

No-finding test changes relation to `conditional_fragment` and leaves all issue arrays empty. It proves that one relation requires a finding; the broader functionally named rule for all non-equivalence is supplied only by the parameterized property test.

Valid conditional-fragment test supplies exactly one added-hypothesis issue. It proves this category is accepted evidence for that relation, relation retention, flattening to a tuple, exact text retention, and no synthetic extra issue.

The phrase 'exact scope failure' is fixture prose, not a checked scope model; the parser does not compare formal and informal scopes here. Any claim that the system discovered or verified the failure exceeds the test.

The final exact tuple assertion is valuable against issue loss but brittle if v2 returns typed categorized findings instead of strings; port the semantic content/category, not necessarily tuple representation.

All exception checks exercise synchronous load-time validation. No race, security boundary, external semantic reviewer, or production declaration lookup is involved. Blank lines and formatting carry no behavior.
files.model_tier: T0_RULE_BASED or T1_SMALL: fixtures and expected contracts are simple. T2_MEDIUM only if a failure requires interpreting changed relation/issue normalization semantics.
playbook_relevance: Semantic anti-laundering checklist: equivalence iff no mismatch/error findings.
Relation-evidence checklist: every non-equivalent/unclear relation must cite at least one categorized issue.
Issue-retention checklist: parser normalization must not erase category, text, or order.
Matrix expansion: relation × issue category × empty/nonempty × criticality.

L30 stdout substring is redundant if the validator's exit code already guarantees all cases, and brittle to wording. Conversely, it is the only assertion tying success to 12 cases; prefer structured JSON with case IDs/count.

L33-L40 load benchmark and expected JSON, extracting all certificate values. Hidden assumptions: JSON schema, every case has certificate, values are strings, and certificate literals are appropriate leak canaries. No expected-case count, ID alignment, uniqueness, or nonempty-certificate assertion.
L42 asserts suite has 12 cases, pinning calibration size. It does not establish expected-outcomes has 12 or corresponds one-to-one.
L43 loops real suite cases. Duplicate case IDs could reuse tmp paths and are not explicitly rejected here.

L44-L47 replace runs_dir with tmp_path/case_id. Hidden assumption: replacing only runs_dir fully redirects all writes; other ProjectSpec paths remain in the checked-in project and must not be mutated.
L48-L55 construct RegimeRunner with case policy, focus=False, StringIO output. This is a hybrid boundary: real loader/snapshot filesystem, fake output stream, no agent/tool execution.
L56 invokes private _initialize_run, a brittle source-structure dependency and possibly bypasses public preconditions/cleanup.
L57-L59 assert pre_workspace exists and bind it. No cleanup assertion or repeated/idempotent initialization case.

L60-L65 exact top-level-name equality is strong for leakage but brittle to harmless generated metadata, version files, or platform artifacts. It checks names only, not entry types, permissions, ownership, symlink targets, or mount boundaries.

L66-L67 explicitly deny benchmark.toml and validation at snapshot root. These are redundant with the exact root-set assertion, but valuable as security-intent documentation; they do not catch renamed/nested copies.

L68-L72 recursively read every file as UTF-8 and concatenate. Binary files or non-UTF-8 text will fail initialization tests even if safe. Content boundaries are erased, no filename/path is searched, and memory use is unbounded for large snapshots.

L73 checks all certificate strings are absent. This can be vacuously true if expected cases/certificates are empty; assert nonempty strings and case alignment. It detects only exact contiguous text and can false-positive on benign shared text or false-negative encoded/whitespace-normalized leaks.

Portability: source checkout, Python subprocess, locale decoding in first test, UTF-8-only snapshot files, filesystem case behavior, symlink semantics, and private runner lifecycle. tmp_path provides isolation but not OS-level sandboxing.
files.model_tier: T0 deterministic/small model for count/layout fixture updates; T1 for benchmark metadata and snapshot lifecycle changes; T2 security-capable model for threat-model reproduction and sandbox/data-exfiltration incidents.

v2_requirements: P0: Preserve plan acyclicity, decision-conditioned research queries, unsolved recommendation cardinality, pilot continuation governance, and independently audited knowledge promotion.

P0: Define promotion audit eligibility precisely in machine-readable terms; add valid audited promotion plus negatives for same task, non-downstream task, ordinary analytic dependent, failed/missing evidence, and unknown verifier.

P0: Preserve manifest-relative path resolution, sandbox-on/network-off defaults, explicit policy parsing, reserved namespace isolation, and add containment checks against traversal/absolute/symlink escapes.
P0: Preserve exact rational conversion and outward-enclosure soundness. Add property-based exact-oracle tests rather than relying on three samples.
P0: Preserve root-bracket validity and bisection sign invariants with endpoint-root, nonfinite, invalid-tolerance, discontinuity, and iteration-limit cases.
P0: Centralize URL policy in a public function; validate every initial and redirected URL before any destination mutation. Specify SSRF, TLS, size, timeout, MIME, and atomic-write policy separately.
P0: Retain CMV and calibration subprocesses as versioned integration oracles with timeouts and structured reports; do not present checker self-consistency as independent formal proof.
P0: Preserve benchmark oracle isolation using explicit per-case secret canaries and an agent-reachability threat model, not only file-tree substring absence.
P1: Expose a public snapshot construction/initialization API so security contracts do not depend solely on RegimeRunner._initialize_run.
P1: Add JSON schemas for checker and calibration-validator reports, require unique check/case IDs, and assert complete expected ID sets.
P1: Record fixture/schema versions and production invariant IDs in each corpus item; distinguish historical exact pins from generic reusable properties.
P1: Run portability lanes for Linux/Windows path behavior where supported and pin/test the SymPy compatibility range.

cross_cutting: The v1 group encodes three nested trust boundaries: model/meta-agent outputs are untrusted and schema/policy validated; campaign solved claims are untrusted until independent success validation; research/workspace trees are untrusted filesystem inputs requiring containment and immutability.

Durability is intent/journal first, caches/derived artifacts second. Resume must validate retained history, reconstruct disposable artifacts, reuse successful expensive outputs, and avoid duplicate terminal side effects.

Exactly-once claims are currently strongest only for one in-process threaded assessment and one strategy receipt. V2 needs process-level crash/concurrency evidence and idempotency keys for every externally visible side effect.

Many test names overclaim: 'repairs ... once' lacks a second-failure/bound assertion; 'executes frozen inputs' only verifies snapshot bytes; 'checks theorem and axioms' uses fake command output; 'novelty' proves syntax/byte difference, not semantic novelty; journal tamper rejection proves continuity detection, not authenticity.

Magic fake-agent triggers embedded in problem/reference text are hidden fixture APIs. Replace them with a scripted fake transport declaring ordered responses: success, nonzero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, schema-invalid output, and interruption barriers.

Prompt prose is not a stable machine contract. Assert structured retry causes, policy codes, role capability, input digests, and authorization sets; reserve exact prose snapshots only for intentional user-facing compatibility tests.

Filesystem and subprocess assumptions skew POSIX/Linux. Mark symlink/chmod/systemd tests by capability, add Windows junction/path/case tests where supported, and define whether network/NFS filesystems are supported or explicitly excluded.

Use deterministic fake clocks and barriers instead of year-2000 timestamps, sleep(0.05), polling deadlines, and monotonic iterator tricks for core unit tests; retain a minimal real timing integration check.

All retained artifacts should carry schema version, run/session ID, phase/round/attempt identity, input digest, producer version, and causal predecessor; tests should validate these bindings to prevent stale/cross-run artifact substitution.

Benchmark blindness and autonomy contract preservation are information-flow properties, not substring/boolean properties. Taint expectations and success contracts, enumerate every child-process/request channel, and independently compare immutable contract digests.
delete_or_defer: DROP exact user/prompt prose assertions such as 'research gate: skip', 'The fixture problem is solved', and validator sentences from core contract tests; retain only in a dedicated CLI/message compatibility suite if wording is a product contract.
DROP dependence on fake-agent magic phrases/files such as 'Trigger invalid assessment' and .request-missing-source; replace with explicit scripted faults.
DROP direct assertions on legacy role-directory numbering and names such as orchestration_planner_repair_2/attempt-001 unless v2 declares that artifact layout public.
DROP the no-op call to _reject_snapshot_symlinks after the only symlink has already been excluded; replace with an actual rejection case.
DEFER distributed cross-host/NFS exactly-once guarantees unless v2 explicitly supports shared-network runs; document local-filesystem scope rather than implying it.
KEEP real sleeper/systemd-adjacent process test only as a platform-marked integration oracle, not a portable unit gate.
KEEP exact generated Lean text only as a small golden if formatting is intentionally stable; otherwise assert parsed semantic contents and use real Lean compilation.
DEFER semantic novelty detection as a hard gate; retain auditable declarations and exact/canonical duplicate detection to avoid claiming model-level novelty proof.

failure_modes: Fake-agent behavior is keyed by magic source text/files, so many end-to-end assertions test fixture protocol compatibility rather than production model behavior.
Most orchestration tests use fake OMP/herdr but real filesystem/controller code; they do not prove real model quality, real network behavior, real sandbox confinement, or actual systemd behavior.
Private-method monkeypatches couple tests to v1 decomposition and can pass while public recovery semantics regress elsewhere.
Prompt substring and exact generated-source/path assertions are brittle to wording, formatting, role renames, attempt layout, and path normalization.
Sequential repeated runs do not exercise simultaneous run allocation; threaded resume does not cover multiprocess, cross-host, NFS, or weak-lock filesystems.
Snapshot tests establish retained bytes and request paths, but do not conclusively establish that every execution read came only from the snapshot.
Journal tampering mutates one exact compact JSON token; alternate serialization, truncation, reordering, deletion, insertion, hash-chain substitution, and rollback are untested.

Source promotion lacks negative cases for source-side symlinks, hard links, traversal/absolute paths, case-fold collisions, TOCTOU swaps, special files, partial-copy rollback, permissions, and Windows junctions/reparse points.
Input copying tests only that an excluded subtree is absent; the subsequent symlink rejection runs on a destination containing no symlink and therefore proves no rejection behavior.

Process-stop test launches a real POSIX executable but fakes sandbox/unit termination; PID reuse, kill escalation, permission denial, stale registrations, and unrelated-process protection are untested.
Benchmark prompt scan only excludes the literal expected_outcome token; expectations could leak as values, aliases, environment, requests, generated directives, or non-prompt artifacts.
Suite-change test treats an appended comment as a change, proving byte-level pinning rather than necessarily semantic suite immutability.

Plan-policy tests cover one over-budget task and one missing dependency edge only; aggregate budgets, boundaries, cycles, mismatched capability task IDs, skip/use contradictions, phase variants, and indirect dependency semantics remain open.
Fixed sleeps/deadlines and filesystem glob ordering can be flaky; run selection via next(iterdir()) assumes a clean, single-entry runs directory.
Tests assume UTF-8, atomic same-filesystem replacement, symlink support, executable chmod/shebang support, stable JSON layouts, case-sensitive paths, and Linux-like process semantics.

invariants: A run reaches complete/solved only after gate, valid plan, campaign, and final assessment artifacts exist.
Meta-agent execution settings, role-specific thinking levels, and execution sandbox/network policy propagate into requests and generated campaign configuration.
Accepted knowledge promotion and obligation disposition are represented in the compute ledger and evidence index.
Failed or invalid gate/planner/assessment outputs receive bounded retry/repair attempts with retained receipts and diagnostic context.
Every durable pre-campaign status is resumable; a corrupt state cache can be rebuilt from an untampered append-only journal, while retained-history tampering is rejected.
Successful planner output is retained across resume rather than expensively or nondeterministically reinvoked.
Each run has a distinct directory and leaves no registered processes or sandbox units after normal completion.
Pre-campaign controller lock acquisition has a finite wait; concurrent resumes serialize terminal assessment and commit it once.

Research writes occur in isolated workspaces; frozen problem/reference inputs are retained; source promotion neither follows destination symlinks outside references nor overwrites retained references.
A campaign completed before assessment can resume to assessment without rerunning the campaign.
Missing critical sources checkpoint before campaign execution and can resume after manual acquisition.
Strategy choice is intent/receipt based and idempotently reconstructs missing, malformed, or stale derived artifacts.
Global stop discovers and terminates a fixed regime meta-agent even before campaign-level registration is available.

Benchmark expected outcomes are withheld from tested prompts; per-case errors are recorded without aborting later cases; interrupted reports resume only unrecorded cases; changed suites cannot resume.
Plans are rejected when phase agent-second budgets are exceeded or regression-fit does not depend on regression-assess.
line_findings: Imports: io/json/path are fixture and artifact plumbing; threading/time/ThreadPoolExecutor exist solely for in-process race and process-stop timing; benchmark_module/regime_module imports expose monkeypatch seams; private/helper imports reveal broad cross-module integration. No meaningful import-only contract should be ported; v2 should import public APIs except deliberate fault-injection interfaces.

project_fixture: writes a minimal theorem, one retained reference, empty knowledge, and schema-v1 TOML with max_tasks=4, max_parallel=2, max_restarts=1, 30-second default, and read/write tools. Hidden assumptions: ProjectSpec creates/resolves runs paths, repeated calls use a fresh tmp_path, references.mkdir has no exist_ok, execution text is trusted TOML, and all tested paths are local UTF-8/case-sensitive. REWRITE as typed fixture factory; tier T1.

benchmark_fixture: two solved cases share one project and checkpoint policy. It assumes report identity/order follows manifest order and relative project/runs paths resolve from suite location. REWRITE as schema fixture; tier T1.

test_regime_runs_gate_plan_agent_and_final_assessment: broad fake-agent integration oracle. Proves state/outcome, analyst/auditor task IDs, report/ledger/evidence, accepted analyst knowledge, meta-phase ledger roles, analyst=high/auditor=xhigh request thinking, one disposed obligation/promotion, execution policy propagation, assessment workspace separation/read access, and user output from the fixture. Defended regressions: skipped gate not recorded, planner/assessment omitted, execution options dropped, assessment writing directly in run, ledger/evidence/promotion not finalized. Fake boundary: fake OMP/herdr and marker state; real controller, files, parsers, registry/evidence logic. Brittle: exact role IDs, messages, counts, path layout, and prose. Claims exceed exercise: no real sandbox/network/model or proof correctness. KEEP_AS_INTEGRATION_ORACLE plus split MUST_PORT_CONTRACT schema tests; tier T2.

test_regime_retries_failed_research_gate_execution: magic problem sentence makes fake transport fail; solved result plus retry prompt diagnostic proves one recovery path. It does not assert attempt receipts/count, retry bound, or distinguish nonzero exit from timeout/malformed output. Replace trigger with explicit scripted agent fault and structured error metadata; MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_regime_resumes_research_gate_after_controller_failure: missing OMP causes both initial/retry gate executions to fail, retains research_gate checkpoint, then resume appends attempt-002 and completes. Proves failed receipt retention and same-run recovery, not power-loss atomicity or all failure classes. Error text 'failed again' and attempt paths are brittle. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_regime_resumes_each_preparation_phase: private _research/_plan exceptions persist phase status; planning additionally truncates state cache and resumes from journal. Research branch uses fake missing-source marker and does not corrupt state. Proves phase checkpoint and one cache-rebuild case; does not prove interruption at substeps. Port as phase-transition crash matrix, not private monkeypatch. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T3.

test_repeated_regime_runs_are_isolated_and_leave_no_processes: three sequential runs get distinct paths, complete evidence, and empty registries. Defends run-directory collision and cleanup leaks. It does not test concurrent allocation, OS child absence beyond registry, or failure cleanup. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT with concurrent negative case; tier T2.

test_pre_campaign_journal_rejects_retained_history_tampering: changes first literal sequence 1 to 9 and expects resume rejection. Proves one continuity/integrity validation, not cryptographic authenticity or general tamper detection. Exact compact JSON replacement is source-format brittle and could silently do nothing if serialization changes. REWRITE with parsed mutation corpus and explicit integrity mechanism; tier T3.

test_pre_campaign_lock_wait_is_bounded: fake lock always reports another controller, monotonic jumps 0→31, and unacquired __exit__ must not run. Proves timeout translation and context-manager safety without wall-clock delay. It does not test retries/sleep cadence, eventual acquisition, lock owner death, or real interprocess exclusion. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE around injectable clock/lock; tier T2.

test_regime_repairs_invalid_final_assessment_once: fake emits an unknown historical task, repair prompt contains validator error, repaired outcome references analyst. Defends acceptance of stale/foreign task IDs. It does not prove 'once' because no second-invalid case or attempt-count assertion exists. Rename claim or add repair-bound negative. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_regime_retries_failed_final_assessment_execution: transport failure is converted into assessment-repair attempt and solved result. Prompt prose is brittle; no receipt/count/bound checks. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE with structured cause; tier T2.

test_regime_repairs_invalid_orchestration_plan_once: fake plan has portfolio strategy without tasks; repaired plan uses only direct and prompt embeds validation reason. Defends orphan strategy-plan acceptance. It does not prove only one repair or other plan invalidities. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_regime_resume_reuses_successful_planner_candidates: valid planner output is retained despite post-parse policy rejection; resume must not execute any planner-prefixed role and eventually writes repair_2 output. Defends expensive/nondeterministic reinvocation after controller failure. Coupled to private validator, role prefixes, and repair numbering; unclear why a retained policy-invalid candidate yields repair_2 rather than stable validation. Port as content-addressed candidate reuse with invocation counter. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T3.

test_regime_isolates_research_writes_from_frozen_inputs: fake research attempts protected mutation and adds a publication; original problem remains, publication is promoted, snapshot is original, each meta request workspace differs from shared pre-workspace, and research gets read paths to frozen problem/references. Defends shared-workspace mutation and loss of legitimate promoted sources. It does not prove kernel-enforced read-only access or no writes through alternate paths. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT plus security integration; tier T3.

test_pre_campaign_input_copy_honors_exclusions: excluded .lake subtree containing a symlink is not copied and keep.txt is copied. _reject_snapshot_symlinks sees no symlink, so this test cannot claim symlink rejection. Defends exclusion matching for root and descendants only. Add unexcluded symlink rejection, nested patterns, normalization, junctions, and destination preexistence. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_research_promotion_rejects_conflicts_and_symlink_escapes: destination parent symlink to outside is rejected without outside write; existing retained file is not overwritten and bytes survive. This is a real local-filesystem security test with no fake agents. Strong invariant: promotion remains beneath references and is non-destructive. Missing source-root symlink/traversal/hardlink/TOCTOU/partial-copy cases. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT, highest security priority; tier T3.

test_regime_resumes_after_campaign_finishes_before_assessment: interrupts final assessment after campaign state is complete but before outcome, verifies pre-state remains executing and resume fills solved outcome/evidence. Defends nonterminal interpretation of complete-without-outcome and avoids campaign rerun implicitly, though no execution invocation counter proves that. Use explicit barrier and counter. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T3.

test_regime_checkpoints_when_a_critical_source_needs_manual_acquisition: fake missing-source marker yields awaiting_sources, source-request schema/title, no campaign state, user message, CLI status=3; adding missing.pdf and resuming reruns research to complete with no missing sources. Defends premature execution and stale research result. Exact title/summary/message and marker are brittle; no validation that supplied bytes match requested source, multiple/optional sources, repeated checkpoint, or policy=continue. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_regime_executes_frozen_pre_campaign_inputs: mutates live problem/reference immediately before original _execute_campaign and verifies snapshot retains original bytes. The test name overclaims: assertions prove snapshot immutability, not that agents actually consumed only those bytes. Add read provenance or fake agent whose output hashes inputs. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T3.

test_concurrent_resume_commits_one_terminal_assessment: two threads resume same run; counted assessment sleeps to widen race; both return same path and only one assessment call occurs. Defends duplicate terminal assessment in one process. Does not test separate processes/hosts, stale locks, duplicate side effects after crash between assessment and commit, or filesystem lock portability. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT with deterministic barrier and multiprocess integration oracle; tier T3.

test_strategy_intent_recovers_missing_and_stale_artifacts: manually establishes awaiting_strategy, injects failure writing strategy-selection, retries, then corrupts selection and next-campaign and retries again; selected strategy and directive are reconstructed, journal receipt appears exactly once, evidence remains valid. Defends crash between durable intent and derived artifacts, idempotency, stale artifact repair, and duplicate receipt. Strong v2 state-machine contract; manual schema_version=2 setup is coupled but intentional. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT, highest crash-consistency priority; tier T3.

test_stop_all_discovers_fixed_regime_meta_agent_without_campaign_registration: real sleeper subprocess and registries; fake sandbox preparation/termination and fake unit terminator; stop-all reports PID/unit and clears registration, blocked thread exits with RegimeError. Defends orphaned fixed meta-agent discovery. POSIX-only chmod/shebang, timing poll, and mocked systemd limit portability/claim. Keep Linux integration oracle and add stale/PID-reuse protections. KEEP_AS_INTEGRATION_ORACLE; tier T3.

test_blind_benchmark_scores_outcome_without_leaking_expectation: real benchmark/controller with fake agents; exact summary scoring and prompt literal scan. Defends obvious expected_outcome prompt leak and scoring regression. Scan is underinclusive and exact summary is schema-coupled. Port taint-based all-input leak test plus schema score test. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT/REWRITE; tier T2.

test_blind_benchmark_records_case_error_and_continues: mocked RegimeRunner raises first, verifies running checkpoint before second, fabricates blocked outcome, and checks final counts/error text. Defends fail-fast loss of subsequent cases and absent incremental report. Does not cover BaseException/interruption policy, malformed outcomes, atomic report writes, or sensitive error redaction. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT; tier T2.

test_blind_benchmark_resumes_only_unrecorded_cases: first case is checkpointed, second raises RunnerInterrupted, resume invokes exactly once, retains started_at/order, and completes accepted. Defends duplicate reruns and report replacement. Fixed fake run paths assume clean fixture. Missing partial/in-progress case semantics and changed runtime options. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT; tier T2.

test_blind_benchmark_resume_rejects_modified_suite: interruption creates report; appending a comment causes resume rejection. Proves byte digest pinning, not semantic change detection. Decide v2 contract explicitly: byte-identical provenance versus semantic canonical digest. REWRITE; tier T1.

test_regime_rejects_plan_above_phase_budget: parsed schema-v3 plan has one 4000-second pilot task and is rejected. Defends hard phase budget bypass. It does not establish exact boundary, aggregate formula, max_attempt multiplication, optional tasks, or every phase. Convert to table/property tests. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT; tier T1.

test_regime_requires_regression_fit_to_descend_from_assessment: valid assess→fit dependency passes; absent edge fails. Defends fit running independently of prerequisite assessment. It does not test transitive descent, task/capability mismatch, cycles, wrong phase, assessment failure gating, or command spoofing through instruction text. MUST_PORT_CONTRACT with graph-policy expansion; tier T1.

failure_modes: The Lean/build/verification success test mocks every command and evidence validation; it proves command construction/parsing, not that Lean accepts the generated contract or that commands are safely executed.
Exact generated Lean source and argv-order assertions are brittle to harmless formatting, qualification, batching, temporary-file placement, and command-runner changes.

The axiom parser is tested only for a missing report count; forbidden axioms, duplicate theorem lines, unexpected theorem names, reordered/noisy output, qualified declarations, ANSI output, parser spoofing, and allowed-set exactness are absent.
contract_preserved=false rejection is only a declared boolean check; it cannot detect semantically weakened theorem types, altered success manifests, misleading directives, or optimizer dishonesty.

The main autonomous-loop test uses a fake RegimeRunner, fake validation, and fake optimizer; it does not prove real regime resume, proof build, evidence validity, subprocess safety, or user approval behavior.
Private helper calls and hand-built state dictionaries couple tests to v1 state shape and can bypass public validation/journal paths.
Old fixed timestamps depend on the current date remaining after year 2000 and do not test monotonic-vs-wall-clock changes, malformed timestamps, exact boundary, or timezone handling.
Resumability is inferred from one pre-campaign state field; missing/corrupt journals/artifacts, terminal campaign state, unknown schema versions, and safe rejection are untested.

No tests cover session journal tampering, concurrent resume, exactly-once round creation, crash points around campaign/analysis/decision commits, max_campaigns, consecutive failures, operator decisions, cancellation, or stop semantics.

Success workspace/path security is untested: symlink/junction escape, required_artifact traversal, command working directory, inherited environment/secrets, executable substitution, and carried-forward workspace provenance.
Portability assumptions include TOML/UTF-8 paths, local atomic filesystem behavior, executable names lake/python, Lean output grammar, case-sensitive module names, and command availability.

cross_cutting: Highest-value production invariants are: strict bounded validation; no fit after negative assessment; train-only preprocessing; deterministic/auditable partitioning; transactional output; symlink-safe bounded ingestion; artifact hash manifest; explicit planner capability disposition; assessment-before-fit DAG; and replayable optional-backend artifacts.

No test exposes a race harness. Symlink checks are single-threaded and only final/root components; they do not prove protection against check-then-open/check-then-create replacement. V2 should prefer directory/file descriptors, no-follow flags where portable, atomic temp creation, containment verification, and adversarial replacement tests.

Hash tests establish deterministic input hashes in limited representations and artifact digest consistency/tamper observability. They do not establish canonicalization across dtype/endianness/version, authenticate receipts, verify hashes automatically before consumption, or protect against receipt+artifact replacement.

Several names overclaim: 'shape agnostic' omits 1D and many shapes; 'without fitting' lacks a fitter spy; 'every ... dimension' is not exhaustive; 'artifact hashes' does not inspect hashes; 'train-only scaling' checks only feature mean; 'seed controls only partition' does not compare nonpartition outputs; 'tampering is detectable' is manual rather than production detection; TensorFlow 'option matrix' is five tuples, not a Cartesian matrix.
Frequent exact English regex/stdout assertions are brittle unless messages are a supported CLI contract. Prefer stable error codes/structured diagnostics and one presentation-level integration test.
Frequent exact dict/set assertions can block additive receipt artifacts/schema evolution. Prefer required-key/subset/schema assertions unless a closed manifest is an explicit invariant.

Real/fake boundary summary: NumPy, JSON, NPZ/text I/O, local filesystems, linear fitting, TensorFlow installed-lane training, and Keras replay are real; CLI is in-process; missing TensorFlow and capability availability are faked; planner validates synthetic plans but executes no tasks; tamper detection is manual.

Portability constraints: symlink tests vary on Windows privilege/reparse semantics; exact TensorFlow determinism varies by TF/Keras/oneDNN/BLAS/compiler/CPU/thread settings; NumPy linear tolerances and NPZ bytes may vary by version; path suffix case behavior and filesystem ordering/case sensitivity vary; direct `main` misses console-script/subprocess behavior; exact error text and set rendering can vary.

Fixture assumptions recur: finite float64, small in-memory arrays, writable local atomic-ish filesystem, no concurrent writers, stable NumPy defaults, UTF-8, sufficient disk, and trusted producer-generated receipt paths. There are no huge decoded payloads, compressed bombs, hostile object arrays, permissions failures, disk-full cases, or process interruption.

There is no explicit overwrite/idempotency contract for existing output directories, no concurrency test for two fits sharing an output, no cleanup test after mid-write failure, and no verifier that rejects altered artifacts before replay.

Recommendation and 'not_proof' semantics are valuable safety labels: a regression recommendation is exploratory and must not be elevated to formal proof. Tests check labels but do not test downstream enforcement of proof-status restrictions.

Priority: P0 security/transactionality/data leakage/config bypass/plan ordering; P1 receipt schema/hash verification/replay/CLI exit semantics/recommendation policy; P2 format compatibility/catalog presentation; P3 exact stdout/error prose and same-process byte determinism.

`sample_arrays(samples=60)`: deterministic float64 fixture; `linspace` and trigonometric second feature avoid trivial collinearity, while targets are exact affine combinations of both features. Hidden assumptions: `samples >= 2`, NumPy float64, stable linear algebra, and recommendation threshold. It does not represent noise, rank deficiency, integer/object dtypes, extreme magnitudes, one-dimensional inputs, or non-contiguous arrays.

`test_assessment_is_shape_agnostic_and_deterministic`: title overclaims shape agnosticism; only one fixed 60x2/60x2 shape and list-vs-ndarray representation are exercised. Assertions prove dimensions, recommendation, equal hashes across those two representations, and exact evidence class. They do not prove hash stability across dtype, endianness, memory layout, NaN payload, process, NumPy version, or serialization version. Exact evidence-class text is a schema contract if public, otherwise brittle vocabulary coupling.

`test_assessment_reports_invalid_numeric_content_without_fitting`: proves returned diagnostics (`recommended=False`, one nonfinite feature scalar, constant target index 1, warning substring). It does not prove 'without fitting': no fitter/backend is spied on, and assessment may do arbitrary fitting internally. NaN and constant target are combined, so no independent recommendation test identifies which defect gates fitting. Warning substring is presentation-coupled. Missing cases: ±inf, NaN target, all-constant features, multiple bad columns, nonfinite count semantics, warning ordering, and immutable input.

`test_config_rejects_unbounded_or_unknown_settings`: protects patience<=epochs, strict unknown-key rejection (mitigating silent typo/config-injection), and hidden-layer count 1..6. Regexes couple to English error text. It samples rather than exhausts bounds and does not test equality at the boundary, negative epochs, bool-as-int, duplicate TOML keys, non-mapping input, or default consistency. 'unbounded or unknown settings' is broader than the three cases.

`test_linear_fit_retains_baseline_split_metrics_and_artifact_hashes`: real fit and real filesystem, twice. Status/proof/backend assertions establish receipt semantics. Validation count/method plus retained indices establish ordered split for this fixture, but training indices and disjoint/exhaustive partition are not checked here. RMSE≈0 relies on exact linear fixture and float64 solver tolerance. Repeated metric/split equality proves same-process repeatability only, not artifact-byte reproducibility. Exact artifact path set forbids additive artifacts. Title falsely claims artifact hashes: neither hash fields nor file bytes are checked. It also does not prove history/NPZ existence independently beyond opening NPZ, receipt atomicity, overwrite policy, target scaling, predictions, or receipt-to-artifact consistency.

line_findings: Imports: `hashlib` is used only for external digest recomputation; `Any` weakens receipt typing and signals no schema object is used. `regression_module` enables private-constant/import-finder monkeypatches, creating source-layout coupling.

Hypothesis settings: 40 examples and no deadline reduce flakes for numerical/filesystem work but provide no exhaustive boundary guarantee. Seeds are only 0..65536, dimensions are modest, and generated normals are almost surely finite/nonconstant.

`test_assessment_preserves_arbitrary_valid_shapes_and_is_deterministic`: exercises samples 3..100, features 1..8, targets 1..4, ndarray vs nested-list hashes, and the exact recommendation formula. It does not cover 1D normalization because generated arrays are always 2D, despite 'arbitrary valid shapes'; nor dtype/layout/large dimensions/nonfinite values. Formula equality is a strong policy contract but brittle if v2 intentionally changes thresholds. Different seeds are data seeds, not proof of cross-process hash stability.

`test_array_contract_rejects_invalid_shapes_and_types`: six valuable negative classes. The first uses 2D features and 1D targets with two samples; the second mismatches 3 vs 2; third rejects feature rank 3; fourth exercises string-to-float failure; fifth/sixth reject zero feature/target width. Error regexes are English-source brittle. Missing: scalar/0D, ragged lists, complex, object arrays, structured dtypes, datetime, masked arrays, sparse matrices, target rank 3, nonfinite values, overflow during conversion, enormous dimensions, and input mutation.

`test_config_rejects_every_unbounded_or_unknown_dimension`: title overclaims 'every'; it samples model_kind, hidden layer value/count, epoch type/max, batch min, NaN learning rate, validation min, split enum, L1 min, seed min, device enum. It omits activation/loss/optimizer enums, upper/lower boundaries for many fields, L2, patience interactions, float infinities, strings, None, mapping subclasses, and unknown keys (covered elsewhere). Exact message fragments are brittle. Security value is high because bool/NaN are classic validation bypasses.

`test_fit_revalidates_direct_dataclass_construction`: proves defense in depth for `epochs=0` despite valid model_kind. It does not prove every dataclass field is revalidated or that immutable/frozen configuration prevents post-validation mutation.

`test_fit_rejects_a_negative_assessment`: proves fit's policy gate on a nine-sample finite fixture and domain error. It does not establish which recommendation reasons are fatal, whether an override exists, or that no output is touched/created before rejection.

`test_load_array_rejects_final_symlink`: real final-component symlink. Protects against straightforward file redirection. It does not cover symlinked parent directories, hard links, junctions/reparse points, file replacement between check/open (TOCTOU), relative dangling links, FIFO/socket/device files, or descriptor-based race resistance.

`test_output_rejects_final_symlink_without_touching_target`: proves an existing final directory symlink is rejected and target remains empty in this single-threaded case. It does not prove race safety between validation and mkdir/open, protect symlink parents, handle preexisting real output, or preserve a nonempty target. Error wording 'regular directory' is awkward/source-coupled.

`test_candidate_discovery_does_not_follow_symlink_root`: establishes fail-closed behavior for a root that itself is a symlink. It does not test symlink children inside a real root, recursive traversal, hard links, permission errors, loops, mount boundaries, or concurrent replacement.

`test_config_loader_rejects_undocumented_suffix`: protects explicit parser selection and avoids parsing JSON from `.txt`. Only lowercase `.txt` is tested; uppercase suffixes, no suffix, multiple suffixes, symlinks, size limits, encoding/BOM, malformed JSON/TOML, and parser confusion remain.

`test_loader_rejects_oversized_input_before_parsing`: private byte limit is reduced to five and a ten-byte invalid NPY is rejected with 'exceeds'. The distinct error strongly suggests the size guard wins, but no parser spy proves parsing was never entered. It does not test exact-limit acceptance, stat/read growth races, compressed NPZ expansion bombs, sparse files, streamed text size, or integer overflow.

`test_loader_round_trips_every_documented_format`: parameterization gives one 6x2 finite float fixture per suffix; NPZ key is explicit. It proves happy-path compatibility, not parser safety. `np.array_equal` enforces exact values for these integers-as-floats. Missing uppercase extensions, 1D arrays, scientific notation, quoted CSV, blank lines, JSON top-level validation, malformed/truncated files, object/pickle arrays, compressed archives, multiple NPZ members, duplicate names, encoding and locale.

`test_csv_header_skip_and_npz_key_failures`: confirms one skipped header row and explicit ambiguity/missing-key errors. It does not test negative/excessive/noninteger `skip_rows`, headers without skip, key type/path traversal-like strings, zero-array NPZ, corrupt ZIP, or whether archive handles close after error.

`test_linear_receipt_is_self_consistent_and_uses_train_only_scaling`: verifies partition disjointness/exhaustiveness/order; feature mean uses training rows; retained `actual` aligns and 1D target becomes `(n,1)`; every listed artifact's current size/hash matches receipt. Title exceeds exercise: only feature mean—not feature scale, target mean/scale, baseline/model fitting—is checked for train-only computation; 'self-consistent' omits predictions, metrics, config, input hashes, unlisted files, duplicate paths, path traversal, receipt signature, and receipt's own integrity. Iterating receipt-provided paths without containment checks would be unsafe in a verifier test, though producer output is trusted here.

`test_random_split_seed_controls_only_the_partition`: proves equal seeds yield equal validation index lists and seed 8 differs from seed 7 for one dataset. It does not prove the seed controls only partition: metrics, model coefficients, artifact bytes, or non-split randomness are not compared. Different seeds can coincidentally produce the same split generally, so inequality is fixture/algorithm-specific and brittle. No cross-process/version determinism is shown.

`test_failed_backend_leaves_no_partial_output`: fake dependency absence, real path assertion. Proves no new output path remains after this early failure. It does not exercise failures after directory creation/artifact writes, rollback of a preexisting output, temp-directory cleanup, fsync/rename atomicity, process kill, disk-full, permission errors, concurrent readers/writers, or actual TensorFlow import failure.

`test_cli_negative_assessment_retains_report_and_returns_three`: strong distinction between scientific non-recommendation and software failure. Proves direct-main return 3, JSON persisted false, stdout substring. Missing stderr/JSON schema, preexisting output behavior, partial-write safety, subprocess exit propagation, and positive/negative mixed warnings. Exact stdout is presentation brittle.

`test_receipt_tampering_is_detectable_from_retained_hashes`: appends bytes to a valid NPZ and manually observes digest mismatch. It proves the manifest contains a prior digest sufficient for detection, not that production detects/rejects tampering; no verifier is called. Appending may leave NPZ readable, which usefully models stealthy trailing-byte mutation. Missing size check, history/model tampering, receipt tampering, swapped artifacts, truncation, path substitution, algorithm tagging, signatures/MACs, and automatic fail-closed consumption.

Formatting/type annotations have no directly asserted runtime behavior. Test names repeatedly make stronger universal claims than their bounded examples; v2 corpus labels should separate `proves` from `motivates`.

failure_modes: Governance omission: planner silently ignores offered capabilities or duplicates decisions.
Capability spoofing: plan names an unregistered model/capability.
Availability bypass: task selects an unavailable backend/capability.
Non-executable plan: instructions vaguely say 'assess' or name an API/CLI without a permitted execution tool.
Provenance collapse: fitting occurs without prior assessment, fit and assessment are conflated into one task, or dependency order does not preserve assessment-before-fit.
Schema semantic drift between catalog, plan parser, and regime policy.

invariants: Plan schema requires capability_decisions and capability names are unique.
Every catalog capability has exactly one decision; unknown extra capability decisions are rejected.
Explicit skip decisions for both regression capabilities are valid.
A capability marked unavailable by the catalog cannot be selected for use.
A used capability must map to a task that names its recognized CLI or Python API and has an execution-capable tool.
Python API invocation with `eval` is accepted.
regression_fit may be used only when regression_assess is also used.
Assessment and fit must be assigned separate task IDs.
Fit must depend directly or transitively on assessment; one intervening audit task is accepted.
line_findings: Imports: `io.StringIO` suppresses/captures runner output but no output is asserted. Monkeypatching `regime_module.regression_capability_catalog` and calling `_validate_plan_policy` are intentional white-box seams and v2 migration liabilities.

`runner_fixture`: writes a minimal real project with schema_version 1 and fixed resource/tool limits, creates references/knowledge and a pre-workspace input directory, then mutates `runner.pre_workspace` directly. Hidden assumptions: TOML parser, POSIX-like paths, private mutable runner state, all named tools are valid, source checkpoint policy bypasses unrelated setup, and project schema v1 remains supported. Numeric fixture content is never read by these policy tests.

Manifest limits (`max_tasks=6`, `max_parallel=3`, etc.) are fixture plumbing, not tested contracts; failures caused by these limits could mask policy behavior. `allowed_tools` constrains test task validity.

`task` helper: creates required pilot tasks with fixed metadata, timeout, one attempt, abort policy, and default read tool. `depends_on or []` and `tools or ['read']` prevent representing an intentionally empty tool list, a hidden fixture bug. No helper validation is independently tested.

`plan` helper: parses schema v3, derives max_parallel from task count, creates one obligation evidenced by the final task, and assumes tasks is nonempty (`tasks[-1]`). Strategy portfolio is empty. This means all policy tests also depend on OrchestrationPlan's unrelated schema constraints.
`skipped_decisions`: canonical explicit skip fixture with human rationale. Exact rationale content is not validated by these tests, so it should not be learned as required wording.
`use_decision`: maps capability to task with a stock rationale; again, rationale quality/truth is not exercised.

`test_plan_schema_requires_unique_explicit_capability_decisions`: first proves omission of the field fails; second inserts the same assess-skip object twice and proves duplicate capability failure. It does not test empty list, duplicate with conflicting decisions/task IDs, malformed decision, duplicate unknown capability, case normalization, or whether all catalog entries are required at parse time versus policy time. Error regexes are brittle.

`test_policy_accepts_explicit_skips`: proves the minimal plan can decline both capabilities. It does not prove rationale is nonempty/substantive, task_id must be null for skips, or skipped capabilities are not invoked at runtime.

`test_policy_rejects_unknown_or_missing_catalog_decisions`: proves one missing regression_fit and one extra unregistered_model fail, via message substrings containing set-rendered facts. It does not test simultaneous missing+extra, catalog duplicates, catalog order, dynamic catalog mutation, unavailable skipped items, or exact-match normalization. Regex can be brittle if set formatting changes.

`test_policy_rejects_unavailable_capability`: clones real catalog, assumes entry zero is regression_assess, marks it unavailable, and monkeypatches provider. `catalog[0]` is order brittle and could disable the wrong capability. Proves policy rejection before execution, not that runtime invocation also checks availability or why unavailable. Only assess is covered, not fit.

`test_policy_requires_named_callable_and_execution_tool`: three cases jointly distinguish vague bash instructions, named CLI with read-only tool, and named Python API with read-only tool. All expect the same message, so they do not prove diagnostically distinct reasons. The contract is likely substring matching against English instructions and tool names; this is brittle, bypassable via negation/comments, aliases, casing, shell wrappers, or mentioning both APIs without invocation. Test title says 'execution tool' but only bash/eval versus read are sampled.

`test_policy_accepts_python_api_invocation`: lexical mention `assess_regression` plus eval is accepted. It does not prove generated code calls the API, arguments are safe, outputs are retained, or eval authorization is scoped.
`test_fit_requires_used_assessment`: fit-use plus assess-skip is rejected. It does not test assess missing, unavailable, assigned to nonexistent task, or failed at runtime.

`test_fit_and_assessment_must_be_separate_tasks`: same task ID for both is rejected even though instructions mention both CLI commands. This protects stage separation/auditability; it does not prove separate output locations, agents, receipts, or temporal order.

`test_fit_accepts_transitive_assessment_dependency`: proves one transitive chain assessment→audit→fit is accepted. It does not explicitly test fit with no dependency or wrong direction in this file, direct dependency, multiple paths, cycles, missing nodes, optional/failed assessment, or dependency closure implementation on deeper/wider graphs. Acceptance proves policy allows transitivity, not runtime scheduler order.
No test actually runs regression assessment/fit, agent tools, or planner execution; claims are restricted to preflight plan acceptance/rejection.

`RegimeRunner._validate_plan_policy` is a private implementation method, so these are policy-unit/integration hybrids coupled to class internals.
Capability availability is faked by monkeypatching the catalog function in `regime_module`; all other catalog behavior is real.
Task/plan helpers synthesize schema-valid dictionaries; OrchestrationPlan parsing is real.
Instruction validation appears lexical/source-text based; no command AST, tool invocation, or runtime evidence is tested.

Keep one end-to-end planner integration oracle after unitizing schema/catalog/dependency rules.

Backend provenance corruption: wrong name/version/config recorded.
Serialization corruption: `.keras` model cannot reload or replay predictions consistent with retained artifact.
Scaling mismatch: producer and replay consumer use incompatible feature/target normalization or output shape.
NaN/Inf training results silently retained.
Comparison semantic drift: boolean does not implement strict lower mean held-out RMSE.
Nondeterministic initialization/training/split under the supported same-process CPU environment.

invariants: Each of five exercised activation/loss/optimizer tuples can train one epoch on CPU and emit finite train/validation losses.
Receipt records TensorFlow backend/version and selected option values.
TensorFlow fit retains history.json, model.keras, and validation-results.npz.
Saved Keras model reloads and reproduces retained unscaled validation predictions after applying retained feature and target scaling.
Prediction shape is 12x2 and values are finite.
Receipt's baseline comparison boolean equals strict model mean-RMSE < baseline mean-RMSE.
For one two-layer configuration, repeated same-process CPU fits with seed 77 have equal metric dictionaries, split metadata, byte-identical history JSON, and exactly equal retained predictions.
line_findings: `pytest.importorskip('tensorflow')` runs at module import/collection and skips every test if unavailable. This is appropriate optional-lane behavior but can hide total loss of coverage in default CI; lane policy must require a non-skipped run somewhere. Import occurs before campaign_builder imports and can initialize global TensorFlow state.

`nonlinear_arrays(samples=48)`: deterministic three-feature/two-target nonlinear float64 fixture with 12-row quarter holdout. It is smooth and small, with no noise, constants, missing values, extremes, rank pathologies, or distribution shift. Default sample count is assumed by the asserted `(12,2)` shape.

Option parameterization is five hand-picked tuples, not a Cartesian 'option matrix': relu/mse/adam, tanh/mae/rmsprop, elu/huber/sgd, gelu/mse/adam, sigmoid/mae/rmsprop. Therefore failures in untested combinations or individual options paired differently are not covered.

`test_tensorflow_option_matrix_trains_and_retains_replayable_model`: uses one hidden layer of six units, one epoch, batch 12, learning rate .005, ordered/default split assumptions, seed 101, and requested CPU. One epoch minimizes cost but does not exercise early stopping despite patience=1, convergence, checkpoint selection, regularization, batching remainders, or long-run stability.

Backend name/version and echoed config assertions prove receipt provenance fields, but exact `tf.__version__` only proves producer used the currently imported package string; build hash, Keras version, Python/NumPy ABI, device, deterministic-op settings, and dependency lock are absent.

Exact artifact path set is brittle against additive artifacts and does not check size/hash fields or absence of partial/temp files. Conversely it is useful if the artifact bundle is intentionally closed-schema.

History assertions prove exactly one loss and val_loss entry and finite values. They do not test other metrics, epoch numbering, JSON numeric precision, empty validation, callback behavior, or that receipt metrics derive from this history.

`tf.keras.models.load_model` is a real serialization check. Replay applies retained feature mean/scale and target scale/mean, then compares to retained model_prediction at 1e-6. This strongly validates artifact/scaler interoperability for same-version same-process load. It does not compare predictions to actual targets, recompute receipt RMSE, check zero scales, validate training-only origin of scalers, or test a clean subprocess/cross-version consumer.
Shape `(12,2)` is fixture-coupled; a semantic assertion based on validation count/target count would be less brittle. Finite prediction assertion is valuable.

Comparison equality proves the receipt boolean implements strict `<` on two stored means. It does not prove either metric was correctly computed from retained actual/prediction values, handle NaN/ties/tolerances, or validate selected_model/criterion fields.

`test_tensorflow_seed_reproduces_history_metrics_and_predictions`: two sequential fits in one initialized process with identical config. Equal receipt metric dicts/split, byte-identical history, and exact array equality are much stronger than most TensorFlow portability guarantees and likely brittle across TensorFlow/Keras/oneDNN/BLAS/compiler/CPU versions. They prove only this environment and execution order, not fresh-process, parallel, GPU, thread-count, or cross-host reproducibility.

The seed test does not reload the model, compare model file bytes/weights, compare artifact hashes, or assert different seeds differ. Global TensorFlow state may carry across runs, so same-process equality is not equivalent to isolated reproducibility.

No test covers installed-but-broken TensorFlow, unsupported version, import errors after `find_spec`, GPU denial, OOM, interrupted save, model deserialization security, custom objects, older/newer `.keras` compatibility, or concurrent fits to the same output.
files.model_tier: T3_LARGE for reproducing/debugging cross-version TensorFlow determinism, Keras serialization, hardware kernels, and numerical drift; T2_MEDIUM for routine pinned-lane assertion maintenance.
files.purpose: Optional real-backend integration oracle for TensorFlow dense-regression configuration compatibility, model retention/replay, receipt comparison semantics, and seeded same-process repeatability.
tests_or_consumers: TensorFlow is a real optional dependency and test collection is skipped wholesale when absent; this is not core-CI proof unless a dedicated ML lane installs it.
Keras training, serialization, loading, prediction, NumPy artifacts, and local filesystem are real.
`device='cpu'` requests CPU, but the test does not independently assert no GPU kernels/device placement are used.
Fixture is deterministic, small, nonlinear, float64 on NumPy input; TensorFlow may cast internally according to backend defaults.
Model is replayed in the same Python process and TensorFlow version that created it; cross-version/process/platform portability is not exercised.
files.v2_disposition: KEEP_AS_INTEGRATION_ORACLE — retain in an optional pinned TensorFlow CPU lane, relax unjustified byte/exact determinism, add subprocess replay and compatibility metadata, and supplement with faster backend-adapter contract tests. Do not make it the sole proof of the v2 model artifact contract.

unknowns: Production source is absent, so inferred invariants may reflect tests rather than documented product requirements; especially recommendation thresholds, closed artifact sets, message text, and catalog order.
It is unknown whether receipt hashes include algorithm identifiers, whether receipt writing itself is atomic, or whether a separate production verifier exists outside these imports.
It is unknown whether `assess_regression` internally fits anything; the v1 test title does not prove it avoids fitting.
It is unknown whether fit validation computes all scalers from training data; only retained feature mean is checked.
It is unknown whether path code uses race-resistant descriptor operations or merely `is_symlink`/`is_file`; single-threaded outcomes cannot distinguish them.
It is unknown whether output directories are allowed to preexist, be resumed, or be overwritten, and what concurrent-fit semantics are intended.
It is unknown whether split algorithm/version stability is a public reproducibility guarantee or only same-release determinism.
It is unknown whether CLI English output and exit code 3 are documented external API guarantees; JSON and exit semantics appear more durable than prose.
It is unknown whether planner instruction matching is intentionally lexical or a temporary implementation; tests imply accepted strings but do not establish security against deceptive text.
It is unknown which OS/filesystems and Python/NumPy/TensorFlow versions v2 must support, which determines symlink behavior and numerical tolerance policy.
It is unknown whether TensorFlow models must replay across versions/processes/architectures or only within the producing environment.
No historical incident descriptions accompany the files, so exact incident causality—versus proactive coverage—cannot be distinguished from test code alone.
v2_requirements: P0: Define a public, versioned regression contract: accepted array ranks/dtypes, normalization, finite-value policy, minimum dimensions, recommendation formula or policy version, and immutable input behavior.

P0: Centralize strict configuration schema validation and invoke it from parse, load, and fit; reject bool-as-int, NaN/Inf, unknown keys, invalid interactions, and all documented boundary violations with stable machine-readable error codes.
P0: Make fit reject non-recommended assessments before creating output or initializing a backend; test each rejection cause independently and use a backend spy to prove no fit/import side effect.

P0: Implement race-resistant input/output handling: reject non-regular files, symlinks/reparse points according to a documented policy, secure parent traversal, bounded reads, atomic temp-directory writes and rename/commit, rollback after failures at every stage, and safe behavior for preexisting outputs/concurrent writers.

P0: Prove preprocessing uses training rows only for feature mean/scale and target mean/scale; prove model and baseline fitting exclude validation rows; recompute predictions and metrics from retained arrays.

P0: Add a public artifact/receipt verifier that validates schema, containment-safe paths, unique paths, size, digest algorithm/digest, and all artifacts before loading; tests must mutate, truncate, swap, remove, and alter receipt entries and assert fail-closed behavior.

P0: Replace lexical planner instruction inference with structured invocation metadata (`interface`, `command/api`, arguments, output/evidence contract, authorized tool). Preserve exact catalog disposition, availability, separate assess/fit tasks, and transitive dependency validation through a public validator.

P1: Version receipt and retained NPZ schemas; specify required versus extensible fields, `not_proof` semantics, comparison tie/NaN rules, split rounding, target 1D normalization, scaler zero-variance behavior, and artifact set extensibility.

P1: Property-test 1D and 2D arrays across safe integer/float dtypes, layouts, boundaries, finite/nonfinite combinations, and recommendation thresholds. Add malformed/ragged/object/complex/scalar/rank>2 negatives and input nonmutation checks.

P1: Expand loader security: exact size-boundary tests, stat/read growth race, decompression ratio/expanded-size limits, `allow_pickle=False`, corrupt/truncated archives, zero/multiple NPZ members, CSV/JSON malformed and encoding cases, and resource closure.

P1: Test random/ordered partitions for disjointness, exhaustiveness, size/rounding, same-seed stability under a documented algorithm version, and changed-seed statistical behavior without requiring every pair to differ.

P1: Run CLI through the installed subprocess entry point for success, scientific-negative exit 3, operational errors, stdout/stderr separation, output atomicity, and paths with spaces/non-ASCII characters; retain direct-main tests only for speed.
P1: Require a dedicated optional-ML CI lane so `importorskip` cannot silently eliminate all TensorFlow coverage; pin supported TF/Keras/NumPy ranges and record build/device/determinism metadata.

P1: TensorFlow replay must occur in a fresh subprocess/environment from the saved model and retained scalers. Compare within documented numerical tolerances, recompute metrics, and test supported version compatibility. Treat exact-byte/history equality as nonportable unless a fully pinned runtime guarantees it.

P2: Generate table-driven config tests from the schema to cover min/max inclusive and just-outside values for every field and every enum; retain a small hand-written adversarial set for bool/NaN/Inf/unknown keys/inter-field constraints.

P2: Test capability discovery on nested files, symlink children, inaccessible entries, ordering, uppercase suffixes, generated-output exclusion, and platform path behavior; consume catalog by capability ID rather than list position.
P2: Introduce stable error codes and structured warning codes; minimize regex assertions on English prose and stdout.
P2: Separate pure policy/unit tests from a small end-to-end oracle that creates a plan, executes assessment then fit, and verifies retained evidence/proof-status propagation.

method.excluded: Generated Lean .lake IR/package trees, binaries, PDFs/HTML rendering bytes, stdout/stderr logs, copied input-snapshot/frozen-input/recovery duplicates, caches, and raw files outside the explicit maintained/run patterns. component_map: `config.py` — v1 campaign configuration authority. Public boundary: `ConfigurationError`; enums `CampaignMode`, `ApprovalPolicy`, `FailurePolicy`, `InputStrategy`; frozen/slotted DTOs `CampaignInput`, `StageSpec`, `HandoffSpec`, `PublishSpec`, `ExecutionSpec`, `TargetSpec`, `ObligationSpec`, `CampaignSpec`. Entry points are `CampaignSpec.load(path)`, `CampaignSpec.load_resolved(path)`, `CampaignSpec.to_resolved_dict(...)`, `CampaignSpec.by_id`, `CampaignSpec.stage_order`, `ExecutionSpec.from_table(...)`, and `ExecutionSpec.to_dict()`. Internal validation boundaries `_validate_handoff`, `_validate_stages`, `_reject_inline_secret_values` are part of current behavior. External schemas are campaign TOML `schema_version=1` and resolved campaign JSON also `schema_version=1`, despite incompatible shapes.

`project.py` — strict project/autonomy configuration. Public boundary: `ComputeProfile.parse`, `LeanTheoremSpec.parse`, `AutonomySuccessSpec.parse`, `AutonomySpec.parse`, `ProjectInput.parse`, `ProjectSpec.load`, `ProjectSpec.with_compute_profile`, `ProjectSpec.thinking_for`, `ProjectSpec.root`. External project TOML is `schema_version=1`. It imports `ConfigurationError` and `ExecutionSpec` from `config.py`, coupling project schema behavior to campaign execution defaults and parser defects.

`models.py` — model-produced artifact contracts. Public parsers/types: `load_json_object`; `ResearchDecision.parse`; `MissingSource.parse`; `ResearchResult.parse`; `PlanStrategy.parse`; `PlanObligation.parse`; `PlanTask.parse`; `CapabilityDecision.parse`; `OrchestrationPlan.parse` and lookup properties; `ContinuationDecision.parse_text`; `Strategy.parse`; `ObligationDisposition.parse`; `KnowledgePromotion.parse`; `CampaignOutcome.parse` and `CampaignOutcome.validate_against`. External versions are research decision v1, research result v1, orchestration plan v3, continuation decision v1, campaign outcome v2; nested records have no independent versions.

`handoff.py` — trust-boundary prompt/validation dispatch. Public boundary: `handoff_prompt_contract(schema)`, `ResearchHandoff.load(path)`, `digest_handoff(path, schema, source_digests=None)`, `ReviewDecision.parse(text)`, and DTOs `SourceRecord`, `ClaimRecord`, `DefinitionRecord`, `ObligationRecord`. Registered schema strings are exactly `research-v1`, `claim-proposals-v1`, `claim-verdicts-v1`, and `semantic-review-v1`. It dispatches to `claims.ClaimProposalBundle.load`, `claims.ClaimVerdictBundle.load`, and `semantic.SemanticReview.load`.

`artifacts.py` — retained file publication and evidence completeness. Public boundary: frozen/slotted `Artifact(path, sha256, size)` and `Artifact.to_dict()`, `utc_now()`, `atomic_write_text`, `atomic_write_json`, `digest_file`, `digest_tree`, `verify_evidence_index`, `verify_evidence_for_repair`. `evidence.json` is exact-key schema v1 with top-level `schema_version,campaign_id,status,generated_at,artifacts` and artifact `path,sha256,size`.

`journal.py` — advisory-lock-protected JSONL full-state snapshot chain. Public boundary: `JournalError`, frozen/slotted `JournalState(state, sequence, repaired_truncated_tail)`, `append_state_snapshot`, `load_state_snapshot`, `journal_path`. `events.jsonl` records are exact schema v1 with `schema_version,sequence,at,previous_sha256,kind,reason,state,sha256`; `kind` is `state_snapshot`. It claims authority, but `inspection.py` reads `state.json` instead.

`claims.py` — strict claim proposal/verdict DTOs and deterministic ledger construction. Public boundary: `ClaimProposal.parse`, `ClaimProposalBundle.load`, `.by_alias`, `.topological_order`, `ClaimVerdict.parse`, `ClaimVerdictBundle.load`, `.by_claim`, and `build_claim_ledger(...)`. Proposal and verdict handoffs are schema v1; produced claim ledger is schema v2 with `campaign_id,status,required_targets,claims,evidence,deterministic_receipts,verifier_disagreements`.

`semantic.py` — strict semantic-review parser. Public boundary: `SemanticRelation`, `SemanticReview.load`, `SemanticReview.issues`, `SemanticReview.to_dict`. Input handoff is exact schema v1. `to_dict()` omits `schema_version`, so it is not a valid round-trip serializer for `SemanticReview.load`.

`inspection.py` — derived retained-run reporting. Public boundary: `inspect_claim_ledgers(run_dir, verify=True)` producing report schema v1 and `inspect_assurance(run_dir)` producing assurance schema v2. It consumes `state.json` v1, `configuration/features.json` v1, obligations from `configuration/resolved.json`, claim ledgers v1/v2, and `artifacts.verify_evidence_index`. Private retained-path and ledger boundaries are `_safe_retained_path` and `_validate_ledger`.

`metrics.py` — derived compute accounting. Public boundary: frozen/slotted `InvocationMetric` and `.to_dict()`, `collect_compute_metrics(run_dir, plan)`, `write_compute_ledger(run_dir, plan, project, outcome=None)`. It consumes request/receipt/output files plus `OrchestrationPlan`, `ProjectSpec`, and optional `CampaignOutcome`; it emits `compute-ledger.json` schema v1.

`agent_runner.py` — OMP attempt CLI and independent supervisor. CLI is `dossier-agent-runner --request PATH`; `main` currently returns 0/1/2 for success/completed-nonsuccess/request-or-OS errors, while `RunnerInterrupted` escapes. Request is exact-key but unversioned. Receipt is schema v1 with running and terminal forms. It consumes `ExecutionSpec.from_table`, sandbox/process-registry APIs, `PaneHeartbeat`, and private `command.py` helpers `_process_exited_without_reaping` and `_signal_process_group`.

`command.py` — general subprocess transport. Public boundary: `run_captured_command(...) -> CapturedCommand`; private helpers `_process_exited_without_reaping` and `_signal_process_group` are de facto interfaces because `agent_runner.py` imports them. Visible consumer is `herdr.HerdrClient._run`. It independently duplicates most of `agent_runner.py` supervision.

`process_registry.py` — child process and transient-unit recovery registry. Public DTOs `RegisteredRunUnit`, `RegisteredRunProcess`; unit APIs `register_run_unit`, `registered_run_units`, `unregister_run_unit`; process APIs `register_run_process`, `unregister_run_process`, `registered_run_processes`; discovery compatibility APIs `registered_run_directories`, `remove_dead_run_registrations`. Unit/process records are separate exact schema-v1 JSON forms under runtime subdirectories.

`processes.py` — controller/Herdr registration and shutdown orchestration. Public registration APIs `register_campaign`, `register_workspace_creation`, `clear_workspace_creation`, `register_workspace`, `unregister_campaign`; discovery `registered_workspaces`, `registered_workspace_intents`; shutdown `terminate_run_processes`, `stop_all_campaigns`; report DTOs `RunProcessReport`, `StopReport`. Controller records are another incompatible schema-v1 family stored directly under the runtime root.

`sandbox.py` — Linux policy compiler and cleanup implementation. Public boundary: `SandboxError`, immutable `SandboxInvocation`, `prepare_sandbox`, `terminate_sandbox`, `terminate_sandbox_unit`, `workspace_size_exceeds`, `remove_secret_bearing_files`, `secret_values`, `redact_text`. It consumes `ExecutionSpec` and emits systemd-run plus bubblewrap argv/metadata; actual support depends on Linux, `/proc`, user systemd, and `bwrap`.

`herdr.py` — typed facade for external Herdr CLI. Public boundary: `HerdrClient`, `HerdrError`, `HerdrWorkspace`, `HerdrWorkspaceRecord`; methods `create_workspace`, `list_workspaces`, `split_pane`, `rename_pane`, `run_in_pane`, `close_workspace`. Transport is `command.run_captured_command` with host environment, no sandbox, and no durable child registration.

risks: Critical correctness: `CampaignOutcome.parse` allows `status='solved'` with rejected obligations and empty top-level evidence; inspection can also award claim closure from failed producer stages and formalization assurance from unrelated Lean/semantic stages.

Critical integrity race: `digest_handoff` validates one path read and hashes a second; returned digest may cover unvalidated bytes. Similar verify-then-use races affect evidence, inspection, allowed executables, inputs, publication, registries, and runner artifacts.

Critical authority split: `events.jsonl` is described as authoritative while inspection consumes `state.json`; evidence does not prove equivalence. Shutdown can update journal, projection, and evidence separately.

Critical execution duplication: `agent_runner.py` and `command.py` differ in deadlines, error states, stream/digest semantics, waits, retries, and cleanup. Daemon pump threads may outlive return; stale output/handoff can survive a failed attempt.

Critical control-plane trust: runtime records retain `run_dir`, `systemctl`, and Herdr executable paths later used for execution or state mutation without a demonstrated owned/private/no-symlink registry root.

Critical secret handling: ambient substring scans are incomplete; exact redaction has encoding/short-secret gaps; command digest meaning changes when secrets exist; destructive workspace scans are race-prone and may delete unrelated data or follow swapped paths.

High resume risk: resolved campaign uses the same version number as source, silently reinstates defaults, re-expands environment/HOME-dependent paths, and performs weaker validation than initial load.

High path risk: noncanonical aliases bypass uniqueness/reserved-name checks; source/external paths may escape roots; publish containment is lexical; metrics intentionally follows arbitrary external paths; intermediate symlinks and TOCTOU are widespread.

High registry/recovery risk: split schema-v1 registries have no migration; malformed records are silently skipped; updates/removals lack locks or CAS; leader PID reuse/death can drop surviving descendant ownership; global shutdown races creation and may remain unbounded.

High sandbox risk: policy parsing is not proof of backend enforcement; `systemctl is-active` nonzero is treated as inactive; workspace quotas are polling-based; scans mutate permissions; no capability preflight or live enforcement evidence is shown.

High evidence/authenticity risk: evidence manifests, journal links, claim IDs, and ledgers are unkeyed/self-asserted. They establish limited consistency, not writer authenticity, independent review, or campaign/run anti-replay.

High compute risk: journal append is approximately quadratic over growing full snapshots; supervisors repeatedly traverse workspaces every 250 ms; sandbox hashes executable/manifests per attempt; process pruning repeatedly scans `/proc`; claim evidence is replicated; inspection and metrics reread mutable trees.

High schema evolution risk: many unrelated artifacts use `schema_version=1`, plan uses v3, outcome/ledger/assurance use v2, and some durable objects are unversioned. Exact-key readers lack migration, and scanners can turn version skew into invisible cleanup failure.

Medium compatibility risk: v1 consumers/tests are unknown. Hidden code may depend on private command helpers, magic exit codes 124/125/126, exact error strings, falsey execution coercion, 0600 replacement modes, permissive IDs/paths, or silent registry/metrics skipping.
Medium platform risk: fcntl, `/proc`, pidfd, systemd user units, bubblewrap, directory fsync, and merged `/usr` assumptions are not guarded by a declared/tested platform matrix.

Residual semantic risk: even v2 structural binding cannot itself prove mathematical truth or informal/formal equivalence; authoritative closure still needs deterministic Lean/kernel evidence and appropriately independent expert review.
