Plan boundary: `MathematicalWorkProposalV2` contains mathematical task intent/capability needs; `ExecutionPlanV2.compile(proposal, effective_policy, budget)` assigns registered tools/model tier/deadline/attempts/parallelism/failure behavior and carries source/config/profile digests.

Budget boundary: `BudgetGovernor.preflight` and `BudgetGovernor.authorize_attempt` cover campaigns, tasks, attempts, restarts, parallelism, wall time, token/cost/model tier, disk, and verifier invocations. Denial is a typed controller decision, not model prose.

Execution boundary: `ExecutionSupervisor.run(ExecutionRequestV2) -> ExecutionResultV2`; `ExecutionRequestV2` contains capability handles and attempt nonce, not arbitrary host paths. `ExecutionResultV2` contains typed outcome, native exit/signal, exact monotonic deadline data, byte-stream artifact references/hashes, sandbox attestation, cleanup results, and attempt-scoped output/handoff references.

Secret boundary: `SecretCapability` exposes an opaque FD/credential/mount only to explicitly authorized execution; stream publication uses one declared redaction/encryption hash domain. Secret substring scanning is not authorization.

Resource control boundary: `ResourceLedger` records controller/process/unit/Herdr resources with `record_kind`, boot ID, generation, state, immutable capabilities, and typed errors. APIs use intent/attach/transition/reconcile/CAS-delete; corrupt records are quarantined.

Shutdown boundary: `ShutdownCoordinator.stop_run` and `.stop_all` return versioned phase reports for freeze, unit/process termination, workspace close, reconciliation, state commit, and evidence commit; operations are idempotent and globally deadline-bounded.

Claim boundary: `ClaimProposalBundleV2`, `VerifierVerdictBundleV2(proposal_digest, verifier_identity, execution_attestation)`, `ClaimLedgerV3`, and `ClaimDecisionPolicyV2`. Global content hash, campaign claim instance ID, and decision/evidence hash are separate.

Semantic/Lean boundary: `SemanticReviewV2` and `LeanVerificationReceiptV2` share `target_id`, informal source digest, declaration identity/type digest, toolchain digest, and campaign/run IDs. Semantic authority includes reviewer provenance/independence; Lean authority includes deterministic checker receipt.

Outcome boundary: `CampaignOutcomeV3.derive(plan, claim_ledger, lean_receipts, semantic_reviews, obligation_evidence, approvals)` computes status from the final success predicate; callers do not supply an unconstrained solved label.

Inspection boundary: `inspect_snapshot(VerifiedRunSnapshot) -> AssuranceReportV3` with separate labels for self-consistent, provenance-authenticated, deterministically checked, independently reviewed, semantically matched, mathematically accepted, and campaign-complete.

Compute boundary: `ComputeReceiptV2` is controller-generated/hash-bound with unique invocation/attempt identity, monotonic timing, provider/model/token/tool/Lean usage, and explicit unknowns. `ComputeLedgerV2.derive(snapshot, plan_digest, project_digest, outcome_digest)` emits canonical timestamp-free aggregate content.

Compatibility boundary: `v1_import` package exposes existing symbol-shaped readers and migrations, emits warnings plus a migration report enumerating normalized aliases/defaults/unsupported security assumptions, and writes only v2 artifacts. No v2 runtime path accepts shallow mixed-version objects.
workflows: Campaign source load: `CampaignSpec.load` reads UTF-8 TOML, enforces exact keys and `schema_version=1`, constructs inputs/stages/handoff/publish/execution/targets/obligations, resolves filesystem paths and environment-dependent execution values, validates unique IDs/targets, validates the stage DAG and research/build boundary, checks obligation evidence-stage references, and invokes ambient inline-secret scanning. `CampaignSpec.stage_order` recomputes a deterministic lexicographic topological order.

Resolved campaign round trip: `CampaignSpec.to_resolved_dict(...)` emits effective execution/publish state and injects per-stage instruction paths into `stage.config`; `CampaignSpec.load_resolved` reads the alternate JSON shape also labeled `schema_version=1`. The writer/reader relationship is intentional, but the reader is weaker than `load`: missing execution and optional sections regain current defaults; several path, uniqueness, source-existence, and symlink/excludes checks are absent.

Project effective configuration: `ProjectSpec.load` parses project TOML v1, resolves project-contained paths, parses autonomy and compute profiles, and delegates runtime policy to `ExecutionSpec.from_table`. `ProjectSpec.with_compute_profile` applies non-null overrides via `dataclasses.replace`; it does not revalidate all coupled effective limits or persist distinct effective-profile provenance.

Model plan/outcome flow: `OrchestrationPlan.parse` accepts plan schema v3, validates task/obligation/capability/strategy references, task DAG, phases, continuation-gate ancestry, and caller task/parallel maxima. `CampaignOutcome.parse` accepts outcome schema v2; `CampaignOutcome.validate_against(plan)` checks exact obligation IDs and downstream audit ancestry for promotions, but does not bind evidence to execution or enforce a complete final solved predicate.

Handoff flow: `handoff_prompt_contract(schema)` renders one of four static contracts. `digest_handoff(path, schema, source_digests)` dispatches to `ResearchHandoff.load`, `ClaimProposalBundle.load`, `ClaimVerdictBundle.load`, or `SemanticReview.load`, then separately reads bytes and returns SHA-256. For `research-v1`, optional source-digest membership is checked. The parse-then-reread sequence creates a validation/hash race.

Claim closure: `ClaimProposalBundle.load` validates proposal schema v1 and its DAG; verifier/adjudicator `ClaimVerdictBundle.load` validates verdict schema v1. `build_claim_ledger` derives campaign-scoped claim IDs, applies governing verdict and dependency-blocking rules in topological order, projects required targets, and emits mutable schema-v2 ledger data plus `closed`. Mathematical truth, verifier independence, and evidence provenance are external to this workflow.

Semantic review: `SemanticReview.load` validates exact schema v1, relation vocabulary, and the rule that `equivalent` has no issues while a non-equivalent relation has at least one. It does not bind the review to campaign/target/source/Lean/toolchain identities.

Atomic artifact/evidence flow: `atomic_write_text` writes a same-directory temp file, fsyncs it, replaces the destination, and fsyncs the parent; `atomic_write_json` adds deterministic JSON formatting. `digest_file`/`digest_tree` calculate SHA-256 descriptors. `verify_evidence_index` verifies exact evidence schema, regular non-symlink final files, per-file digest/size, and exact retained non-workspace set completeness; `verify_evidence_for_repair` exempts named controller-owned paths.

Journal flow: `append_state_snapshot` takes `LOCK_EX`, reads and verifies the entire existing JSONL chain, truncates a non-LF tail, appends a canonical full state snapshot with sequence/hash link, and fsyncs. `load_state_snapshot` also takes `LOCK_EX`, can destructively truncate a tail, verifies the full chain, and returns only the latest mutable state mapping.

Inspection flow: `inspect_assurance` first verifies `evidence.json`, then calls `inspect_claim_ledgers(..., verify=False)`, reads `state.json`/features/resolved data by pathname, aggregates claim target statuses and stage-category counts, derives obligation states, and emits profiles/gaps. It does not correlate `state.json` to `events.jsonl`, deeply recompute ledger validity, require a succeeded claim-ledger producer, or pair Lean and semantic artifacts by digest.

Metrics flow: `collect_compute_metrics` discovers request files, silently skips malformed requests, follows request-named receipt/output paths, classifies roles using the caller-supplied current plan, and aggregates durations/output bytes. `write_compute_ledger` combines these metrics with current `ProjectSpec` limits and optional live `CampaignOutcome`, then atomically emits compute-ledger v1.

Agent attempt flow: `agent_runner.execute` parses an unversioned exact-key request, writes a running receipt, constructs OMP argv, optionally prepares a sandbox unit, registers process ownership, pumps/redacts stdout and stderr, polls deadline/workspace size, retries blank exit-0 output in the same mutated workspace, performs destructive secret cleanup, writes bounded logs/output, and commits a terminal receipt. Existing output is not removed on final failure/blank output.

General command flow: `run_captured_command` independently prepares sandbox/registry state, launches a new-session process, pumps bounded decoded streams, polls timeout/workspace, terminates groups/units, runs secret cleanup, and returns `CapturedCommand`. Its timeout, cleanup, capture, and digest semantics differ from `agent_runner`.

Sandbox flow: `prepare_sandbox` resolves the executable/workspace/cwd, filters environment even when unsandboxed, fingerprints executable/manifests, and when sandboxed compiles systemd cgroup properties plus bubblewrap mounts/namespaces. Supervisors poll `workspace_size_exceeds`; after execution they call `remove_secret_bearing_files`.

Crash recovery/shutdown flow: `process_registry.py` stores child/unit identities; `processes.py` stores controller and Herdr creation/workspace state in a separate registry. `stop_all_campaigns` discovers records, stops units/process groups, resolves/closes Herdr workspaces, marks campaign state stopped under `.campaign.lock`, and regenerates evidence. The sequence is not one atomic or resumable state machine.

Herdr flow: `HerdrClient` executes CLI commands via `run_captured_command`, parses a loose JSON `result` envelope for create/list/split/rename/close, and uses a distinct zero-exit-only contract for `run_in_pane`. `create_workspace` places environment values in argv; shutdown code separately treats `workspace_not_found` as idempotent close success.

component_map: `src/campaign_builder/runtime.py` — v1 campaign execution control plane and de facto run-store/recovery specification. Public boundaries: `CampaignRunError`; `campaign_run_lock(Path)`; `CampaignOptions`; `CampaignBuilder(...).run()/resume()`; `approve_handoff()`; `verify_campaign_bundle()`; `replay_verifier_command()`; `campaign_state()`; `campaign_status()`; `campaign_status_exit_code()`; `refresh_campaign_evidence()`; `campaign_resolved_for_run()`; `path_is_excluded()`. Constructor inputs are exactly `CampaignSpec`, `CampaignOptions`, `FeatureRegistry`, `HerdrClient`, Python executable, and optional selected run directory. Retained run tree includes `configuration/`, `input-snapshot/`, `workspace/`, `agents/`, `stages/`, `logs/`, `prompts/`, `recovery/`, `state.json`, `events.jsonl` via `journal_path()`, `evidence.json`, `input-manifest.json`, `.campaign.lock`, optional `replays/`, and promoted outputs. State/evidence/config/input schemas are independently `schema_version=1`; command and replay receipts consumed here are `schema_version=2`.

`src/campaign_builder/features.py` — v1 closed-by-ID feature layer, config parsing, prompt rendering, executor adapters, typed handoff checks, and mathematical trust-policy joins. Public contracts: `FeatureResult`, `FeatureContext`, `CampaignFeature` Protocol, `FeatureRegistry.feature_ids/feature()/validate()`, and `snapshot_workspace_inputs()`. Stable feature IDs are exactly `agent`, `command`, `lean_contract`, `claim_ledger`, `semantic_contract`, and `artifact_promote`. Config classes are `AgentConfig`, `CommandConfig`, `LeanContractConfig`, `LeanSubstitutionConfig`, `ScalarBound`, `ClaimLedgerConfig`, `SemanticContractConfig`, and `PromotionConfig`. Runtime coupling is the unversioned in-memory `FeatureContext`/`FeatureResult` boundary plus path-based artifacts, `retry_targets`, and `required_changes`.

`src/campaign_builder/lean.py` — deterministic proof-gate implementation and schema-v2 evidence producer. Public boundaries: `GateCommandReceipt`, `AxiomReport`, `ProofGateResult`, `scan_lean_sources()`, `validate_substitution_value()`, `render_contract()`, `run_proof_gate()`, and `failed_proof_gate()`. External command sequence uses `lake build`, `lake env which lean`, `lake env lean ...`, and an absolute Lean executable with `--run`; `ProofGateResult.to_dict()` hard-codes `schema_version=2`. It is a formal acceptance primitive, but v1 compiles from a mutable project and splits compiler identity between `lake env lean` and the separately validated absolute Lean reader.

`src/campaign_builder/regime.py` — pre/post-campaign orchestrator. Public boundaries: `MissingSourcePolicy`, `RegimeError`, `RegimeOptions`, `RegimeRunner.run()/resume()`, and `choose_strategy()`. It owns research gate → research/planning → frozen campaign generation → `CampaignBuilder` execution → outcome assessment → knowledge/research publication → successor-strategy choice. Pre-campaign state is journal-backed schema v1; generated campaign TOML is schema v1; user-visible checkpoints include missing sources and awaiting strategy.

`src/campaign_builder/autonomy.py` — retained outer loop across regime campaigns. Public boundaries: `AutonomyError`, `AutonomyRuntimeOptions`, `InterCampaignAnalysis.parse()`, `SuccessValidation`, `AutonomyRunner.run()/resume()`, `record_autonomy_decision()`, and `autonomy_status()`. Session state is journal-backed schema v1; statuses are `ready`, `campaign_running`, `analysis_retry`, `awaiting_approval`, `checkpoint`, `solved`, `stopped`, and `budget_exhausted`. It adds deterministic build/type/axiom/verification commands after a model-assessed `CampaignOutcome`.

`src/campaign_builder/benchmark.py` — strict suite parser and prefix-resumable regime benchmark. Public boundaries: `ExpectedOutcome`, `SourcePolicy`, `BenchmarkCase`, `BenchmarkSuite.load()`, `BenchmarkRuntime`, `run_benchmark_suite()`, and `resume_benchmark_suite()`. Manifest is schema v1; report is exact-key schema v2 with `running|complete`. It currently executes `RegimeRunner`, not `AutonomyRunner`, and therefore scores model-assessed outcomes rather than autonomy’s kernel-checked success contract.

`src/campaign_builder/publication.py` — digest-approved destructive publication transaction. Public boundaries: `PublicationPlan.canonical_dict()/to_dict()`, `plan_publication(run_dir)`, and `publish_campaign(run_dir, approve_digest)`; internal recovery entry point is `_recover_pending_publication`. Plan, terminal, and pending receipts use exact-field `schema_version=1`; phases include `prepared`, `swapped`, `committed`, and `rolled_back`. Lock order is `campaign_run_lock` then destination lock. `plan_publication()` is not actually read-only because it invokes recovery.

`src/campaign_builder/cli.py` — single `argparse` control surface. Commands are exactly `run`, `regime-run`, `regime-resume`, `choose-strategy`, `autonomy-run`, `autonomy-resume`, `autonomy-decide`, `autonomy-status`, `resume`, `validate`, `approve`, `verify`, `status`, `dashboard`, `replay`, `claims`, `audit`, `publish-plan`, `publish`, `regression-assess`, `regression-fit`, `features`, `benchmark`, and `stop-all`. Exit behavior is fragmented: 0 success, 1 unsuccessful/general, 3 checkpoint/approval/not-recommended, and `parser.error` conventionally 2. `--visible` is parsed but unused; several status/resume branches read `state.json` directly instead of authoritative journals.

`src/campaign_builder/terminal_status.py` — non-durable presentation only: `format_elapsed()`, `PaneHeartbeat`, `RoleStatus`, and `ControllerDashboard`. It must remain outside campaign state/evidence. V2 disposition is KEEP with lifecycle, locking, Unicode-width, and testability fixes.

`src/campaign_builder/__init__.py` and `src/campaign_builder/__main__.py` — package facade and logic-free module-execution shim. `__init__.py` eagerly re-exports the explicit `__all__`; `__main__.py` executes `SystemExit(main())`. Preserve the facade and shim, add an API/version compatibility manifest, and consider lazy imports without removing v1 exports before consumer inventory.

Prompt and fixture boundaries — `final_reporter.md`, `inter_campaign_optimizer.md`, `planner.md`, `research_gate.md`, and `researcher.md` contain important policy but rely on prose joins to hidden controller state. Benchmark manifests use schema v1 and expected report semantics use schema v2; current fixtures classify false and underdetermined cases together as `unsolved`, while runtime/control layers also use `blocked`, checkpoints, and awaiting statuses. These are support contracts, not demonstrated calibration.

Auxiliary boundaries — `regression.py` produces schema-v1 non-proof receipts and should be isolated/deferred beyond a linear baseline; `math_tools/exact.py` is KEEP with resource limits; `numeric.py` is KEEP/FIX and must remain exploratory; `symbolic.py` must rename/deprecate `proved`; `references.py` needs a policy-gated acquisition service. These may feed features, but none may independently close a formal target.
coupling_and_duplication: `runtime.py` simultaneously owns controller lifecycle, scheduler, state machine, run-store schema, journal projection, filesystem layout, checkpoint transaction, evidence index, process/Herdr reconciliation, handoff approval, provenance import, verification, replay, and public status helpers. This is the primary v1 monolith.

`features.py` simultaneously owns feature registry, config schemas, executor adapters, agent prompt/request protocol, mutation isolation, typed handoffs, command receipts, Lean policy, claim/semantic closure joins, promotion, and retry economics. It is both plugin API and mathematical trust policy.

Runtime↔feature coupling is unversioned `FeatureContext`/`FeatureResult` plus heterogeneous path strings and filenames. Consumers identify artifacts by basename, schema version, or field presence; claim ledger requires exactly one JSON artifact per command receipt stage, so adding diagnostics can break it.

Status machines are duplicated across `_validate_retained_state`, `_load_run`, transition branches, `campaign_state`, `campaign_status`, `campaign_status_exit_code`, regime pre-state, campaign outcomes, strategy selection, autonomy session/rounds, benchmark report, and CLI mappings. `replan_required` is produced but nonresumable; `awaiting_sources`/`awaiting_strategy` are public yet asymmetrically produced/handled; benchmark maps missing outcome to `checkpoint` although expected taxonomy includes `blocked`.

Retry/reset closure is duplicated in `_reset_stages` and `_route_retry`, with different clearing of summaries, artifacts, feedback, and handoff/output state. Handoff invalidation and promotion cleanup are special-cased instead of artifact dependency invalidation/tombstones.

Resource truth is duplicated across retained state, Herdr creation labels, Herdr workspace IDs/listing, and process registry. Dynamic retry exposes the coupling because resources are allocated from the initial pending set rather than lazily per ready stage.

Persistence protocols are duplicated: campaign, regime, and autonomy journal full-state snapshots; benchmark atomic projection only; strategy selection intent/artifact/receipt; autonomy operator decision file then state; publication pending/terminal receipts. There is no shared commit ID, transition reducer, or idempotent step receipt.

Path/exclusion policy is duplicated and inconsistent across `runtime.path_is_excluded`, feature promotion matcher, input copy, verifier snapshots, source inventory, evidence indexing, and publication. Most checks are `resolve/check/use`, not dirfd-confined operations.

Schemas drift independently: state/evidence/config/input/promotion/source/agent/continuation/claim/semantic artifacts mostly v1; command/Lean/replay receipts v2; review decisions unversioned; benchmark report v2; publication v1. Type is frequently inferred from path/basename/fields. There is no schema registry, compatibility matrix, migration transaction, or implementation digest.

Feature IDs are treated as frozen replay semantics, but retained `features.json` carries IDs/mapping rather than feature implementation/package/parser/sandbox/toolchain digests. A changed installation can reinterpret a retained v1 run under the same ID.

Artifact identity is path-based while evidence is hash-based and `workspace/` is excluded. This creates stale artifact references, basename ambiguity, mutable lineage, live-workspace replay mutation, and successful workspace outputs that resume does not globally certify.

Crash consistency is split across journal, `state.json`, `evidence.json`, checkpoints, pending output cleanup, publication receipts, Herdr intents, process registry, compute ledger, outcome, knowledge indexes, and shared project trees. Recovery is therefore encoded by status exceptions and broad repair-path inference rather than one commit protocol.

Overbuilding: every attempt full-copy+fsyncs the whole workspace; verifier agents copy the whole workspace and compute multiple full source/dependency snapshots; handoffs hash broad source inventories; full-state journal records duplicate cumulative events; `_write_evidence` repeatedly rehashes almost the entire run; publication repeatedly hashes evidence/source/destination/staging; model retries rerun broad proposal/verifier sets and repeat long prompt prefixes.

Overbuilding without delivered semantics: `CampaignOptions.max_parallel` is inert; the scheduler is serial. The architecture pays DAG, Herdr, checkpoint, evidence, replay, and distributed-resource reconciliation complexity while lacking atomic workspace restore, immutable artifacts, a unified transition model, or tests.

Control-plane coupling: `regime.py` embeds model request formats, prompt names, `ProjectSpec` budgets, campaign TOML generation, runtime statuses/locks, evidence, regression capability strings, global knowledge publication, and CLI recovery semantics; `autonomy.py` embeds regime and runtime file/status details; `benchmark.py` embeds regime checkpoint/outcome behavior.

Documentation/prompt overclaim is not executable evidence: terms such as `resumable`, `frozen replay`, `without following symlinks`, `closed registry`, `independent`, `symbolic`, `blind`, `verified status`, and `calibrated` exceed what supplied code/tests demonstrate.

durable_invariants: Single cooperative raw campaign controller: `.campaign.lock` is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, must be a regular file, and is held by nonblocking exclusive `flock` for run/resume/approval/replay. This is advisory POSIX coordination, not hostile-writer exclusion.

Retained campaign state is exactly schema version 1 for validation purposes and must match campaign ID and exact stage-ID set; statuses, attempts/revisions/interruptions, artifact paths, cleanup IDs, and handoff campaign producer/path/schema/digest/timestamp are constrained. Unknown top-level fields remain accepted, so schema strictness is incomplete.

Journal-first ordering: `_save_state` appends the journal snapshot before updating `state.json`; `state.json` is a projection. Regime and autonomy use the same conceptual ordering. V1 journal records contain complete cumulative state, including the ever-growing events list.

Every execution attempt checkpoints the entire workspace before marking a stage running and persisting state. A running stage must have attempts > 0. Failed/interrupted attempts intend to restore the pre-attempt checkpoint; successful attempts retain mutations.

Scheduling legality: pending stages run only after dependencies succeed; failed/skipped dependencies force descendants to skipped. Build stages additionally require a succeeded and approved frozen handoff. Required-stage success is the mathematical campaign completion criterion.
Approval binding: an approved handoff is valid only for the exact SHA-256 digest; a changed digest is rejected before build scheduling.

Artifact/path intent: feature artifacts must resolve below `run_dir/workspace`; handoffs must be regular non-symlink workspace files at handoff time; configuration/copied input manifests are re-digested on resume; verified imports pin source run ID, campaign ID, complete state, evidence digest, indexed path hashes/sizes, and reject observed symlink ancestry.

Evidence/durability intent: JSON writes are atomic, journal snapshots append, checkpoints and publication trees are fsynced, and publication uses same-parent staging/rename. The protection is mutation detection via hashes, not signatures/MACs/remote attestation.

Replay policy intent: only complete evidence-verified campaigns and replayable command stages are accepted; declared evidence inputs and selected sandbox/security metadata must remain equal. V1 does not enforce canonical-workspace nonmutation.

Feature-schema closure: feature config tables reject unknown keys and enforce typed bounds/path syntax; `FeatureRegistry` rejects duplicate IDs and unknown feature IDs; campaign configs are eagerly validated before execution. `FeatureRegistry(features=())` nevertheless selects defaults because of `features or defaults`, and constructor injection means global closure is not literal.

Layered mathematical assurance: prose/model output is not sufficient. Command receipts, Lean proof gates, claim verdict aggregation, semantic equivalence review, obligation disposition, and—only in autonomy—post-solve build/type/axiom/command validation are separate layers. Soundness of imported parsers, sandbox, claims, semantic, and command modules is not established by the supplied corpus.

Publication authorization: only a complete evidence-valid run may publish; approval is lowercase SHA-256 equal to a freshly recomputed canonical plan; source files and staging are rehashed; lock order is run then destination; rename/fsync/backup receipts intend crash recovery; selected top-level preserved entries are type-bound, not content-bound.

Model-tier invariant for v2: state transitions, parsing, scheduling, hashing, closure, budget arithmetic, path policy, receipt validation, Lean execution, evidence, replay policy, and publication remain deterministic. Humans own frozen contracts, handoff/publication approval, and exceptional corruption adjudication; models produce bounded research/planning/semantic content but never durable transition legality.
keep: Keep the public concepts and names through a compatibility window: campaign run/resume/status, typed handoff approval, evidence verification, command replay, provenance import, regime gate→research→plan→freeze→execute→assess, autonomy post-solve validation/approval, benchmark prefix resume, and digest-approved publication.

Keep `campaign_run_lock`’s strong leaf defenses (`O_NOFOLLOW`, regular-file check, nonblocking exclusive `flock`) as a v1 compatibility primitive, while v2 adds parent confinement, lease semantics, typed contention, and documented POSIX scope.

Keep journal-before-projection authority, exact campaign/stage identity validation, fail-fast feature config validation, dependency closure, required/optional stage semantics, digest-bound handoff approval, post-copy artifact hash verification, and explicit incomplete/replan/restart outcomes after formalization.

Retain a v1 read-only validator/importer and explicit one-way migration; v2 must not mutate a v1 bundle before migration.

risks: Critical publication defect: after `publication.pending.json` reaches `prepared`, failure before any swap can leave pending state while final cleanup deletes staging; later recovery requires staging/failed paths and rejects the retained state. This needs an immediate v1 regression fix before broader v2 work.

Critical workspace durability defect: `_restore_checkpoint` removes live workspace then `copytree`s the checkpoint. Crash, ENOSPC, permission failure, or power loss can leave a missing/partial workspace.

Critical replay integrity defect: replay executes against the live complete workspace, snapshots only declared evidence inputs, permits undeclared mutation, and refreshes evidence while workspace content is excluded. `frozen replay` is therefore not an accurate security property.

Critical approval boundary defect: `approve_handoff` loads incompletely validated state, does not verify full evidence/configuration, and directly joins retained handoff path under workspace; corruption/path traversal safety depends on unsupplied `digest_handoff`.
Critical feature bug: `SemanticContractFeature.validate` unconditionally adds non-null `repair_target` to unknown, rejecting every configured repair route.
Critical scheduler/resource defect: dynamic retry can route to an agent with no Herdr pane because panes are allocated only for agents pending at `_execute` entry.

Critical benchmark assurance mismatch: benchmark claims autonomous/outcome false-closure measurement but runs `RegimeRunner`, does not invoke autonomy’s deterministic success contract, and treats missing outcomes as `checkpoint`; current scores cannot be equated with kernel-checked closure.

High TOCTOU exposure: lock leaf defense is strong, but most parent traversal, copy, cleanup, promotion, import, publication, and evidence reads are path-based resolve/check/use. Advisory flock does not stop writers that ignore it; hardlinks, bind mounts, mount replacement, and hostile shared ownership are largely unaddressed.

High evidence gap: workspace files are excluded from `evidence.json`; successful-stage sources/outputs can mutate without general resume detection. Selected handoffs, command inputs, promoted artifacts, and autonomy checks only partially compensate.

High state-machine inconsistency: validation permits combinations such as `complete` with running stages; top-level extras permit undeclared `herdr_close_error`; completed timestamp/status, awaiting handoff state, max attempts, and event semantics are not fully cross-validated.

High retry inconsistency: `_route_retry` and `_reset_stages` clear different fields; failed-attempt artifact paths may survive restoration; attempts are not reset and rerouted exhausted stages may still run; invalid retry options are checked after pending output cleanup mutates retained outputs.

High evidence-repair risk: running-attempt repair allowances use broad prefix/path inference; `_recoverable_attempt_evidence_paths` uses `startswith(attempt_name)`, and correctness depends on unsupplied `verify_evidence_for_repair`.

High signal/finally risk: partial signal handler installation may not be restored; `KeyboardInterrupt` is translated to stopped and swallowed; finalization/evidence/handler errors can mask the original failure.

High publication race risk: path-based staging/copy/rename, accessible staging modes, no destination snapshot revalidation, unbound preserved bytes, and external writers can alter what an approved digest actually authorizes.

High Lean trust-boundary risk: live project changes across scan/build/compile; validated absolute Lean differs from compiler invoked through Lake; project-local `.olean` staging is untrusted and TOCTOU-prone; executable/toolchain digests are absent.

High control-plane race risk: regime shared references/knowledge publication lacks project-wide locking; autonomy checkpoint resume mutates before controller lock; AFK fallback can overwrite a later operator decision; benchmark has no run lock.
High mutable-lineage risk: autonomy carries paths into prior live workspaces without digests; regime recursively copied nested symlinks may be exposed to model roles before later freeze rejection.

High model/cache drift: retained feature IDs and succeeded meta-agent receipts do not bind implementation, prompt, model, tools, workspace inputs, or policy hashes, permitting stale reuse or semantic reinterpretation.

High compute/disk amplification: full workspace copy+fsync per attempt; verifier copy-and-multiple-hash; broad source inventories; cumulative full-state journal snapshots; repeated full-run evidence scans; duplicate publication hashing; repeated planner/gate/assessor/optimizer calls; broad claim reroutes; very large timeout upper bounds.

High external-side-effect limitation: workspace rollback cannot reverse unsandboxed commands, network effects, shared project publication, or unregistered descendants. Process cleanup correctness and sandbox enforcement are in unsupplied modules.

Medium CLI/API compatibility risk: no external consumer inventory, no stable machine output across commands, fragmented exit codes, direct projection reads, and eager `__init__.py` imports. V2 removals could silently break scripts or Python users.

Medium schema migration risk: exact-key validators make additive changes breaking; other validators ignore schema version or unknown top-level fields. Without explicit migrations, v2 code could either reject valid history or silently reinterpret it.

Medium mathematical assurance risk: campaign configuration remains a trust root for target meaning, allowed axioms, command-to-target coverage, model independence, and semantic mapping. `covers_targets` and verifier labels do not prove semantics.

Medium authenticity limitation: SHA-256 indexes and approval digests detect accidental drift but are forgeable by a writer able to alter the bundle. Cross-principal export requires explicit signatures/MACs and threat-model documentation.

Evidence limitation: no supplied tests, run bundles, benchmark executions, incident data, or performance measurements support durability, security, calibration, or cost claims. All risk priority labels here reflect structural impact, not observed incident frequency.

v2_interfaces: `RunStore` — append immutable `RunEventV2`; read a commit-head snapshot; rebuild/publish `RunStateV2`; transaction/open-state checks; v1 read-only import. No feature or model execution logic.

`RunEventV2` — canonical envelope with `record_type`, `schema_version`, `run_id`, `campaign_id`, `sequence`, `commit_id`, predecessor/checksum, transition type, payload, producer implementation digest, idempotency key, and recorded time. Exact migration/unknown-field policy lives in a schema registry.

`RunStateV2` and `StateMachine` — typed run/stage/resource/approval states and a pure reducer/validator. One source of truth for legal transitions, cross-field invariants, status text, resumability, and exit codes.

`Scheduler` — pure ready-set and affected-closure computation; no state mutation during query. Serial in v2.0 unless isolated branches are implemented. Attempt/revision budgets and failure-policy transitions are explicit inputs.
`WorkspaceTransaction` — immutable snapshot root, writable stage branch, commit/discard, crash-safe restore by root-pointer swap, changed-byte accounting, and symlink/hardlink/mount policy.

`ArtifactRefV2` — one typed immutable reference containing namespace, content digest/Merkle root, size/kind/media type, producer run/stage/attempt, schema/type, locator/display path, and assurance class. Dependency APIs accept references, not mutable paths.

`EvidenceCommitV2` / `EvidenceIndex` — binds configuration/input/state/event/resource/artifact roots and producer/toolchain identities; supports incremental additions, verified commit-head reads, and optional signed export attestations.

`FeatureEnvelopeV2[Config,Result,Receipt]` — `feature_id`, config/result/receipt schema versions, capability manifest, deterministic validator, executor implementation digest, artifact I/O classes, retry compatibility, and migration adapter.

`FeatureExecutor` adapters — `AgentExecutor`, `CommandExecutor`, `LeanExecutor`, `ClaimLedgerExecutor`, `SemanticContractExecutor`, and `ArtifactPublisher`; model-task prompts/config are separate from deterministic execution/validation.
`ResourceManager` — durable create/close intents, stage-scoped lazy acquisition, idempotency keys, leases, remote/process reconciliation, and explicit cleanup outcomes.
`HandoffApprovalService` — full bundle validation, fd-confined handoff read, digest binding, approver/policy record, invalidation by artifact dependency, and optional cross-owner signature/MAC.
`ProvenanceImporter` — signed/pinned source bundle option, fd-stable traversal, selected immutable artifact references, destination staging, post-copy verification, and atomic import commit.

`ReplayService` — input is an original `EvidenceCommitV2` plus typed replay receipt; execution occurs in a disposable read-only snapshot with pinned executable/toolchain/environment/sandbox policy and declared output-only writes; canonical run is never mutated.

`ProofGateReceiptV3` — compatibility reader for current `ProofGateResult` schema v2 plus v3 source-tree root, contract/rendered hashes, substitutions, declaration identities, per-declaration axiom sets, Lake/Lean executable digests/versions, command receipts, sandbox attestation, and protocol version.

`PublicationTransactionV2` — canonical plan plus approval, destination snapshot semantics, transaction event reducer, private dirfd-anchored staging, backup/swap/verify/commit/rollback, and explicit committed/recovery-required outcome. Compatibility reader for publication schema v1 receipts.

`CampaignControlV2` — typed higher-level events composing pre-campaign research/plan/freeze, campaign execution, outcome/assurance, strategy decision, autonomy round, and benchmark case. It references `RunStore` commits rather than embedding raw runtime dictionaries.

`ProjectRepository` — project-wide locked transaction for references, knowledge, accepted reports, and indexes using content-addressed artifacts, limitations union, verifier receipts, and exact producer attempt IDs.
`DecisionArbiter` — atomic compare-and-swap for operator decision, timeout fallback, strategy intent/receipt, and checkpoint resume under one session lease.
`BenchmarkRunStore` — frozen suite/case closure, case idempotency keys, journaled prefix/materialized report, assurance-contract verifier, and typed status+reason codes.

`SchemaRegistry` — canonical encoding, record type/version, producer/minimum reader, strictness/extensions, migration path, implementation identity, and golden fixtures for all retained JSON/TOML/receipt protocols.

`SafeFilesystem` — normalized relative paths, dirfd/openat-style no-follow traversal, private staging, regular-file/ownership/link/mount checks, no-replace atomic publication, directory fsync, and one exclusion matcher.
`CommandResultEnvelope` for CLI — stable machine JSON and human rendering, command/API version, status/reason, commit/evidence IDs, warnings/deprecations, and documented exit code.

Compatibility surfaces — preserve existing `CampaignBuilder`, `RegimeRunner`, `AutonomyRunner`, benchmark functions, CLI commands, and `campaign_builder.__all__` as adapters that either operate v1 read-only, invoke migration, or delegate to v2 without silently reinterpreting v1 feature IDs/defaults.
workflows: New raw campaign: `CampaignBuilder.run()` selects/creates a run directory, acquires `.campaign.lock`, creates the v1 directory tree, retains resolved configuration and instructions, copies or records inputs, writes input/config manifests, initializes journal-backed state and evidence, provisions controller/Herdr state, and enters `_execute`. Setup is nontransactional, so an interrupted initialization can leave an unusable initialized-looking directory.

Stage execution: `_ready_stages()` finds pending stages whose dependencies succeeded and also mutates descendants to skipped when prerequisites fail. `_execute` always selects `ready[0]`; despite the DAG and `CampaignOptions.max_parallel`, execution is serial. Before every attempt, `_checkpoint_workspace()` copies and fsyncs the entire workspace, state becomes running, a feature is resolved through `FeatureRegistry`, and `execute(FeatureContext)` returns `FeatureResult` or selected operational exceptions are normalized.

Feature outcomes: `_consume` records status, summary, artifacts, retry targets, and required changes. Success keeps workspace mutation; failed/revision outcomes trigger checkpoint restoration and retry/revision routing. Build stages are gated on a succeeded, explicitly approved research handoff whose exact SHA-256 digest still matches. Required-stage success is campaign completion; optional failures may coexist with `complete`.

Retry/revision: `_reset_stages` and `_route_retry` separately compute affected descendants, clear different subsets of stage fields, invalidate affected handoffs, schedule promoted-output cleanup, and persist state/evidence around cleanup. Dynamic routing can make an agent pending after Herdr panes were allocated, creating a missing-resource failure. Attempt budgets are not formalized across reroutes and revisions.

Resume/recovery: `CampaignBuilder.resume()` locks the run, loads journal state through a temporary recovery pass, compares with authoritative reread, verifies retained configuration/input/evidence with special repair allowances, recovers interrupted attempts/processes/Herdr workspaces/checkpoints, completes pending output cleanup, and resumes only selected statuses. Recovery semantics are spread across state status, journal tail, checkpoints, evidence repair paths, Herdr creation labels/IDs/listing, and process registry.

Approval: `approve_handoff()` locks the run and binds approval to the current handoff digest. In v1 `_approve_handoff_locked` does not first perform the full retained-state/evidence/config/path validation used by resume; therefore approval is not a complete bundle transaction.

Replay: `replay_verifier_command()` requires a complete evidence-verified campaign, reconstructs `CommandConfig` via `FeatureRegistry`, checks declared evidence inputs and selected sandbox metadata, then executes against the live canonical workspace and adds replay receipts/evidence. This contradicts the claimed frozen/read-only replay boundary because undeclared workspace mutations can persist and workspace files are excluded from evidence.

Verified import: prior-run artifacts are accepted only after source campaign/run/status/evidence identity checks and per-file hash/size verification, then copied into the destination. Source traversal is pathname-based rather than fd-stable, but post-copy verification protects selected bytes against ordinary source mutation.

Regime workflow: `RegimeRunner` snapshots pre-campaign inputs, invokes model research gate/research/planning roles, deterministically validates budgets/capabilities, renders schema-v1 campaign TOML, freezes inputs/plan, drives `CampaignBuilder` with bounded restarts, asks a model for `CampaignOutcome`, validates evidence paths, publishes research/knowledge, and journals a strategy intent/artifact/receipt transaction. Shared project publication is not protected by a project-wide lock.

Autonomy workflow: `AutonomyRunner` repeatedly runs/resumes regime campaigns, treats model `solved` as insufficient, verifies evidence and required artifacts, runs build, generated Lean declaration/type/axiom checks, and configured verification commands, then invokes a read-only optimizer and arbitrates operator or AFK decisions. Resume and AFK/operator arbitration are not one atomic lock-protected transition.

Benchmark workflow: `run_benchmark_suite()` snapshots suite TOML, serially runs one `RegimeRunner` per case, catches per-case exceptions, derives observed outcome, and atomically rewrites a schema-v2 report. Resume accepts only a strict recorded prefix. There is no benchmark lock/idempotency key, complete case closure freeze, or kernel-backed false-closure check.

Publication workflow: `plan_publication()` locks the run, recovers pending publication, verifies complete state/evidence/config/source and destination safety, hashes an exact plan, and returns an approval digest. `publish_campaign()` recomputes the plan under run+destination locks, stages exact bytes, writes `publication.pending.json`, swaps destination with backup, writes terminal receipts, fsyncs, and refreshes campaign evidence. A prepared-before-swap exception path can delete staging while leaving an unrecoverable pending receipt.

acceptance_gates: GATE P0-SCHEMAS — All public records have explicit versions, closed/extensible field policy, stable error/event/phase codes, identity bindings, and JSON paths. No core test relies on English prose when a machine field exists.

GATE P0-PROCESS — Central containment contract passes normal exit, timeout, controller signal, leader-first exit, resistant descendants, PID reuse/start-time mismatch, stale registration, pidfd failure, EPERM, EMFILE/ENOSYS, and orphan ambiguity without signaling unrelated processes. Adapter-specific campaign/Lean/Herdr/regime smoke tests pass.

GATE P0-DURABILITY — Journal validates sequence/hash chain under all mutation classes; corrupt-tail policy is deterministic; `state.json` is rebuilt only from valid events; every intent-based workflow converges across all crash cuts; multiprocess resumes serialize and commit externally visible terminal effects once.

GATE P0-PREFLIGHT — Secret policy, retained-evidence verification, verified-import pins, publication approval, exact Lean declaration/signature, negative regression assessment, immutable success-contract digest, and filesystem containment/type checks all fail before external mutation or backend initialization.

GATE P0-EVIDENCE — Evidence index is a nonempty closed world with exact-byte digests and campaign/run/index identity; import/copy is link-safe and race-resistant; receipts validate stage/path/digest/coverage; execution reads only authorized frozen roots; stale/cross-run substitution is rejected.

GATE P0-PUBLICATION — Approved plan digest binds bytes and destination semantics; lock uses canonical destination; under-lock revalidation occurs immediately before swap; staged bytes are rehashed; fsync ordering is complete; every prepared/commit/rollback crash cut recovers; committed state never regresses; unrelated evidence is untouched.

GATE P0-SECRETS/SANDBOX — Untrusted lanes receive a minimal environment and no undeclared secret; redaction covers all tested stream splits and sinks; secret-derived artifacts are scrubbed or produce a distinct failure; sandbox denies undeclared host writes/network/user bus and enforces documented resource guarantees.

GATE P0-LEAN/SEMANTICS — Real pinned Lean oracle builds the actual staged challenge; declaration signature is unchanged and appears exactly once; structured axiom report is independently parsed and target-bound; claim verifier is nonmutating/capability-free and pins evidence; stale handoffs and target substitutions fail. Reports use scoped labels and never infer truth/independence merely from lane separation.

GATE P0-CLAIMS — Proposal/verdict/adjudication schemas are strict; canonical claim-ID golden vectors pass across implementations; graph and complete-decision-set negatives pass; closure algebra is consistent for verified/rejected/blocked/missing-gate states; every target field and evidence receipt is frozen and validated.

GATE P0-REGRESSION — Config validation is centralized at parse/load/fit; nonrecommended input causes no output/backend import/init; input/output operations are race-resistant and transactional; preprocessing and all fitting exclude validation rows; public artifact verifier rejects mutation/truncation/swap/removal/receipt alteration before loading.

GATE P0-BENCHMARK — Fixture validator uses ordinary exceptions and structured per-case JSON; both manifests and all projects validate; private answer keys are unreachable under an explicit channel threat model; each prompt obligation maps to a deterministic or declared rubric check; run artifacts, not fixture answers, determine results; status and reason distinguish missing evidence, underdetermined, refuted, unknown, budget exhaustion, verifier error, and checkpoint.

GATE P1-ORCHESTRATION — Typed state machines cover gate/research/plan/campaign/assessment/strategy/optimizer/approval/benchmark transitions; retries and budgets are bounded and durable; reusable success is not reinvoked; targeted invalidation reruns required descendants; operator feedback and AFK deadlines retain causal provenance.

GATE P1-PLANNER — Every catalog capability is uniquely used or skipped; unavailable capability use fails; invocation metadata is structured and tool-authorized; regression assess and fit use separate tasks with transitive ordering; promotion auditor is distinct/downstream/audit-classified/successful/evidence-bearing.

GATE P1-TOOLING — Exact rational/enclosure and root invariants pass generated tests; URL policy checks every hop before destination mutation; CLI contracts pass installed-entry-point tests; CMV/calibration reports validate against schemas and complete expected ID sets; TensorFlow replay passes in fresh process within declared environment/tolerance.

RELEASE REPORT GATE — Publish a matrix of passed, skipped-by-capability, unsupported, quarantined, and failed contracts. A skipped P0 contract is a release failure unless the corresponding platform/capability is explicitly outside the v2 support statement.

LEGACY TAXONOMY FACT: `unsolved` currently combines complete-but-underdetermined (`dependent-system`) and conclusively refuted (`odd-prime-conjecture`, `signed-cross-multiplication`). V2 must preserve historical mapping for report migration but use distinct mathematical reason codes such as `underdetermined` and `refuted`. `blocked` currently represents unavailable retained evidence.

POLICY FACT: `missing-table-entry` has `continue` in `benchmark.toml` and `checkpoint` in `focused-benchmark.toml`. The supplied code does not execute or test either transition, so intentional override versus drift is unknown. V2 must encode override provenance/rationale and test both state transitions.

BLINDNESS FACT: `tests/test_benchmark_calibration.py` TESTED absence of benchmark control files and literal expected certificate strings in initialized UTF-8-readable snapshots, plus an expected top-level shape. This is narrower than noninterference. All benchmark projects set `sandbox=false` and grant broad read/bash/eval/write/edit capabilities, while answer keys live under the benchmark tree; therefore actual answer-key inaccessibility is IMPLIED, not established.

V2 BENCHMARK CONTRACT: suite/project/case/evidence/run/verifier schemas are versioned and validated; private adjudication material is physically outside agent visibility; case obligations are typed and checked individually; outputs use `status` plus `reason_code`; deterministic preflight handles arithmetic/rank/residue/sign/source/signature checks; policy transitions are executable; empirical run metadata and confusion matrices are stored separately from fixture validation.

V2 CASE OUTCOMES: retain seven solved fixture intents; represent `redacted-mean` and `missing-table-entry` as `blocked` with `missing_evidence`; represent `dependent-system` as `underdetermined`; represent `odd-prime-conjecture` and `signed-cross-multiplication` as `refuted`. Keep legacy `unsolved` only as a migration projection, not the authoritative semantic result.

V2 ACCEPTANCE IS EXISTENTIAL AND OBLIGATION-BASED: arithmetic accepts any valid certificate meeting every mandatory obligation; Lean accepts any unchanged-signature, kernel-valid, policy-compliant proof; canonical prose/answer files are documentation/private smoke fixtures, not the sole accepted output.
contract_inventory: Scope and naming rule — the audit supplies exact file paths but not individual pytest function symbols. Therefore this specification names exact source files and behavioral contracts without inventing test names. V2-04 Mutation manifest: compare workspace and recovery trees against an immutable baseline and list added/modified/deleted paths; baseline-only copies must not be labeled recovery progress.
V2-05 Scheduler observability: record runnable roots, selected tasks, `max_parallel` use, resource/concurrency decision, queue time, starvation, and why independent roots did not start.

V2-10 Source-row evidence: bind PDF page/proposition/equation/branch/domain/orientation excerpts to source hash and reviewer sign-off; unresolved rows must trigger research reconsideration.

Retry: durable retry intent and `pending_output_cleanup` precede promotion deletion; resume completes cleanup idempotently; producer reset invalidates derived approvals, promotions, downstream artifacts, and stale research outputs.

Publication filesystem: destination stays inside the configured root; traversal, overlap, symlink boundaries, and special preserved entries fail closed; a destination-scoped lock serializes all runs targeting the same canonical destination; preserve behavior is exact and plan-bound.

Publication durability: files and required directories are fsynced before `prepared`; preservation/recovery moves and affected directories are fsynced before phase advancement; a durable committed marker is irreversible and is forward-repaired/cleaned, never rolled back; terminal receipt recovery also repairs evidence idempotently.

Process ownership: canonical run ownership is durably registered before launch. Process records retain PID, start time, and group/session identity; unit records retain unit and `systemctl`; unregister and outcomes use complete identity, never PID alone.

Shutdown: units and exact owned process members/groups are stopped and verified inactive before unregister or checkpoint restore. Identity mismatch, `EPERM`, non-`ESRCH` pidfd failure, cleanup failure, or unverifiable liveness remains a survivor/error, not success.

Sandbox/environment: every command, agent, Lean gate, replay, and regime meta-agent uses one explicit containment/environment contract. Sandboxed execution receives no declared secret values; non-retention is value-aware across config, argv, env, output, receipts, workspace, evidence, success/failure/timeout/interruption, and inaccessible paths.

Trusted contract/helper/artifacts are outside candidate-writable paths, and trusted axiom facts cannot come from forgeable, ambiguous, truncated, or project-controlled channels.

Runner retry: retry if and only if an invocation exits 0 with whitespace-only stdout; total invocations are exactly `empty_output_retries + 1`; timeout, nonzero exit, spawn error, and nonblank success are never retried; per-invocation evidence remains deterministic while top-level receipts stay compatible.

Campaign data: required approval is an intentional pause and cannot also be called uninterrupted one-command completion; immutable contracts are actual DAG gates; profiles remain within role/stage; source challenge uses research scope; repair routes to a proof-producing stage; `contracts/frontier.lean` preserves exactly the two required declarations without compatibility assumptions.

Audit claims: distinguish reviewer hypothesis, source-confirmed defect, executed reproduction, landed edit, source-verified fix, focused test pass, full-suite pass, and post-fix audit. Skipped/interrupted calls and parent assertions without command output do not count as validation.
incident_classes: INC-01 — Publication authorization and operator flow. Initial implementation lacked a non-mutating way to obtain the approval digest (`RuntimeReviewer`, severity unavailable) and `PublicationSecurity` reported unspecified blocking findings. Source fixes later added `publish-plan`, canonical full-plan JSON, exact lowercase SHA-256 approval, retained resolved config, `PublishSpec.root`, and shared locking. The exact original security finding bodies and exact canonical schema are unavailable.

INC-02 — Publication source/staging TOCTOU. `RuntimeReviewer` found that source was planned/verified and then copied without proving the staged tree still matched the approved plan. `SecurePublication` later added exact staged-copy re-verification immediately before swap. This is source-verified only; mutation tests were written but not run.

INC-03 — Publication recovery validate-after-mutate [P1]. `ReleaseCoherenceAudit` located the defect at `src/campaign_builder/publication.py:235-238`: nonterminal pending recovery could act on forged/incomplete receipt state before complete validation. `PublicationPreflightFix` added `_validate_pending_publication_receipt` and `_validate_nonterminal_recovery_state` before rollback/delete/rename. No focused execution is retained.

INC-04 — Publication destination concurrency [P1 in crash audit]. Run-scoped locking allowed different runs to interleave against one destination (`publication.py:112-135` context). `PublicationDestinationLockFix` added `_publication_destination_for_lock` and `_destination_publication_lock`, with run-lock-then-destination-lock ordering across recovery through cleanup. The forked regression was not run; exact alias canonicalization is not reconstructable.

INC-05 — Publication durability and irreversible commit [P1 set]. `ReleaseCrashAudit` found staged bytes/directories not fully fsynced (`publication.py:740-772`, `871-882`), rollback possible after a durable committed marker (`657-686` context), and preserved-entry recovery moves not fsynced. `PublicationDurabilityFix` added `_fsync_regular_file`, `_fsync_staging`, recovery directory fsyncs, and `commit_durable` gating. Source ordering was reread; crash/interrupt tests were not run.

INC-06 — Publication path/preserve safety. Reviews covered root allowlisting, overlap, traversal, symlink/hardlink/special-entry attacks, and exact preserve semantics. `PublicationFixes` source-added two-time `lstat` validation, recursive no-follow directory checks, rejection of symlink/FIFO/socket/device/special entries, and type/policy binding to the approved plan. Hardlink policy and all original `PublicationSecurity` attack details remain unavailable.

INC-07 — Publication evidence/terminal recovery [multiple P1s]. System/crash reviews found terminal receipt recovery could omit evidence re-indexing or bless unrelated drift. `artifacts.verify_evidence_for_repair(run_dir, *, permitted_paths=...)` and terminal recovery source changes verify all non-publication indexed paths before repair. Later reviews reported terminal receipt evidence repair present, but no executed prepared/swapped/committed/rolled-back matrix exists.

INC-08 — Verified-artifact mutable provenance. Initial `verified_artifact` accepted a mutable source run path without externally retained pins. `PinnedVerifiedArtifact` added jointly required `expected_campaign_id`, `expected_run_id`, and `evidence_sha256`, raw `evidence.json` hashing, evidence/state/directory identity checks, resolved round trip, and a manifest pin for run `20260815T021428Z-1e993d`. The actual digest is intentionally absent and must not be guessed.

INC-09 — Run concurrency [RuntimeReviewer finding, severity unavailable]. Two controllers could resume one run because `running` was resumable and no exclusive lock serialized mutation. `RuntimeStateHardening` added `campaign_run_lock(run_dir: Path)` using `.campaign.lock`, `O_NOFOLLOW`, nonblocking exclusive `fcntl.flock`, and `CampaignRunError`. Publication was required to reuse it. No multiprocessing or target-filesystem execution is retained.

INC-10 — Malformed retained state [RuntimeReviewer finding, severity unavailable]. Syntactically valid malformed `state.json` could cause `KeyError` or illegal transitions. `RuntimeStateHardening` added top-level, exact-stage-ID, status/attempt/artifact/summary/completion/feedback validation before assignment/indexing. The malformed-state tests were written but not run.

INC-11 — Handoff approval bypass [P1]. `src/dossier_builder/campaign_runtime.py:333-338` gated build readiness only through dependency ancestry, so a non-ancestral build could bypass the configured approved handoff. `RuntimeStateHardening` changed readiness to gate every build stage on configured approval. No executed non-ancestral regression is retained.

INC-12 — Stale handoff reuse. A retry could report success without writing a new handoff and inherit the prior attempt’s valid JSON. `FreshHandoffRetry` removes a prior regular file/symlink after source inventory and before every producer attempt, rejects directory/special entries, preserves invalid current output, and added `test_retry_requires_handoff_created_by_current_attempt`. The test was not run.

INC-13 — Evidence authority on resume [P1]. Resume could consume successful dependency artifacts/checkpoints or refresh evidence before validating retained evidence; a crash after upstream success could leave artifacts unindexed and later tampering could be blessed. `ResumeEvidenceGateFix` added stage-boundary evidence baselines and `verify_evidence_for_repair` before retained consumption/reindex, with a narrow current-running-attempt/controller allowlist. SIGKILL/tamper regressions were not run.

INC-14 — Journal/projection authority and crash ordering [multiple P1s]. System/crash reviews found status, stop, resume, retry, approval, terminal failure, evidence refresh, and regime operations using stale `state.json` or ordering durable steps incorrectly. Many source changes introduced journal authority, durable `pending_output_cleanup`, checkpoint ordering, and recovery logic. Two final unresolved P1s remain: accepting a verified journal-ahead status during resume repair, and clearing retained research outputs before rerunning after a source checkpoint.

INC-15 — Retry-derived-state invalidation. Reviews found routed/operator retry could delete promotion outputs before durable intent, retain stale approvals/promotions, mishandle multi-failure successes, or lose checkpoint state. `RuntimeCrashFixes` added `pending_output_cleanup` before deletion and idempotent resume cleanup; other patches reportedly invalidated approvals/promotions. No crash-boundary execution proves the full phase ordering.

INC-16 — Herdr create/register crash window [P1]. A workspace could be created externally before durable registry persistence and become undiscoverable. `RuntimeCrashFixes` added durable `herdr_creation_label`, label-based discovery/closure, durable workspace-ID registration, then intent clearing. Real-service discovery and crash injection were not run.

INC-17 — Systemd unit ownership/lifetime. Sandbox reviews found controller-crash ownership/lifetime gaps. `SandboxOwnershipFix` added canonical-run `RegisteredRunUnit(run_dir, unit, systemctl)`, durable registration before `Popen`, stop/verify-inactive before unregister, `unit_errors`, and deadline-derived `RuntimeMaxSec`. `FinalSecurityReview` statically verified these and reported no current P0/P1 in that scope; no real/fake-systemd SIGKILL test result exists.

INC-18 — Process exact identity and stale unregister [P1]. PID-only unregister could delete a replacement registration after PID reuse. `ProcessTreeRecoveryFix` introduced `RegisteredRunProcess`, exact PID/start-time/group/session identity, exact unregister, and a post-capture start-time recheck. Security re-audit statically observed this original defect fixed.

INC-19 — Process-tree shutdown and failure accounting [P1 set]. Crash audits found leader-only termination, descendants surviving, `PermissionError` and non-`ESRCH` `pidfd_open` failures treated too leniently, and outcome cardinality collapsed by `{target.pid: target}` at `processes.py:330-332`. Later source rewrites added process-group/session handling, per-member pidfds, exact outcomes, and survivor/error reporting; the exact PID-keyed collapse was withdrawn on reread. No real process-tree/PID-reuse execution exists.

INC-20 — Residual process-group provenance [P1 reviewer concern]. Final identity/coherence audits still argued that per-member pidfds authenticate current member PIDs but do not by themselves prove the numeric PGID/SID is the originally owned group after leader/PGID reuse (`processes.py:350-500` context). Main asserted remediation, but no final source verdict or deterministic reuse test resolves the disagreement.

INC-21 — Stop-all ownership discovery [P1]. Stop-all discovered campaign directories but could omit fixed-regime meta-agent ownership records. `MetaAgentStopFix` added `registered_run_directories` based on exact process/unit registry records and unions those with campaign-registered runs. The focused stop-all regression was not run.

INC-22 — Secret non-retention [P1/high]. Initial key-intersection defenses missed the same secret value under another inline environment key (`CB-SECRET-001`). Later source patches reportedly became value-aware and fail-closed across cleanup paths. The record has no executed alternate-key, output, receipt, workspace, evidence, unreadable-directory, symlink, or interruption matrix.

INC-23 — Sandbox cleanup/failure receipts. Reviews found inaccessible-directory traversal, interruption gaps, silent cgroup termination failure, and sandbox-launch receipts lacking intended/effective containment metadata. `_scandir_entries`/`_workspace_entries`, finally-equivalent cleanup, surfaced errors, and receipt metadata were statically reread. INC-24 — Replay integrity. `CB-REPLAY-001` found changed executable/environment could be used during replay; `CB-REPLAY-002` found a successful replay could mutate covered evidence. Later aggregate audits said no current P0/P1, but no one-to-one fix history or replay mutation/fingerprint test result is retained.

INC-25 — Empty-output retry behavior. Feature implementation added `empty_output_retries`, retrying only exit-0 whitespace stdout, at most `N+1` invocations, with per-invocation receipts and preserved top-level compatibility. No reviewer found a loop defect, but recovery/exhaustion/default/nonzero/timeout/spawn-error/nonblank tests were authored and never executed.

INC-27 — Fixed-regime stale research [P1]. `publication_research` reused completed limited output after `awaiting_sources` resume (`regime.py:328-332`, also `315-338`). `StaleResearchResumeFix` changed invocation to `reuse_completed=not resuming` and updated the fake/regression. INC-28 — Regime/meta-agent containment and transactionality [multiple P1s]. Arbitrary metadata flowed through `features._resolve_substitutions` into `lean.render_contract`, allowing newline/Lean command/declaration/forged-report injection. `LeanSubstitutionSecurityFix` added `validate_substitution_value`, strict typed/lexical validation at resolution and rendering, and malicious/legitimate regressions. Frozen contract/helper were initially written into attacker-writable project paths; then `audit_olean` remained writable; then separate-module imports could resolve from mutable project paths. review_process_lessons: Multiple adversarial waves were valuable because each used a different trust model against the integrated tree. Feature-local workers checked assigned interfaces; `RuntimeReviewer` traced config/runtime/CLI/publish and found non-ancestral approval bypass, missing run serialization, publication TOCTOU, stale handoffs, missing plan UX, and malformed-state crashes that no single owner saw.

The campaign-data wave added unique value: `CampaignReviewer` compared actual manifest DAGs, profile roles, repair routing, and approval semantics against operator claims. Those defects were invisible to Python-focused reviews and were not mathematics defects.

The filesystem/security wave added unique value: `PublicationSecurity`, sandbox, hermetic-environment, and secret source-to-sink reviews challenged malicious retained runs, alternate-key secret values, symlink/special entries, replay mutation, cleanup failure, and launch metadata. The alternate-key secret bypass specifically demonstrated why matching secret key names was not equivalent to preventing secret-value retention.

The crash waves added unique value by enumerating every durable boundary rather than normal success: journal append versus projection, retry intent versus deletion, checkpoint restore versus terminal failure, external Herdr create versus registry persistence, prepared/swapped/committed publication markers, fsync placement, pidfd acquisition, signal delivery, and evidence refresh.

The system/coherence waves added unique value after narrower “no high” verdicts because they expanded scope to regime meta-agents, semantic declaration binding, strategy transactions, frozen inputs, stop-all discovery, and recovered-publication evidence. The earlier verdicts were not wrong within scope; treating them as global release approval would have been wrong.

Current-tree rereads were essential on a moving tree. Reviewers correctly withdrew stale findings after observing external trusted roots, inline Lean collection, exact process outcomes, full registration identities, `RuntimeMaxSec`, and pre-launch ownership registration. This prevented already-fixed defects from remaining in the incident list.

Explicit symbol ownership reduced damaging churn: `CampaignInput` pins versus `PublishSpec.root`; PID/start-time APIs versus `RegisteredRunUnit`; one shared `campaign_run_lock`; one `verify_evidence_for_repair`; and distinct test helper names. These coordination decisions prevented duplicate lock and evidence-repair conventions.

Review churn was concentrated in repeated optimistic edits to `tests/test_campaign_builder.py`, interrupted/skipped tool calls, concurrent changes that invalidated line numbers, broad `git diff`/grep/full-file passes that added little beyond focused tracing, and audits that violated “no commands” with read-only git commands. These consumed time without creating execution evidence.

The largest auditability failure was opaque/truncated `yield(result)` payloads. Exact `PublicationSecurity` blocking findings, several severities/line ranges, `RecoveryStateMap`’s schema, and some final Lean/process finding bodies were lost. Main had to request summaries over IRC, leaving aggregate titles where exact attack sequences should have been retained.

The largest verification failure was orchestration policy: repeated “finish/yield without validation” instructions converted regressions into design artifacts rather than evidence. Later reviewers had to infer behavior statically, and concurrent API churn caused the one attempted semantic integration run to fail before coverage completed.

The useful sequence evidenced by this record is specific: assign narrow symbol ownership; implement; integrate; freeze a commit; run separate runtime, campaign-data, filesystem/security, secret source-to-sink, crash-order, and system-coherence passes; convert each exact finding into one owner plus regression; execute focused tests and fault injection; run full gates; then reread and re-audit that exact commit. V1 repeatedly completed the review/fix portions but never retained the freeze, execution, and final-gate portions.
timeline: 1. Orchestration baseline: `Main` split ownership across shared Python/manifests/tests, required IRC coordination, and prohibited worker-run tests, linters, formatters, mypy, Lake, and other gates. The retained Main record ends at `eval(py) ⇒ pending`; no final integration command or result exists.

Initial v1 feature wave: `PublishAndStatus`, `VerifiedArtifactInput`, `EmptyOutputRetry`, `FrontierProfiles`, and `FrontierCampaigns` added publication/status, verified-artifact import, blank-output retry receipts, generic frontier profiles, and the two CMV campaigns. Tests were authored but not run. Concurrent appends to `tests/test_campaign_builder.py` collided repeatedly before append regions and ownership were coordinated.

Missing-at-first histories were later supplied: `PinnedVerifiedArtifact` added provenance pins, and `SecurePublication` added `PublishSpec.root`, full-plan approval, `publish-plan`, shared locking, staged verification, and transactional publication logic. None of these histories ran tests.

Sandbox/environment review wave: `SandboxSecurityReview` found CB-SBX-001..006 critical/high issues, then statically closed that exact set after remediation; `HermeticEnvReview` found inline-secret, Lean-fingerprint, cleanup, interruption, and inaccessible-directory defects, then reported its current tree correct. Post-fix audits found adjacent defects missed by the targeted assignments: `PostFixCrashAudit` found exact identities collapsed by `{target.pid: target}`; `PostFixSecurityAudit` found proof-gate acceptance despite truncated trusted output; `PostFixCoherenceAudit` found rejection of legitimate verified journal-ahead state and stale research products surviving source-checkpoint rerun.

There is no retained frozen-tree focused/full test run, no final Main gate, and no final post-fix coherence/crash/security audit closing the remaining P1s. A parent-reported 157-test pass and real-Lean smoke pass lack commands/output and are not audit evidence.
v2_requirements: Release record: freeze one commit and retain command, environment/toolchain fingerprint, exit status, complete output, and artifact links for every focused test, full suite, parser/DAG check, formatter/linter/type check, Lake/Lean smoke, multiprocess test, crash/fault injection, and end-to-end plan→approve→publish flow.

Finding traceability: every incident must retain ID, explicit severity or “unassigned,” exact symbol/path/line on the frozen commit, trigger/attack sequence, expected invariant, minimal fix, regression name, executed result, and independent post-fix disposition. Rerun the lost `PublicationSecurity` and recovery-map reviews rather than inventing their missing payloads.

Close Lean P1s before release: eliminate shared compiler stdout/stderr as authority; reject truncation before parsing; produce a controller-authenticated complete result bound to rendered-contract digest and exact declaration; remove or attest any second project-controlled `lake env`; keep trusted sources/artifacts/dependencies outside candidate-writable resolution; run forged-marker, conflicting-tail/truncation, Lakefile-decoy, helper/module replacement, declaration-confusion, and workspace-mutation tests on the pinned Lean v4.33.0-rc2 toolchain.

Close process identity P1: define formal group/session ownership across leader exit and numeric reuse; persist complete controller/member/group/session identities; authenticate each signaled member with pidfd plus start time; never broadcast to unauthenticated membership; preserve same-PID historical records in targets/outcomes; test leader exit, surviving descendants, deterministic PID/PGID reuse, `EPERM`, `EMFILE`, exact unregister, and controller reaping.

Close coherence P1s: accept only structurally/hash-verified monotonic journal-ahead state during mirror repair; before source-checkpoint rerun, invalidate/delete all retained research and downstream evidence; add focused crash/resume contamination tests.

Publication: retain side-effect-free `_validate_pending_publication_receipt` before every nonterminal mutation; exact schema/path/token/plan/approval/recovery identity validation; destination lock held from recovery through cleanup in fixed order after run lock; full-plan canonical digest; exact staged re-verification; no-follow/special-entry/hardlink policy; data and directory fsync; irreversible commit; narrow evidence repair; and injected failures around every marker, rename, fsync, preserve move, receipt, and cleanup step.

Runtime/journal: publish a machine-checkable event schema with sequence, previous hash, current hash, complete state or deterministic delta, durability semantics, and torn-tail handling; reconstruct projections deterministically; serialize every control-plane operation under the run lock; test crash points for initialization, attempt start/end, retry, approval, stop, strategy, replay, publication, evidence refresh, and process registration.

Evidence: baseline after every successful stage transition before dependents launch; verify before any resume consumption or reindex; permit only exact controller/current-running-attempt paths; fail missing terminal evidence; test first interrupted attempt, upstream-success SIGKILL, finalized retry, terminal state, unrelated drift, and all feature-specific checkpoint layouts.

Retry/handoff: journal `pending_output_cleanup` before operator and routed deletion; resume cleanup idempotently; invalidate downstream approvals/promotions/research; remove stale handoff after inventory before each producer attempt; reject directory/FIFO/device/special entries; execute all retry and stale-handoff regressions.

Processes/units/stop-all: durable canonical ownership before launch; deadline-derived `RuntimeMaxSec`; exact process and unit identities; verify inactive before unregister; ownership-registry-derived run discovery; execute real/fake-systemd SIGKILL and process-tree tests proving no survivors and truthful error reporting.
