Formal benchmark: Lean append/succ/and-swap and CMV certificate oracles require exact declaration signature, pinned build, `#print axioms`, source scan, artifact hashes, and semantic gate where applicable. Score false closure as a hard veto: a model `solved` claim with failed external verification must produce `verification_status=failed`, never solved.

Frontier benchmark: curate at least 20 frozen obligations split among known-playbook hard problems, unresolved frontier mathematics, and high-impact conflicting evidence. Blind the labels from the router. Report Sol precision/recall, but enforce hard invariants separately: no ineligible Sol call and no automatic closure from Sol prose. Initial release target: ≥90% correct tier classification overall; tune thresholds from observed results rather than hiding errors in fallback.

Diversity benchmark: attempt same-model, shared-context, same-checkpoint, missing-identity, and producer-as-adjudicator attacks. Assert `independence_status=failed`; then test approved multi-provider/model-family clean-room paths.

Crash/security suite: port P0 contracts from publication, runtime/journal, process identity, sandbox, stale handoff, secret redaction, verified import, and evidence completeness. Routing expectation is deterministic/Terra implementation plus human authority—not Sol. Use state-machine/property tests and privileged Linux lanes where required.

Cost dashboard: per obligation and tier report calls, successful/failed/superseded durations, retry time, queue time, tokens/cost, retained novel artifact bytes, verifier yield, closure yield, and unknown accounting. Compare v2 against v1 without treating ceilings as consumption. Release gates: zero unreceipted invocations, zero execution from null plans, zero fail-open continuation, zero false closures, and zero unexplained model identities.
cost_risks: Repeated Sol planning/repair can dominate cost without adoption, as shown by 1,564.658 s across three planner generations and 1,070.293 s before a second repair. Mitigation: deterministic template bypass, prevalidation, one field-level revision, atomic adoption, and cached decisions keyed by contract/evidence/policy digest.

Monolithic high-tier work can consume full deadlines and retain nothing: 3,601.921 s and 1,500.962 s zero-output failures, plus a 3,007.963 s empty source attempt. Mitigation: staged producer/audit units, early heartbeat/no-progress watchdogs, checkpoint manifests, bounded outputs, and resume from retained partials.

Collapsed retry counters hide both cost and root cause; several runs show `empty_output_retries=1` without invocation detail and one run observed 4/4 role conditions. Mitigation: invocation-level receipts, startup health probe, material-change retry admission, and separate configured/used/observed fields.

Sol over-routing is a major latent risk because many difficult-looking files already have known playbooks. In particular, process shutdown/resource ledgers, sandbox engineering, publication recovery, schemas, and Lean command supervision are code/security tasks, not frontier mathematics. Mitigation: registry match is mandatory and Sol eligibility is audited.

Terra/Luna under-routing can create false economy if weak outputs trigger repeated repair. Mitigation: route by task class and verifier requirements, not file size; cap attempts; escalate only on substantive valid-but-insufficient evidence; stop malformed-output loops.

Scheduler starvation wastes wall time and delays independent evidence even without consuming model compute. Mitigation: ready-queue receipts, bounded starvation SLO, concurrency/resource reasons, and continuation of unaffected dependency cones.

Duplicate immutable snapshots, reports, build trees, and repeated 8,700-job Lean builds create storage/I/O and compilation waste. Mitigation: content-addressed snapshots, Merkle deltas, shared immutable toolchain caches, canonical aliases, and label builds `baseline_only` versus `target_including`.

Human review can become a bottleneck if used for routine state transitions. Mitigation: reserve humans for contract, semantic, security, publication, and corruption authority; provide compact digest-bound review packets and deterministic validation before/after approval.

Provider/model provenance gaps prevent calibration and cost attribution. Mitigation: reject audited model invocations with null provider/model/revision, explicitly mark unavailable usage fields, and never infer model identity from `thinking` strings.

False closure is the highest-impact cost because it can trigger publication and future campaigns on bad evidence. Mitigation: deterministic obligation closure, external replay, formal/exact verifier priority, semantic human gate, and benchmark false-closure veto.

Independent high-tier review can double or triple inference spend. Mitigation: require it only for mandatory/high-impact claims, preserve valid verdicts across selective retries, use deterministic/formal checks first, and route routine claims to Terra rather than Sol.

Frontier criteria can be gamed through self-declared novelty. Mitigation: novelty is an auditable declaration plus method signature; deterministic playbook search, retained failure evidence, independent gap confirmation, and obligation impact are required before Sol.

Strict no-escalation on infrastructure failures may increase blocked runs but avoids paying larger models to diagnose missing dependencies or sandbox faults. Mitigation: fast deterministic preflight, typed health probes, and a separate infrastructure-recovery budget.

Instrumentation itself adds overhead. Mitigation: append O(1) typed events, stream/hash bounded spools, checkpoint changed bytes only, use content addressing and deduplication, and benchmark transition cost as O(changed bytes + new events), not O(total run size).
deterministic_first: 1. Canonicalize and freeze the task: task ID, target/obligation IDs, source and artifact digests, allowed axioms, policy version, risk class, and required output schema.

2. Match against the versioned playbook registry by capability ID and preconditions—not prompt keywords. If exactly one playbook matches, compile its steps, tools, timeout, attempts, parallelism, and failure behavior deterministically.

3. Run cheap falsification before generation: strict schema checks, path/DAG checks, exact arithmetic, small counterexample search, static Lean contract checks, dependency/toolchain preflight, retained-source reuse, and existing-evidence replay.

4. If a deterministic implementation exists, run it and verify the receipt. Do not call Luna/Terra/Sol for manifest parsing, graph closure, status computation, benchmark answer checking, path safety, or success determination.
5. If bounded language work remains, route to Luna with a generated schema and read-only evidence. Reject semantic auto-repair; only deterministic syntax repair is allowed.

6. If the task needs substantive code reasoning, routine mathematics, or formal repair under a known method, route to Terra. Derive operational fields in the controller; the model proposes only mathematical/code content and declared capability needs.

7. Instantiate the Sol Planner only when the frontier gate proves that a mandatory mathematical obligation is unresolved and no registered playbook or retained result discharges it. Sol returns a typed mathematical plan; deterministic policy compiles the execution plan and budget.

8. Before expensive descendants, require a signed continuation receipt aggregating pilot outputs. The gate must identify accepted/rejected/unknown claims and exact artifact hashes and must explicitly say `continue`.
9. Compute closure deterministically over the obligation DAG. Sol/human prose is evidence input, never the closure algorithm.

10. On failure, classify first: contract/schema, infrastructure, resource, evidence-integrity, mathematical refutation, mathematical unresolved, semantic unclear, or policy/approval. Infrastructure and contract failures go to deterministic repair, not a higher reasoning tier.
escalation_rules: Deterministic→Luna: only when all hard validation passes, the remaining operation is bounded extraction/rendering, output has an exact schema, and no field controls truth, security, budget, path, capability, or status. Maximum 2 invocations: initial plus one syntax/omission repair. A second invalid output terminalizes as `MODEL_CONTRACT_FAILED`; it does not escalate for intelligence.

Luna→Terra: trigger when deterministic task classification marks substantive cross-artifact/code reasoning or mathematical entailment, or when a valid Luna artifact fails a substantive deterministic verifier. Do not trigger on malformed JSON, blank output, timeout, missing dependency, or sandbox failure. Maximum 2 Terra producer attempts, each materially different and separately receipted.

Terra retry admission: require a prior limitation code, a materially different method signature, and an expected new machine-checkable artifact. Whitespace, paraphrase, higher token budget alone, or a different prompt wrapper is not novelty. Preserve accepted verdicts and retry only implicated obligations.

Terra→Sol invention: all must hold: (1) a mandatory primary-target obligation remains `UNRESOLVED_MATH`; (2) deterministic preflight and all applicable registered playbooks are exhausted; (3) at least two materially distinct Terra attempts have valid receipts, unless the task is preclassified by the approved contract as frontier; (4) at least one independent Terra audit confirms the gap rather than an infrastructure failure; (5) no deterministic counterexample or kernel rejection already settles it; (6) remaining Sol budget is positive; and (7) expected impact is primary-target closure or removal of a blocking high-value uncertainty.

Sol Planner admission: the controller emits `frontier_eligible=true` with unresolved obligation IDs, playbook-search result, retained failed-method signatures, source-gap status, maximum Sol calls, and a plan-output schema. Without that receipt, no Planner call is legal. Routine projects use deterministic plan templates plus Luna/Terra task filling and never invoke the named Planner.

Terra/Sol→Sol adjudication: allowed only for a conflict on a mandatory mathematical claim where independent producer/verifier artifacts are schema-valid and evidence-bearing, deterministic replay cannot decide, and a wrong acceptance could close or materially redirect the campaign. The adjudicator must receive frozen artifacts without hidden producer dialogue and must issue one verdict per claim.

Sol→human: required for `UNCLEAR` informal-to-formal correspondence, source interpretation that changes the target, security capability exceptions, publication/destructive actions, contract amendments, authenticity/corruption disputes, or unresolved disagreement between two independent Sol judgments. Human cannot waive kernel failure or fabricate missing evidence.

Immediate no-escalation stops: deterministic refutation; Lean/kernel failure on the exact required declaration; missing mandatory evidence; budget exhaustion; untrusted/tampered artifact; invalid target substitution; unauthorized capability; sandbox preflight failure. These become typed blocked/refuted/failed outcomes.

Measurable rate limits per obligation: Luna ≤2 calls; Terra producer ≤2 methods plus ≤1 independent Terra verification; Sol Planner ≤1 initial plus ≤1 evidence-linked revision; Sol invention ≤2 attempts; Sol adjudication ≤1, with a second independent Sol only when policy labels impact `critical`; human review count is explicit. Any override requires a digest-bound human budget amendment.

No-output watchdog: preserve heartbeat/tool activity and checkpoint at the earlier of 10 minutes or 25% of the task deadline; terminate or checkpoint a no-progress invocation at the earlier of 20 minutes or 50% of deadline. A retry requires a health probe or material configuration change. This directly addresses 1,500–3,600 s zero-output v1 incidents.

Scheduler rule: every dispatch cycle records the ready set and selection. If a required independent root waits longer than the lesser of 5 minutes or 20% of its phase budget while capacity exists, emit `STARVATION_POLICY_VIOLATION` and schedule it or explain a typed resource conflict.
planner_policy: Planner identity: Sol. The role is a mathematical decomposition/invention planner, not the operational scheduler and not the owner of tier, tools, timeout, retries, parallelism, security grants, or failure transitions.

Admission packet: immutable problem/success-contract hash; target and obligation registry; retained source/evidence inventory; known-playbook matches; failed method signatures; deterministic falsification results; unresolved frontier rationale; allowed capabilities; remaining aggregate budget; and required typed plan schema.

Allowed outputs: `plan`, `infeasible`, or `contract_invalid`. A plan contains obligation-preserving task proposals, method signatures, prerequisite evidence, falsification pilots, one explicit continuation gate, and expected evidence classes. Operational values are recommendations only and are overwritten by deterministic policy.

Required structure: preserve exact primary target; decompose by obligations; pilot each expensive strategy; identify distinct methods by mathematical signature; specify what observation falsifies each lane; require independent audit before promotion; distinguish source, semantic, formal, exact, interval, numeric, and prose evidence.

Forbidden Planner behavior: path validation, DAG acceptance, success determination, model/provider self-selection, raw command authorization, changing the target, waiving evidence, marking solved, authorizing continuation, or using prose to override policy.

Deterministic acceptance: validate exact schema, IDs, DAG, phase reachability, gate uniqueness and fail-closed semantics, budget ceilings, capability catalog, target fidelity, evidence contracts, method-signature distinctness, and infeasible/contract-invalid consistency before adoption.

Repair policy: at most one Sol revision, supplied only the validator’s structured defect codes and prior-plan hash. Store generated→validator-failed→repaired→accepted/abandoned lifecycle events and a machine-readable field diff. Never regenerate the full plan for a local policy defect.

Known-playbook bypass: when every mandatory obligation maps to an approved template and no frontier gap exists, the controller compiles the plan without invoking Planner. Luna/Terra may populate bounded task content, but this is recorded as template execution, not a Sol plan.

Adoption is atomic: descendants cannot schedule while `adopted_plan_digest` is null. The state stores schema version, Planner identity, prompt/input digests, validator version, accepted plan digest, budget compilation digest, and supersession lineage.

Plan quality metrics: zero target substitutions; zero fail-open gates; 100% required-obligation coverage; 100% DAG/policy validity before adoption; ≤1 repair; and no campaign execution from a null/unaccepted plan.
principles: Control-plane invariance: schema parsing, exact-key checks, canonicalization, DAG/closure, routing, budgets, capability grants, scheduling, retries, hashing, state transitions, success computation, and receipt validation are deterministic. No model may upgrade its own result or authorize continuation.

Playbook-first routing: if a task matches a registered v1 playbook and its inputs/outputs can be expressed in a typed contract, execute it with deterministic code or the cheapest qualified model. Model novelty claims are never sufficient to bypass a playbook.

Evidence-strength separation: keep execution status, artifact validity, mathematical status, semantic status, and approval status distinct. `process_succeeded` never implies `claim_verified` or `campaign_solved`.

Sol scarcity rule: the named Planner is Sol, but it is instantiated only after deterministic frontier eligibility. Sol is otherwise reserved for genuinely unresolved frontier mathematics or high-impact mathematical adjudication. Known implementation, parsing, orchestration, testing, and recovery playbooks are not Sol work.

Human authority is narrow and explicit: humans own campaign/success contracts, authoritative informal-to-formal equivalence, security-policy acceptance, destructive publication approval, and exceptional corruption adjudication. Humans do not perform routine controller transitions.

Machine authority dominates where available: exact arithmetic, certificate checkers, Lean kernel/build/axiom checks, strict parsers, and reproducible commands outrank Luna/Terra/Sol prose. A model verdict cannot overrule a valid kernel or deterministic counterexample receipt.

Obligation-level routing: route and retry only the unresolved obligation, proposal, verifier, or repair stage. Preserve valid independent evidence and never rerun an entire campaign merely because one obligation failed.

Fail-closed continuation: expensive descendants require a signed/hash-bound deterministic continuation decision naming satisfied lane criteria. Optional-gate failure, `failure_policy=continue`, planner prose, or process success cannot authorize descendants.

Budget before inference: deterministically cap total attempts, wall time, tokens, model tiers, parallelism, revisions, retries, and autonomous rounds before any model call; enforce continuously, not only in post-hoc metrics.

Evidence anchors from v1: repeated planner rework without adopted plans (`20260824T232129Z-003b99`, 1,564.658 s), monolithic x-high timeouts (`20260824T165745Z-caad31`, 3,601.921 s; `20260824T190417Z-90df1d`, 1,500.962 s), empty-output retries hidden by aggregate fields, a 643 s active stage with no invocation/terminal receipt (`20260824T235503Z-841a3c`), and starvation of independent roots justify deterministic preflight, staged execution, explicit retry ledgers, checkpointing, and scheduler receipts.
producer_reviewer_diversity: A verifier must be a separately launched principal with no producer conversation, hidden scratch state, writable canonical workspace, or unreviewed summaries. It sees only frozen source/proposal artifacts and the verification rubric.

Minimum routine mathematical review: Terra producer + independently instantiated Terra verifier + deterministic closure. For formal claims, add the Lean/exact verifier; model diversity never substitutes for the kernel.

High-impact claim review: Terra or Sol producer + verifier differing in at least two of `{provider, model family, checkpoint/version, organization}` where available. If only one provider is approved, require different model family/checkpoint plus clean-room context and record the limitation.

Sol adjudication must be a third identity, not the Sol Planner or producer. It receives proposal and verdict digests, disagreement codes, and evidence inventory; it cannot silently rewrite the claim statement.

Semantic equivalence: authoritative human reviewer must not be the artifact producer or contract author when impact is high. Sol may provide a nonauthoritative review, but the human receipt owns the final relation.
Security/publication: human approver must be distinct from the implementer for high-impact changes; deterministic tests and transaction receipts remain mandatory.

Mechanically compute `independence_status` from retained identities and context lineage. Values: `satisfied`, `degraded_with_approved_exception`, or `failed`. Self-asserted phrases such as “cold” or “independent” have no effect.

Verifier coverage is claim-complete: exactly one terminal verdict per proposal claim, all mandatory targets covered, disagreements retained, and no verdict may repair statement/scope/quantifiers. A changed statement creates a new content hash and restarts review.
Promotion requires a downstream, successful, audit-classified verifier edge carrying evidence hashes. Same-stage, same-context, failed, or evidence-free reviews cannot promote knowledge.
receipt_fields: Envelope: `artifact_type`, `schema_version`, `producer_version`, `campaign_id`, `run_id`, `stage_id`, `attempt_id`, `invocation_id`, sequence, prior/current event hash, creation time plus monotonic timing anchor, anti-replay nonce, intended consumers, payload hash, signature/attestation.

Routing decision: task/obligation IDs, route `{deterministic|Luna|Terra|Sol|human}`, task class, risk/impact, matched playbook ID/version, eligibility predicates with pass/fail values, alternatives rejected with reason codes, escalation parent receipt, approver if any, and policy/budget digest.

Model identity: provider, endpoint, model family/name, exact revision/checkpoint, context limit, reasoning/effort setting, decoding parameters, seed if supported, wrapper/executable hash, prompt-template hash, rendered-input hash, tool policy, network/sandbox state, and clean-room/context-lineage ID.

Invocation lifecycle: configured retry allowance; ordinal; launch/start/end timestamps; queue/setup/run/drain/cleanup durations; monotonic deadline; PID/pidfd/start time/session/process-group/cgroup or unit identity; typed terminal cause; signal/exit code; heartbeat/checkpoint events; and retry trigger/change/disposition.

Compute: input/output/cached/reasoning tokens where available; provider-reported usage; wall/CPU/GPU time; peak RSS; tool and Lean time; measured/estimated/unknown labels; monetary cost; missing-data reason; aggregate budget before/after. Never infer consumption from timeout ceilings.

Inputs: canonical content-addressed source inventory, target/contract hash, plan/project/outcome digests, toolchain/executable hashes, cwd capability, environment-policy digest, before-workspace/Merkle root, and source locators/version/license where relevant.

Outputs: bounded stdout/stderr representation and full-stream digest, output byte count/truncation status, exact output schema, artifact hashes/sizes/canonical run-relative locators, after-workspace root, added/modified/deleted mutation manifest, freshness token, atomic publication result, retention/checkpoint status.

Validation: parser/validator version, exact error codes and field paths, deterministic commands with argv/cwd/environment digest, exit status, stdout/stderr hashes, Lean declaration/type hash, toolchain/build/axiom receipt, certificate replay, mutation-test outcomes, verifier identity, and replay recipe.

Mathematical evidence: claim/content hash distinct from campaign instance ID, target and obligation scopes, evidence class, assumptions/domain/quantifiers, dependencies, producer/verifier edges, one verdict per claim, disagreement/adjudication record, semantic relation/issues, limitations, and deterministic closure result.

Status separation: `controller_status`, `execution_status`, `artifact_status`, `verification_status`, `semantic_status`, `scientific_status`, `gate_decision`, and `outcome_reason`; include timestamps for execution end, validation, outcome classification, strategy selection, and administrative closure.

Scheduler: ready set, selected task, capacity and `max_parallel`, resource conflict, queue duration, starvation clock, preemption/cancellation reason, dependency state, and why each ready independent root was or was not launched.

Completeness: manifest of expected stages/records, present/missing/malformed counts, slice first/last sequence, whole-run versus partial-slice declaration, external telemetry completeness, and a prohibition on `complete=true` unless all hashes and terminal records verify.
tier_matrix: DETERMINISTIC — Eligibility: known algorithm or policy with typed inputs and a machine-checkable oracle. Work: all config/project/model/handoff/artifact/journal/inspection/metrics/runtime state logic; path confinement; schema migration; DAG/status/claim closure; budget assignment; command and Lean verification; capability compilation; benchmark adjudication; exact/numeric tools; routing itself. Examples: `config.py`, `project.py`, `models.py`, `handoff.py`, `artifacts.py`, `journal.py`, deterministic portions of `claims.py`, `semantic.py`, `runtime.py`, `features.py`, and all calibration certificate checkers. Exit: typed result or typed failure only; never escalate merely because parsing or infrastructure failed.

LUNA — Eligibility: bounded routine language transformation with no unresolved mathematics, no security authority, and deterministic output validation. Work: CLI/help adapters, structured extraction from already retained sources, report rendering from adjudicated records, protocol facade maintenance, low-risk fixture/docs normalization, elementary exposition after a deterministic certificate exists. Examples: `cli.py`, `herdr.py` facade work, routine source metadata extraction, Markdown rendering, elementary benchmark explanations. Luna may not choose paths, tools, budgets, status, claim truth, or continuation.

TERRA — Eligibility: a known playbook requires nontrivial code reasoning, routine mathematical proposal/checking, formal proof repair, or execution-kernel implementation, but no demonstrated frontier gap exists. Work: unified subprocess supervisor (`command.py`/`agent_runner.py`), process registry and resource-ledger implementation, benchmark integrity work, routine Lean proof repair, mathematical proposal and independent verification under typed contracts, semantic review only as nonauthoritative input. Terra executes known playbooks; it does not redesign controller policy. The v1 `processes.py` label of Sol is overridden for ordinary transactional shutdown/resource-ledger implementation because the input already supplies the playbook.

SOL — Eligibility: the deterministic frontier gate passes. Work only: (a) the named Planner for a genuinely unresolved mathematical campaign, producing obligation decomposition and distinct methods; (b) invention on a mandatory frontier obligation after cheaper evidence-bearing attempts fail; or (c) high-impact mathematical adjudication where accepting the wrong verdict could falsely close a primary target. Relevant examples include unresolved CMV source-to-model/reduced-boundary geometry, inverse/asymptotic bridges, or conflicting theorem-level evidence—not parser, scheduler, process, publication, or sandbox engineering.

HUMAN — Eligibility: authority cannot safely be delegated or the issue is not purely mathematical. Work: freeze/approve problem and success contracts; authoritative informal-to-formal equivalence (`semantic.py`); sandbox/security threat-model approval (`sandbox.py`); destructive publication approval/recovery (`publication.py`); policy decisions in `regime.py`/`autonomy.py`; source/license exceptions; exceptional corruption adjudication. Human output is itself digest-bound and independently validated before a controller transition.

FORMAL/EXACT VERIFIER — Not a model tier but an authority lane: Lean kernel/build/axiom audit, exact arithmetic, certificate checker, schema validator, deterministic counterexample search, and replay service. It can reject any model tier. A positive model review never substitutes for this lane where a verifier contract exists.

compute_waste: The clearest implementation waste was repeated authoring of unexecuted regressions and concurrent collisions in `tests/test_campaign_builder.py`; these created design intent but little assurance evidence.

The largest campaign waste class was monolithic no-checkpoint work: `scalar_checker_pilot` lost about 3601.921 invocation-seconds with zero output, and `scalar_formula_topology` lost about 1500.962 invocation-seconds with zero output.

Empty-output work was repeatedly expensive: `source_reconstruction` lost 3007.963 seconds before retry, and `source_carrier_producer` used 3002.488 seconds on an exit-0/no-output invocation before retry. V2 must checkpoint and terminate no-progress work earlier.

Planner churn consumed multiple hundreds to thousands of seconds per run without durable generated→validated→accepted/superseded lifecycle records. Later candidates often existed while authoritative state still had `plan=null`.

`20260824T235503Z-841a3c` held `exact_certificate_pilot` active for 643 seconds before interruption without a terminal invocation receipt, promoted artifact, handoff, summary, or checkpointed novel product.

`20260815T202603Z-dc18b6` spent 1803 seconds on a timed-out API attempt, at least 1:14:02 on superseded successful API/synthesizer work, and repeated final contract/promotion after initial completion without retained rationale.

Duplicate immutable baselines, recovery copies, assessment mirrors, outcomes, and build caches caused avoidable storage/I/O. Content-addressed deduplication is required; planned timeout budgets must never be reported as consumed compute.
Compute accounting must remain qualified: wall duration is not CPU/GPU/token/billed compute, and configured quotas are not consumption. Missing telemetry prevents stronger cost claims.
failure_classes: Global code completion is not established. Numerous source edits landed, but there is no retained frozen commit, Main integration result, full test run, formatter/linter/type-check/Lake gate, end-to-end campaign test, or final post-fix audit on one immutable tree.

Open P1 Lean-trust blockers remain: trusted facts parsed from shared compiler stdout, a second project-controlled `lake env`, acceptance despite stdout/stderr truncation, and no retained controller-authenticated complete report bound to exact declaration and rendered-contract digest.
Open P1 process-ownership concern remains: per-member pidfds do not have a final retained proof or deterministic test establishing original PGID/SID provenance after leader exit and numeric reuse.
Open P1 coherence defects remain: legitimate verified journal-ahead state may be rejected during mirror repair, and source-checkpoint rerun may retain stale research products and downstream evidence.

Campaign-definition closure is absent: the required-approval versus uninterrupted-one-command contradiction, missing bridge DAG gate, overbroad boundary profile, wrong source-challenge profile, and non-proof-producing repair route were not closed by a retained manifest edit plus parser/DAG execution.

Publication hardening is source-only. No retained multiprocess or fault-injection matrix proves malformed-receipt no-mutation, canonical destination alias locking, staged re-verification, preserve/swap safety, fsync ordering, irreversible commit, rollback safety, terminal evidence repair, or idempotent recovery.

Runtime/recovery hardening is source-only. No retained crash-boundary matrix proves journal authority, retry intent before deletion, evidence verification before resume consumption, handoff freshness, Herdr create/register recovery, process-tree shutdown, or systemd ownership cleanup.

Secret, sandbox, and replay closure is static and incomplete as release evidence. No executed alternate-key secret, output/receipt/workspace/evidence, mode-000/symlink/interruption cleanup, cgroup failure, executable/environment replay fingerprint, or evidence immutability matrix is retained.

The retained campaign series is mathematically unsolved overall. No run establishes the exact target `CMVConjecture.cmv_conjecture_3_12`, complete subcutoff coverage, source normalization and finite-perimeter carrier transfer, exact theorem `#check`, allowed-axiom `#print axioms`, or final independent audit.

Operational termination was repeatedly confused with completion: controller `complete`, evidence-package `complete`, process `succeeded`, audit process `succeeded`, and generic `PASS` appeared alongside incomplete DAGs, rejected findings, stopped gates, detached evidence, and unsolved mathematics.

Several runs have stale or incomplete lifecycle records: active children left `running` after parent stop, planner outputs not adopted while state remained `plan=null`, failed stages left serialized as running, missing invocation receipts, detached artifacts, missing model identity, and absent interruption actor/signal/reason.

Review evidence itself was lossy: `PublicationSecurity` finding bodies, `RecoveryStateMap` schema, exact line locations/severities, and some final Lean/process findings were truncated or opaque. Missing payloads must be rerun, not reconstructed.
review_lessons: Use orthogonal claims. A landed edit, source-verified fix, focused test pass, campaign completion, mathematical solution, and assurance pass are different facts and must never be collapsed into `done`, `success`, or `PASS`.

Freeze first, then review and execute. Moving-tree reviews were useful for withdrawing stale findings, but they could not provide release closure. All final gates and independent audits must target the same immutable commit and artifact set.

Keep review scopes explicit. A scoped `no P0/P1` verdict closes only its named threat model; later system, coherence, Lean, process, and secret reviews showed why a narrow verdict cannot be promoted to release approval.

Separate producer and adversarial reviewer trust. The most valuable findings came from reviewers using different models: DAG/operator semantics, malicious filesystem state, alternate-key secret values, crash boundaries, process reuse, and forged Lean output.

Every exact finding needs durable traceability: ID, severity or `unassigned`, frozen symbol/path/line, trigger sequence, violated invariant, owner, patch, regression, executed result, and independent post-fix disposition.

Review output is a release artifact. Structured payloads must not be hidden behind truncated `yield(result)` summaries; complete machine-readable findings and human-readable attack traces must be retained.

Focused tracing beats broad churn. Narrow symbol ownership, shared contracts such as one run lock and one evidence-repair verifier, and targeted current-tree rereads were productive; repeated broad grep/full-file passes and concurrent test appends were not.

A continuation gate returning `stop` can be a successful assurance action. Conversely, an audit process exiting 0 can carry a rejecting verdict. Process outcome and semantic verdict require separate fields.
Campaign data needs its own audit. Manifest DAG, profile role, approval semantics, routing, and immutable contract dependencies are not Python/runtime defects and are not mathematical proof defects.

Crash testing must enumerate durable boundaries, not just normal paths: intent before mutation, journal before projection, registration before launch/create, data and directory fsync before markers, irreversible commit, and evidence verification before repair or consumption.
security_requirements: Close all open Lean P1s before release: shared compiler stdout/stderr cannot be the authority; truncation must fail before parsing; the controller must authenticate a complete report bound to exact declaration, rendered-contract digest, source/toolchain/dependency hashes, and invocation identity; remove or attest any project-controlled second `lake env`.

Keep trusted Lean sources, rendered contracts, helpers, compiled artifacts, dependency roots, and report channels outside candidate-writable paths. Run forged-marker, conflicting-tail/truncation, Lakefile-decoy, helper/module replacement, declaration-confusion, substitution-injection, and workspace-mutation tests on the pinned toolchain.

Define formal process/group/session ownership across leader exit and PID/PGID/SID reuse. Persist complete historical identities, authenticate every signaled member with pidfd plus start time, never broadcast to unauthenticated membership, preserve same-PID records, and test deterministic reuse, EPERM, EMFILE, reaping, survivors, and exact unregister.

Register canonical process/unit ownership durably before launch; enforce deadline-derived `RuntimeMaxSec`; discover stop-all targets from ownership registries; verify inactive before unregister; treat identity mismatch, unverifiable liveness, cleanup failure, and non-ESRCH errors as survivors/errors.

Publication must validate the entire pending receipt before any mutation; bind exact root/destination/source/preserve policy/plan/approval/recovery identity; lock run then canonical destination; reject traversal, overlaps, symlinks, special entries, and policy-forbidden hardlinks; reverify staging; fsync data/directories; enforce irreversible commit; and fault-inject every boundary.

Secrets must be controlled by value, not key name, across config, argv, env, stdout/stderr, receipts, workspace, evidence, checkpoints, success/failure/timeout/interruption, symlinks, and inaccessible directories. Sandboxed commands receive no declared secret values unless campaign-wide trusted execution is explicit.

All command classes—agents, Lean, replay, publication helpers, and regime meta-agents—must use one explicit containment/environment contract. Cleanup must fail closed and surface cgroup, permission, symlink, and interruption errors.

Replay must freeze and attest executable, argv, environment, dependencies, toolchain, sandbox policy, and inputs; verify evidence before and after replay; and reject changed tools/environments or mutation of covered evidence.

Verified-artifact import requires all three pins together: expected campaign ID, expected run ID, and lowercase evidence SHA-256. Hash raw evidence before trust; cross-check evidence/state/directory identities; import only evidence-indexed nonempty regular files under a safe no-symlink prefix; test every mismatch/tamper/partial-pin case.

Runtime resume must verify evidence before consuming retained success, checkpoints, strategy state, publication state, or terminal state. Repair permissions must be exact-path allowlists, never broad writable trees.

Campaign manifests are security/assurance inputs: approval semantics, immutable contract gates, profile scope, research roles, repair targets, and root/pin fields must be parser-validated and DAG-audited before acceptance.

No release while any P0/P1 is open, disputed without a final ruling, untested after fix, or represented only by a parent assertion. Missing historical finding payloads must be rerun under the v2 threat model.
state_machine_requirements: Maintain independent top-level dimensions: `code_status`, `controller_status`, `campaign_status`, `mathematical_status`, `assurance_status`, `publication_status`, and `incident_status`. No field may imply another.

`CODE_COMPLETE` means the intended implementation scope is integrated on a named frozen commit, ownership conflicts are resolved, generated/schema migrations are present, and no known scope item is missing. It does not mean tests passed, the campaign completed, the mathematics is solved, or assurance passed.

`CAMPAIGN_COMPLETE` means an adopted hash-bound plan exists; every required stage has a terminal acceptable semantic outcome; all mandatory gates explicitly authorize continuation; required evidence and handoffs are indexed; active children are reconciled; and finalization is journaled. A controller that is merely `COMPLETE`, `STOPPED`, `FAILED`, or `INTERRUPTED` is only terminal, not necessarily campaign-complete.

`MATHEMATICALLY_SOLVED` means the immutable target statement is established at its declared trust level and scope, all configured mathematical obligations are discharged, coverage has no gaps, required source/bridge obligations hold, and exact theorem/build/axiom evidence is retained. Bounded rows, conditional contracts, agent prose, modeled cutoff theorems, or generic `PASS` cannot set this state.

`ASSURANCE_PASSED` means all mandatory focused tests, full gates, fault-injection matrices, security/crash/coherence reviews, and release checks passed on the same frozen commit with complete retained output and no open P0/P1. Source reread, parent assertion, skipped test, or scoped audit cannot set this state.

The hash-chained journal is authoritative and `state.json` is a replaceable projection. Events require schema version, monotonic sequence, previous hash, current hash, actor, operation, complete state or deterministic delta, durability point, and torn-tail handling.

Every control-plane mutation—start, resume, stop, retry, approval, evidence refresh, strategy, replay, publication, process registration, and finalization—must reconstruct from the latest validated journal and execute under the canonical `.campaign.lock`.

Plans require explicit `GENERATED → VALIDATOR_FAILED|VALIDATED → ACCEPTED|SUPERSEDED|ABANDONED` transitions with parent hash and structured diff. No task may start while `state.plan=null`; prose/control-field contradictions must fail validation.

Stage and attempt states require separate process and semantic outcomes: `PENDING`, `RUNNABLE`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `PROCESS_SUCCEEDED`, `PROCESS_FAILED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `INTERRUPTED`, `ARTIFACT_VALIDATED`, `SEMANTIC_ACCEPTED`, `SEMANTIC_REJECTED`, `SKIPPED`, and `CANCELLED`. Exit 0 alone never yields semantic acceptance.

Interruption is atomic and typed: record actor/reason/signal/exit code, journal cancellation intent, terminate and reap owned process/unit trees, terminalize every active attempt/stage, checkpoint partial outputs, reconcile parent/child status, and only then mark the controller terminal.

Retry requires a durable intent before deletion, durable `pending_output_cleanup`, idempotent resume cleanup, fresh handoff generation per attempt, invalidation of approvals/promotions/downstream artifacts/research, and explicit retry ordinal/cause/budget.

Evidence must be indexed after every successful stage transition before dependents run. Resume must verify retained evidence before dependency/checkpoint/terminal consumption or reindexing, with only exact controller/current-attempt paths allowed to differ.

Verified monotonic journal-ahead state must be repairable into the projection; malformed, non-monotonic, hash-invalid, or semantically illegal state must fail closed. Source-checkpoint rerun must clear stale research and all derived evidence first.

Continuation gates are structurally fail-closed: `required=true`, failure policy stop/abort, signed decision bound to plan/input/evidence hashes, and descendants schedulable only on explicit `continue`.

Publication has an explicit transaction: `PLANNED → APPROVED → PREPARED → SWAPPED → COMMIT_DURABLE → CLEANED`, with validated recovery states and terminal `PUBLISHED|ROLLED_BACK|FAILED`. A durable commit can only be forward-repaired, never rolled back.

Finalization records separate timestamps for execution end, assessment, scientific disposition, strategy selection, publication disposition, assurance disposition, and administrative closure. Reopening creates a new revision rather than mutating an earlier completion.
status_vocabulary: `EDIT_LANDED`: source change exists. No correctness implication.
`SOURCE_VERIFIED`: reviewer confirmed current-tree symbols/control flow. No execution implication.
`CODE_COMPLETE`: scoped implementation is integrated on a frozen commit with no known missing code in scope. No campaign, mathematical, or assurance implication.
`FOCUSED_TEST_PASSED`: named command passed on named commit and environment. It does not imply full-suite or release assurance.
`FULL_GATES_PASSED`: all declared build/test/lint/type/parser gates passed on one frozen commit. It still does not imply mathematical solution or independent assurance.
`PROCESS_SUCCEEDED`: subprocess exited acceptably and produced its expected receipt. Its semantic result may be reject/stop/unsolved.
`CAMPAIGN_TERMINAL`: controller reached `COMPLETE`, `STOPPED`, `FAILED`, or `INTERRUPTED`. This is not campaign completion.

`CAMPAIGN_COMPLETE`: adopted plan executed all required stages to acceptable semantic outcomes, mandatory gates continued, evidence finalized, and no active child remains. It does not imply mathematical solution.
`MATHEMATICAL_UNSOLVED`: exact target or one or more required mathematical/trust obligations remain open. This is the retained status of the CMV campaign series.
`MATHEMATICALLY_SOLVED`: immutable exact target established with complete declared coverage/source/formal obligations and retained validation. No supplied run reaches this state.
`ASSURANCE_NOT_RUN`: mandatory release gate or final cross-module audit was not executed on the frozen candidate. This is the retained global implementation status.
`ASSURANCE_FAILED`: a mandatory gate found an open blocker or produced an invalid/incomplete result.

`ASSURANCE_PASSED`: all mandatory executed gates and independent reviews passed on the same frozen commit with no open P0/P1 and complete evidence. No supplied implementation record reaches this state.
`ROW_VERIFIED` or `BOUNDED_CERTIFICATE_PASSED`: exact scoped numerical evidence only; must carry `global_coverage=false` while any interval/face/transition is uncovered.
`CONTRACT_UNDISCHARGED`: premises or source/bridge obligations remain open even if arithmetic consequences check.
`PUBLICATION_PROMOTED`: files were copied/promoted internally. Distinct from `PUBLISHED`, which requires terminal publication transaction and receipt recovery.

Current retained verdict: broad source fixes landed, global `CODE_COMPLETE` is not established; some individual campaigns were `CAMPAIGN_COMPLETE`, others merely terminal or partial; the CMV mathematics is `MATHEMATICAL_UNSOLVED`; global release assurance is `ASSURANCE_NOT_RUN` and therefore not passed.

Deduplicate immutable snapshots, recovery baselines, assessment mirrors, outcomes, and build caches by content hash. Keep novel products and mutation diffs separate from baseline copies and account for storage/I/O.

anti_patterns: Generic prompt labeled as a playbook without typed inputs, step DAG, validators, receipts, gates, invalidation, and terminal derivation.
A model choosing its own tool, model tier, timeout, retries, path, parallelism, security capability, failure policy, continuation, or solved status.
Calling Sol because work is expensive, long, cross-module, or failed operationally; Sol is only evidence-admitted frontier planning/revision or separately admitted critical mathematical adjudication.
Treating exit 0, `PASS`, controller `complete`, campaign completion, publication, model confidence, compiled source, or audit-process success as mathematical closure.
Validating one read and hashing another; pathname validate-then-use; parsing receipts by filename/basename/field presence; arbitrary strings as evidence.
Retrying blank, malformed, timed-out, sandbox-failed, or missing-dependency output with a stronger model rather than deterministic recovery.
Whole-campaign rerun for one failed obligation; discarding valid independent evidence; resetting attempts or collapsing retry invocations.
Self-review, shared hidden context, producer-as-adjudicator, writable canonical workspace for verifier, or self-asserted `independent`/`cold` labels.
Silent statement repair: dropping assumptions, changing quantifiers/domains/branches/endpoint strictness, replacing source perimeter with modeled perimeter, or substituting a nearby declaration.
Promoting numeric telemetry, MPFR smoke output, source prose, or model review to exact/formal evidence; averaging conflicting evidence classes.
Reusing stale output/handoff because its path exists; accepting output not bound to current nonce/input/contract/toolchain/policy; keeping old approval after dependency change.
Deleting or overwriting failed, stale, rejected, or corrupt records instead of append-only tombstones and lineage.
Full-state journal replay and whole-tree hashing on every step when incremental event/evidence commits suffice; reporting configured ceilings as consumed compute.
Fail-open continuation from optional gate failure, `failure_policy=continue`, missing decision, process success, or planner prose.
Using human review for routine transitions or using human approval to waive formal rejection, missing evidence, unauthorized capabilities, or deterministic counterexamples.
Mutating a v1 run in place or emitting new v1 schemas; silently restoring defaults/security fields during migration.

Calling a partial certificate global, calling a sufficient decimal cutoff sharp, calling a modeled theorem source-level, or identifying topological frontier with reduced boundary by terminology alone.
Publishing or replaying against a mutable canonical workspace; allowing recovery/planning to mutate before full preflight and lock acquisition.
Opaque review summaries without complete findings, identities, attack trace, evidence refs, and closure verdict.
A playbook result with `succeeded` but missing expected-record manifest, launch/terminal receipts, output-schema validation, freshness check, diversity computation, or limitations.

controller_enforced_rules: The controller, not a model, resolves the playbook, validates its definition, compiles the step DAG, assigns tools/models, checks budgets, schedules steps, evaluates gates, applies invalidation, and derives terminal status.

Every playbook run is bound to immutable `contract_digest`, `input_root`, `policy_digest`, `registry_digest`, definition digest, and anti-replay nonce before preflight. A null or mutable binding blocks execution.

Every step must have a durable launch intent/receipt before side effects and a terminal receipt in `finally`. Missing terminal receipts force `recovering`; they can never be inferred from files, process exit, or prose.

Every declared output is schema-validated, hash-bound, attempt-scoped, atomically published, indexed, and connected to exact inputs and receipts. Existing or stale output cannot satisfy a new attempt.

Universal gates injected into every playbook are: `U0_definition_and_binding`, `U1_preflight_and_budget`, `U2_receipt_completeness`, `U3_output_schema_and_hash`, `U4_invalidation_freshness`, `U5_independent_audit`, `U6_terminal_derivation`. A playbook cannot remove or weaken them.
`U0` checks approved definition status, versions, implementation digest, exact input and contract bindings, known registrations, DAG acyclicity, and output/gate reachability.
`U1` runs deterministic falsification, capability/toolchain preflight, source/evidence replay, path confinement, budget authorization, and checks that no side effect occurred before pass.

`U2` requires one launch and one terminal receipt for every invocation, reconciled process/resource identity, complete expected-record manifest, and explicit unknown telemetry. Zero-output or interrupted attempts remain visible.

`U3` validates exact output schema, cardinality, binding fields, digest/size, atomic publication, mutation policy, and retained evidence completeness. Output parser success on bytes different from hashed bytes is forbidden.

`U4` recomputes the dependency fingerprint and transitive invalidation closure immediately before audit and terminal derivation. Changed dependencies tombstone outputs, revoke approvals, and reset affected reviews.

`U5` computes independence from identities and context lineage, enforces claim-complete verdict coverage, and requires formal/exact authority where available. Failed or degraded-unapproved diversity blocks success.
`U6` derives result from mandatory step/gate/output states. Process success, model confidence, generic `PASS`, configured completion, or publication cannot set playbook success.

Required mathematical routine audit is a producer principal plus separately launched clean-room Terra verifier plus deterministic/formal checks where available. High-impact review must differ in at least two registered identity dimensions where available; approved exceptions are digest-bound and cannot omit formal checks.

Sol is never an executor, verifier of its own plan, scheduler, gate decider, or closure authority. Sol may only emit a typed plan or one evidence-linked revision after a controller-issued frontier/adjudication eligibility receipt.

The controller rejects target, quantifier, domain, assumption, perimeter-semantics, candidate-universe, declaration, or endpoint changes as output repair. Such changes create a new contract/content hash and require new review.
Machine authority dominates prose: deterministic counterexample, exact checker, Lean kernel/build/axiom receipt, strict schema validator, and reproducible replay can reject any Luna/Terra/Sol result.

Retries are obligation-local. Admission requires a typed limitation code, materially different method signature or material infrastructure correction, expected new machine-checkable artifact, and remaining budget. Whitespace, paraphrase, larger token allowance, or wrapper changes are not novelty.

No-output watchdog is mandatory: checkpoint/health event by the earlier of 10 minutes or 25% of deadline; stop/checkpoint by the earlier of 20 minutes or 50% without progress. Retry requires a health probe or material configuration change.

Scheduler receipts contain ready set, selected step, capacity, queue time, and resource conflict. A required independent root waiting beyond the lesser of five minutes or 20% of phase budget while capacity exists triggers a starvation violation.

Success and failure remain orthogonal to campaign and mathematical status. A successful playbook means its SOP completed and evidence is valid; deterministic campaign closure separately decides whether obligations are solved.
Repairs are append-only. Corrupt, stale, superseded, rejected, and failed artifacts remain retained with lineage and cannot be overwritten, averaged, or silently omitted.

Human authority is required for authoritative informal-to-formal equivalence, contract amendments, security exceptions, destructive publication, and exceptional corruption/authenticity disputes. Human approval cannot waive kernel failure, deterministic refutation, missing evidence, or unauthorized capability.
Canonical content excludes presentation timestamps where reproducibility requires it; publication metadata may carry time outside the content hash. All digests state their domain.

Every run exports an expected-record manifest, receipt manifest, evidence manifest, first/last event sequence, event head, and whole-run versus partial-slice declaration. `complete=true` is forbidden unless every expected terminal record verifies.
playbooks.definition: PlaybookV2 is an executable, immutable, semantically versioned, evidence-gated mathematical standard operating procedure. It is a registered program over typed artifacts: the controller resolves inputs by digest, evaluates preconditions, compiles a deterministic step DAG, assigns role-constrained executors, records every invocation, validates every output against a named schema, computes audit independence, applies invalidation transitively, and derives a terminal result. A playbook is not prompt text: prompts, when needed, are versioned step resources whose hashes are inputs to an otherwise controller-owned protocol. Playbooks never determine campaign success directly; they emit evidence and typed decisions consumed by deterministic obligation closure. V1 readers remain quarantined, read-only migration inputs, and no playbook may emit a v1 record.
evidence_contract: Evidence classes are distinct and nonfungible: `formal_audited`, `exact_checked`, `proof_object_checked`, `interval_certified`, `deterministically_verified`, `source_derived`, `semantic_human_approved`, `independent_model_review`, `model_proposal`, `numeric_telemetry`, and `operational_receipt`. No averaging or rhetorical promotion is allowed.

Every evidence item is an `ArtifactRefV2` bound to campaign/run/playbook/step/attempt, immutable inputs, contract digest, producer identity, execution attestation, schema, digest, size, and assurance class.

Formal evidence requires clean pinned build, exact declaration signature/type hash, source and dependency roots, compiler/kernel/toolchain identity, complete untruncated output or authenticated report channel, axiom/unsafe/sorry scan, replay recipe, and terminal receipt. Compilation does not establish source fidelity or semantic equivalence.

Certificate evidence requires a generated manifest of domains, branches, exact witnesses, margins, coverage cells, joins/endpoints, checker/proof-object version, source generator digest, deterministic replay, and mutation tests. Numeric telemetry is retained separately and cannot close uncovered regions.

Claim evidence records content hash separately from campaign claim ID; exact statement, assumptions, domains, quantifiers, dependencies, target mapping, evidence refs, producer, verifier verdicts, disagreements, adjudication, limitations, and closure state.

Semantic evidence binds target ID, informal source digest, declaration identity/type digest, toolchain digest, campaign/run IDs, reviewer identity and independence, relation, typed issues/locations, and authoritative human approval when required.

Receipts separate `controller_status`, `execution_status`, `artifact_status`, `verification_status`, `semantic_status`, `scientific_status`, `gate_decision`, and `outcome_reason`. One dimension never implies another.

Evidence is complete only when the exact retained set matches the manifest under a stable locked snapshot bound to state sequence/digest and event head. Self-consistency is labeled separately from authenticity.

Invalidation is evidence-preserving: stale evidence keeps its original status and lineage but is excluded from current closure. Fresh replay can create a new descendant; it cannot mutate the old item.
A playbook result exposes limitations and unresolved obligations even when successful. `succeeded` means the SOP ran correctly, not that a theorem or campaign is solved.

default_models: Luna executes pinned build/scan/report steps.
Terra performs ordinary independent contract-to-receipt audit.
Sol disabled.
escalation: Infrastructure/receipt defects → deterministic recovery only.
Routine proof break with unchanged target → Terra maintenance playbook.
Substantive mandatory frontier gap after two valid Terra methods and independent confirmation → controller may admit Sol planning, never audit execution.
Semantic mismatch between exact theorem and informal target → human semantic review; no automatic success.
gates: Universal gates U0–U6 apply, including output schema, freshness, receipt completeness, invalidation, and independent audit.
`F0_trust_boundary`: pinned executable/toolchain and nonwritable trusted source/report channel.
`F1_clean_build`: actual target-including clean build succeeds with complete output.
`F2_signature`: exact declaration exists once and type hash matches.
`F3_axioms`: axiom set is within policy; no forbidden proof holes/unsafe path.
`F4_audit_diversity`: Terra auditor is clean-room and distinct from any proof author; formal verifier receipt is mandatory.
Success: every mandatory declaration passes F0–F4 and manifests verify. Failure: typed formal rejection, integrity failure, infrastructure block, or contract mismatch; no model escalation.
outputs: One `LeanVerificationReceiptV3` per required declaration, plus exact source/build/output refs and a `PlaybookResultV2`. Cardinality and exact target coverage are controller-checked.
preconditions: Immutable repository/source root, target declaration registry, exact expected type or type-hash policy, allowed-axiom policy, pinned Lean/Lake/Mathlib/toolchain digests, and verification root are present.
No trusted build input or report channel is candidate-writable; capability preflight passes.
Claim is not already discharged by a fresh receipt with identical dependency fingerprint.
initial_playbooks.purpose: Turn reported Lean/formal source claims into controller-authenticated, reproducible receipts before any `formal_audited` label. This is the first gate for CMV and any retained theorem claim.
steps: `controller.preflight`: verify source inventory, import reachability, exact declaration uniqueness, toolchain pins, report-channel integrity, output bounds, and absence of mutable trusted paths.
`luna.execute_known`: create/use one verification root importing every declared public target; run clean build with the pinned executable, not a project-substitutable second environment.

`formal.verify`: emit exact theorem signatures/type hashes; scan reachable source for `sorry`, `admit`, custom axioms, unsafe/native substitution, and forbidden constructs; run `#print axioms` or structured equivalent per declaration.
`luna.execute_known`: capture complete command/environment/source/dependency/output digests and replay recipe; fail on truncation or ambiguous declaration output.
`terra.audit`: independently compare frozen contract, declaration types, source reachability, allowed axioms, and receipt bindings; Terra cannot repair during audit.
`controller.derive_result`: publish audit manifest and per-declaration status without inferring source fidelity or semantic equivalence.

default_models: Luna performs deterministic import/normalization.
Terra handles ordinary cross-artifact mapping and clean-room audit.
Sol disabled.
escalation: Malformed/schema/path failures → deterministic quarantine, not model escalation.
Ambiguous ordinary reference mapping → one additional Terra method.
High-impact mathematical conflict with valid evidence that replay cannot settle → Sol adjudication only under a separate eligibility receipt.
Target/source interpretation change → human authority.
gates: Universal U0–U6 enforce receipts, schema, freshness, invalidation, diversity, and terminal derivation.
`C0_closed_inventory`: every supplied artifact is parsed or quarantined with reason.
`C1_scope_preservation`: no dropped hypothesis, domain, branch, semantics, or endpoint condition.
`C2_authority`: audit overlays and permanent corrections are applied; prose cannot supersede stronger receipts.
`C3_graph`: IDs/edges are unique, known, acyclic, and target coverage is explicit.
`C4_independent_audit`: Terra verifier covers exactly all claims and conflicts.
